February 2026

God of War Shines in February State of Play with Surprise Game and Trilogy Remake

PlayStation's February State of Play featured God of War: Sons of Sparta, a new $29.99 PS5 game out now that explores young Kratos training with his brother Deimos using pixel art and spear combat. Santa Monica Studio also revealed a full remake of the original PS2 and PS3 God of War trilogy is in early development, tying into the franchise's 20th anniversary.

Other highlights included a John Wick single-player gun-fu game with Keanu Reeves and Silent Hill: Townfall set for 2026, leaving gamers thrilled especially over the Kratos reveals.

News

WWE 2K26 Teases Karmen Petrovic's Sword Entrance on Valentine's Day

The official WWE Games account shared a nearly minute-long video of NXT star Karmen Petrovic, a third-degree black belt and Bosnian-Canadian wrestler signed since 2023, making her dramatic entrance in black leather gear with sword props amid purple and blue lights. Petrovic hyped it herself with 'who’s that girl? ' and Valentine's nods to her SHINGSHINGSQUAD fans. While many praised the smooth sword animations and her signature match gear, some critiqued the model's face likeness, body proportions, and minor glitches like sword clipping.

News

WWE 2K26 Reveals Maryse's Updated Entrance and Retro Gear

WWE Games shared a 46-second video of Maryse's refreshed model and entrance for WWE 2K26, set for March 13 release on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2. Fans praised the graphical upgrades from older games like 2011's version and the unlockable alternate attire tied to her Showcase mode rivalries with The Miz. While some criticized the face and hair as too modern for the 2009 throwback look, others celebrated the new gear and hair physics as a solid win. The reveal has fans hoping for similar updates to other legends like Bobby Lashley.
News

WWE 2K26 Gameplay Shows Stephanie Vaquer's Devil's Kiss with Booker T Commentary

WWE 2K Games shared a 13-second gameplay video from WWE 2K26, featuring NXT star Stephanie Vaquer delivering her brutal Devil's Kiss facesit pound in a packed arena, perfectly synced with Booker T's iconic commentary from her real matches. Vaquer, who joined NXT in early 2025 after success in Mexico, has made the move a fan favorite with Booker T's 'Ahh Ahh Ahh!' chants. The game launches March 13 with over 400 stars, and fans loved the authentic energy while calling for more entrances and reveals ahead of the February 27 ratings special.

XBox

XBox offers offers two current-generation consoles, the powerfulXbox Series X (both disc and digital editions) and the more affordable, all-digital Xbox Series S, along with the subscription service Xbox Game Pass.

Xbox Consoles Overview

The Xbox Series X is Microsoft's flagship console, designed for true 4K gaming and featuring a disc drive, while the Xbox Series S is a more compact, digital-only alternative targeting 1440p resolution.

News/Profile

Playstation

The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is Sony's current generation of home video game consoles, available in standard (disc) and Digital Editions, as well as a more powerful Pro model released in November 2024. The original launch models have been replaced by slimmer hardware revisions.

Key Features

Immersive Experience: Both models offer breathtaking 4K visuals (up to 120fps on compatible games) and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D Audio effects.

DualSense Controller: Features haptic feedback (realistic physical sensations) and adaptive triggers (dynamic resistance) for deeper immersion.

Ultra-High Speed SSD: A custom solid-state drive allows for lightning-fast loading times, enabling game developers to design vast worlds with near-instant data streaming.

Backward Compatibility: The PS5 is compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games, many of which benefit from faster and smoother frame rates with Game Boost technology.

PS5 Pro Enhancements: The Pro model features a faster GPU (about 45% faster), improved ray tracing, and AI-driven upscaling technology (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution or PSSR).

Upcoming Games (2026)

Sony's February 2026 State of Play event revealed an array of upcoming titles:

Resident Evil Requiem: Expected February 27, 2026.

Legacy of Kain: Defiance Remastered: Slated for March 3, 2026, for both PS4 and PS5.

Ghost of Yotei: Legends DLC: A 4-player co-op update for the existing game coming in early March.

Pragmata: Capcom's new IP is scheduled for April 24, 2026.

Beast of Reincarnation: An action RPG from Game Freak, set to launch on August 4, 2026.

Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2: Bringing remasters of MGS4, Peace Walker, and more on August 27, 2026.

Saros: A new sci-fi action game from the creators of Returnal, a PS5 exclusive coming in 2026.

WWE 2K26 is the latest installment in the professional wrestling video game series, scheduled for release on March 13, 2026, with early access available from March 6, 2026, for premium editions.

CM Punk is the official cover star for the Standard Edition.

WWE 2K26

Key Details and Platforms

The game is being developed by Visual Concepts and published by 2K. It will not be released on last-generation consoles (PS4, Xbox One), focusing exclusively on current generation hardware.

Developer: Visual Concepts

Publisher: 2K

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Windows PC (via Steam), and Nintendo Switch 2

New Features

WWE 2K26 promises a range of new features and improvements across its game modes, including the largest roster in franchise history with over 400 Superstars and Legends.

New Match Types: Additions include I Quit, Inferno, Dumpster, and Three Stages of Hell matches.

2K Showcase: Punked: A career-spanning story mode focused on CM Punk, featuring a mix of historical matches and "fantasy warfare" scenarios, narrated by Punk himself.

Roster: Features over 400 playable characters, including current Superstars and Legends such as The Rock, Triple H, John Cena, and CM Punk.

MyGM Mode: Expanded to support more match types (intergender, 5, 6, and 8-man matches) and additional brands.

Universe Mode: The WWE Draft is integrated into this sandbox mode, along with new promo types and a "Watch Show" spectator option.

Creation Suite: Increased to 200 Create-A-Superstar save slots and 2000 custom image slots, with deeper body and face morphing tools.

Commentary Team: Wade Barrett and Booker T have been added to the commentary team.

Pro Wrestling Manager/Advovate/GOAT Paul Heyman On WWE2K26

“I appreciate the question and I understand where it’s coming from, but if I were to do that, then I’m living my own fantasy within the video game and I don’t know if you are aware of this, I am maybe a couple of weeks, months, maybe even a year or two older than the typical gamer that’s out there today.

“So because of that I try not to play to my own fantasy booking, I try to play to the audience’s fantasy booking, and not just the WWE audience, but the video game audience itself. ‘Cause I would like to steal people from other video game franchises. I like to entice people to not play Fortnite, but to play WWE 2k26. I would like to entice people to not play Call of Duty, but to play WWE 2k26.

“So it’s not just a matter of, ‘Ooh, what would happen if I put Lou Thesz and Bruno Sammartino and Brock Lesnar in a triple threat match together?’ It’s more of, ‘What can appeal to today’s gamer audience? What appeals to that crowd? What can I do to tickle their fancy, to entice their imagination?’ Not just live out my own fantasies that I would have trouble booking for whatever different reason in today’s environment, including Thesz versus Sammartino versus Lesnar.” Paul Heyman

Tom Brady Jabs Logan Paul in WWE-Flag Football Feud

The playful rivalry kicked off on Brady's Impaulsive podcast appearance, where he called Paul's WWE flips 'cute' compared to the real competition of his Fanatics Flag Football Classic on March 21 in Saudi Arabia, featuring stars like Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey. Paul hit back, claiming most NFL players would flop in a WWE ring and questioning Brady's athletic credentials despite his seven Super Bowls. Fans divide along lines, with NFL loyalists eyeing wrestling's scripted side while WWE backers highlight its high-flying risks, as both worlds boast crossover athletes like Brock Lesnar.

Charlotte Flair Gifts Alexa Bliss Black Roses in Hilarious Galentine's Segment

On the February 13 SmackDown from Dallas, Flair—rocking a red corset and rose-petal tutu—apologized for Royal Rumble mix-ups and escorted Bliss to her Triple Threat qualifier against Giulia and Zelina Vega. Bliss sealed the win with her Twisted Bliss on Vega, earning a spot in the Women's Elimination Chamber on February 28 in Chicago alongside Tiffany Stratton and Rhea Ripley. The lighthearted moment had fans laughing and cheering, with Flair channeling her dad Ric Flair's 'Wooooo!' and Bliss looking genuinely amused as three more qualifiers remain. (Grok)

Fans are split, with NFL supporters backing Brady's edge and wrestling fans enjoying the troll, all building hype for the event.

Carny Island: Media and Online News Buzz

Brett Clements is an Australian artist, writer, filmmaker, and game designer best known as the creator of the cult hybrid video board game franchise Nightmare / ATMOSFEAR (which sold over 4 million units).

Carny Island Overview

• Concept: Carny Island is a hybrid video board game and digital experience that mixes physical tabletop play with mobile phones used as interactive entertainment portals.
• Gameplay: Players scavenge graves for body parts and loot to build their own Frankenstein-style creation while trying to survive characters like Uncle Shrift. • Production Team: Developed alongside the team at Mongril Labs, with AI tools supporting coding, testing, and production, and a reunion with former Roadshow Entertainment president Milt Barlow for global licensing.
• Engine/Media: Built using development transitions into Godot, documented via regular dev logs and updates on the Carny Island Official Website and Carny Island YouTube Channel.

Background & Career • Media & Television: A multi-decade veteran across Australian television, network advertising, and journalism, having worked on projects like Simon Townsend's Wonder World! and A Couple 'A Cowboys.
• Other Projects: Involved in producing and directing various digital, real-estate, and documentary ventures, including the guerrilla-shot docu-series SQUAD.
• Online Profiles: You can follow his ongoing production logs via Brett Clements' Portfolio or his LinkedIn Newsletter

*Media Man Group is officially representing (b2b and Media/Online Media/Business Development) Carny Island

God of War Shines in February State of Play with Surprise Game and Trilogy Remake

PlayStation's February State of Play featured God of War: Sons of Sparta, a new $29.99 PS5 game out now that explores young Kratos training with his brother Deimos using pixel art and spear combat. Santa Monica Studio also revealed a full remake of the original PS2 and PS3 God of War trilogy is in early development, tying into the franchise's 20th anniversary.

Other highlights included a John Wick single-player gun-fu game with Keanu Reeves and Silent Hill: Townfall set for 2026, leaving gamers thrilled especially over the Kratos reveals.

The official WWE Games account shared a nearly minute-long video of NXT star Karmen Petrovic, a third-degree black belt and Bosnian-Canadian wrestler signed since 2023, making her dramatic entrance in black leather gear with sword props amid purple and blue lights. Petrovic hyped it herself with 'who’s that girl? ' and Valentine's nods to her SHINGSHINGSQUAD fans. WWE Games shared a 46-second video of Maryse's refreshed model and entrance for WWE 2K26, set for March 13 release on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2. Fans praised the graphical upgrades from older games like 2011's version and the unlockable alternate attire tied to her Showcase mode rivalries with The Miz. XBox

XBox offers offers two current-generation consoles, the powerfulXbox Series X (both disc and digital editions) and the more affordable, all-digital Xbox Series S, along with the subscription service Xbox Game Pass.

Xbox Consoles Overview

The Xbox Series X is Microsoft's flagship console, designed for true 4K gaming and featuring a disc drive, while the Xbox Series S is a more compact, digital-only alternative targeting 1440p resolution.

News/Profile

Playstation

The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is Sony's current generation of home video game consoles, available in standard (disc) and Digital Editions, as well as a more powerful Pro model released in November 2024. The original launch models have been replaced by slimmer hardware revisions.

Key Features

Immersive Experience: Both models offer breathtaking 4K visuals (up to 120fps on compatible games) and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D Audio effects.

DualSense Controller: Features haptic feedback (realistic physical sensations) and adaptive triggers (dynamic resistance) for deeper immersion.

Ultra-High Speed SSD: A custom solid-state drive allows for lightning-fast loading times, enabling game developers to design vast worlds with near-instant data streaming.

Backward Compatibility: The PS5 is compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games, many of which benefit from faster and smoother frame rates with Game Boost technology.

PS5 Pro Enhancements: The Pro model features a faster GPU (about 45% faster), improved ray tracing, and AI-driven upscaling technology (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution or PSSR).

“I appreciate the question and I understand where it’s coming from, but if I were to do that, then I’m living my own fantasy within the video game and I don’t know if you are aware of this, I am maybe a couple of weeks, months, maybe even a year or two older than the typical gamer that’s out there today.

“So because of that I try not to play to my own fantasy booking, I try to play to the audience’s fantasy booking, and not just the WWE audience, but the video game audience itself. ‘Cause I would like to steal people from other video game franchises. “So it’s not just a matter of, ‘Ooh, what would happen if I put Lou Thesz and Bruno Sammartino and Brock Lesnar in a triple threat match together?’ It’s more of, ‘What can appeal to today’s gamer audience? text:
President Trump met Monday at the White House with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani — the chief mediator between Washington and Tehran in the war with Iran that began on February 28 and is now in its ninth month — and he came out of the meeting with a message of pressure, not peace talks: the blockade holds, the Gulf states stand behind it, and Iran will not be allowed a nuclear weapon.

In a Truth Social post after the meeting, Trump said he had "an excellent conversation" with the Qatari leader about Iran. Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait "and others, would prefer the status quo," he wrote — "in other words, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History, and the new Operation Iron Gate — Therefore, Land and Sea." Then the line the whole region heard: "All have agreed that Iran cannot have a Nuclear Weapon — That is non-negotiable!"

Trump warned that should anything change in the Middle East, the United States is "'locked and loaded' and ready to go" — though, he added, "at this point, however, that seems to be quite unlikely." He said "Israel, and the entire Middle East, are protected from Iranian danger and threats," and pointed to "positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict." Vice President Vance also met with the Qatari prime minister during the visit.

Later that afternoon, at the White House briefing podium, Trump said it again in person. "Iran cannot have, and everybody's agreed, Iran will never have a nuclear weapon," he told reporters — a point he called non-negotiable, and one he said Iran understands. He described the status quo as "the greatest military blockade ever" together with "the new iron gate" operating by land and by sea, and promised, "we will take care of business." He said he hopes to make a deal with Iran, but warned that "nothing's going to happen" imminently; pressed on when the war ends, he answered that it will be "ending fairly soon." The United States, he said, is "fully locked and loaded with the best equipment," with another aircraft carrier "all loaded up to the gills." Two further claims were his own: that there have been no American losses or injuries in six months, and that more oil has moved through the Strait of Hormuz recently than ever before under the blockade.

Operation Iron Gate is the newest layer of that pressure. U.S. Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday — about twenty civilian and military staff based in Tampa, Florida, created at the direction of Admiral Brad Cooper — extending the blockade beyond the sea to Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Its targets: advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials, and the illegal revenue streams that fund Tehran's war machine. CENTCOM says the task force will "monitor, detect, and disrupt" those flows.

The naval blockade, in place since July, covers Iran's ports. CENTCOM says it has blocked more than $25 billion in Iranian crude exports, redirected 147 commercial vessels, and disabled five that refused to comply. A third aircraft carrier, USS Theodore Roosevelt, is expected in the region this week.

The pressure is not theoretical. Over the weekend, Iran said tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and American forces disabled a commercial vessel — the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda — in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after it tried to run the blockade.

Diplomacy is moving on a separate track, but no deal is near. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington ends the blockade and lifts some sanctions; Secretary of State Rubio on Sunday called those demands "outrageous and ridiculous" and said he saw no imminent agreement. Qatar has presented a bridge proposal — a short trust-building framework under which the U.S. would lift the blockade and release some $8 billion in frozen Iranian assets — and Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says Tehran has submitted a seven-day roadmap and is waiting for Washington's answer.

THE GOOD NEWS: Scripture tells us who finally ends wars. "He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; He breaks the bow and shatters the spear; He burns the chariots with fire" (Psalm 46:9). What does Scripture SAY? That peace is God's work before it is ever man's — presidents and mediators do not make wars cease; He does. What is God DOING? He governs kings and go-betweens alike, and the pressure now bearing down on a regime racing toward a nuclear weapon is the magistrate's sword doing its God-given work of restraining evil; if this long war truly bends toward an end, that will be His mercy, not man's genius. How does He REGARD it? He hates the shedding of innocent blood, and He delights in a peace that protects the vulnerable — Israel and the whole region rest under His watch, not Washington's. So the church prays for an honest peace, gives thanks when evil is restrained, and puts no final trust in princes. Our hope is not in blockades or summits. It is in the God who breaks the bow.

text:
GOOGLE ONCE PROMISED THAT NO HUMAN WOULD SEE YOUR GMAIL THROUGH ITS AI.
THAT PROMISE NOW COMES WITH A FOOTNOTE.

In September 2023, Google made a simple privacy promise about its AI assistant.
It fit in one sentence.
If you connected Gmail, Docs and Drive to the assistant, your content "is not seen by human reviewers."

That sentence is still online today.

But on October 16, 2026, Google added a note in brackets right after it.

The note says that with newer features, data from those apps "can be used to train generative AI models."
And it says that data "can also be subject to human review in limited circumstances."
On November 9, 2026, a post titled "Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators" reached the front page of Hacker News.

When I checked it, it had about 450 points and more than 100 comments.
Many people in that thread said they had no idea.

One commenter wrote that the post made them check their own Google accounts, and that the setting was switched on.

I think this is the most important AI story of the week for ordinary people.

Not because a new model came out.
Because it is about the most private place most of us have online.
Our inbox.

This is a long post, because the details matter here more than the headline.

I read Google's own help pages, its privacy notice and its blog posts, and I quote them directly so you can check every line yourself.
Where something is only claimed by one person online, I will say so.

WHAT GOOGLE PROMISED IN 2023

On September 19, 2023, Google announced Bard Extensions.
Bard was the old name of Gemini.
Extensions let the assistant look inside your Gmail, Docs and Drive to answer questions.
Google's example was planning a trip and asking the assistant to pull dates from your email.
Another example was asking it to find your resume in Drive and turn it into a personal statement.
The privacy line in that post was very clear.
"If you choose to use the Workspace extensions, your content from Gmail, Docs and Drive is not seen by human reviewers, used by Bard to show you ads or used to train the Bard model."
Three promises in one sentence.
No human reviewers.
No ads.
No training.
Google repeated the same promise in a second blog post about its responsible approach to generative AI.

WIRED quoted that exact line in its 2023 guide to using Bard with Gmail and Docs.
For a lot of people, that sentence was the reason they felt safe trying it.

WHAT THE FOOTNOTE SAYS NOW

Here is the note Google added to both of those blog posts, dated October 16, 2026.
"As we've continued to make Google products more personalized and helpful, we've added features that enable users to choose to connect Workspace apps to other Google services."
"If users choose to enable these new features, data from Workspace Apps will be processed to personalize other Google experiences, and depending on a user's settings, that same subset of data can be used to train generative AI models."
"It can also be subject to human review in limited circumstances."
So the old sentence was not deleted.
It was kept, and a footnote was placed next to it.
The footnote reverses two of the three original promises for people who turn on the newer features.
Training is now possible.
Human review is now possible.
The ads promise is the one part still standing, and I will come back to it.
To be fair to Google, the note does not say the old feature changed overnight.
It says new features work differently.
But for the person who read the 2023 sentence and connected their Gmail, that difference is very easy to miss.

WHAT GOOGLE'S HELP PAGE ACTUALLY SAYS

The real detail is on a Gemini help page called "About personalization with Connected Apps."
This is the page for a feature Google calls Personal Intelligence.
It lets Gemini draw on your own data across Google apps.
The list of apps you can connect is long.
Google Workspace, which the page says includes Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Keep, Tasks, Chat and Meet.
Search services, Maps, Shopping, Flights and Hotels.
Contacts.
Google Wallet and payments.
Google Photos, if eligible.
The page then lists what data is shared.
Emails, files, events, photos, videos, contact info "such as phone numbers, addresses, and birthdays", payment methods, and financial account info linked through services such as Plaid.
It also says the data "may relate to topics you find sensitive, like race, religion, and health, or confidential info."
And it adds a line many people will skim past.
"If new data is added to these apps in the future, Gemini will have access to that data."
So connecting is not a one-time share.
It is an open door to everything that arrives later.
Now the part about human review, in Google's own words.
"When connected to Gemini, a subset of Connected Apps data processed by Gemini is reviewed by human reviewers (including trained service providers) to debug our services, help keep them safe, and improve them."
"Trained service providers" is Google's phrase for outside reviewers working for companies it hires.
The page says reviewers "assess if Gemini responses were low-quality, inaccurate, or harmful" and "suggest better responses."
Then comes the line that I think every Gemini user should read twice.
"Please don't connect your apps to Gemini Apps if they contain confidential information that you wouldn't want a reviewer to see."
Think about what that sentence means for a normal person.
Whose Gmail does not contain confidential information?

Bank alerts.
Medical appointment emails.
Password reset links.
Salary slips.
Arguments with family.
Lawyer letters.
Tax documents in Drive.
The warning is honest.
It is also a warning that almost nobody can follow while still using the feature as advertised.

THE "SUMMARY" THAT CAN BE THE WHOLE EMAIL

Google says it does not train its AI directly on your inbox.
Here is the exact wording.
"Gemini does not train generative AI models directly on your Gmail inbox, Drive, Contacts, Calendar or other Workspace apps, on your Google Wallet and payments services, or on imagery or audio from your Google Photos library."
That sounds reassuring.
But the next sentences explain what it does train on.
"When you interact with Gemini, summaries, excerpts, generated media, and inferences from your relevant media, emails, files, and transactions may be used to help us answer your prompts."
"We train our generative AI models off of these summaries, excerpts, generated media, and inferences."
And then this.
"In some cases, for example, where the email or file is brief or particularly relevant to respond to the prompt, the summary may just be the email or file."
Read that slowly.
Google is not training on your whole inbox.
It is training on the pieces of your inbox that Gemini pulled into a conversation.
And sometimes that piece is the entire email.
Most important emails are short.
A one-line message from your doctor.
A two-line OTP or delivery notice.
A short note from your boss.
Those are exactly the emails that are "brief or particularly relevant."
The help page even gives an example of how this works.
If you ask Gemini to plan restaurants for an upcoming trip, it "might review your emails to get information about your upcoming hotel reservation and flight itinerary, as well as restaurants you've visited on prior trips."

WHAT GOOGLE SAYS IT DOES TO PROTECT YOU

Here is Google's side, also in its own words, because a fair post has to include it.
"Before trained service providers review interactions personalized using Connected Apps, we take steps to protect your privacy, such as disconnecting interactions from your Google Account and reducing personal information in this data, unless it's to address abuse or harm."
For training, the page says Google takes "steps to reduce personal information" or applies "privacy preserving techniques like differential privacy."
Differential privacy is a known statistical method for adding noise so individuals are harder to pick out of a dataset.
Google's Privacy Hub also says, "We take your privacy seriously, and we do not sell your personal information to anyone."
And it says, "Your Gemini Apps chats are not being used to show you ads. If this changes, we will clearly communicate it to you."
So the 2023 ads promise survives, at least for Gemini chats, with a clear "if this changes" attached.
Those protections are real steps.

But notice what they are.
Disconnecting a chat from your account name does not remove your name from the email itself.
"Reducing" personal information is not the same as removing it.
And the abuse-or-harm exception means those protections switch off in some cases.

THE FEEDBACK BUTTON IS A BIGGER DOOR THAN IT LOOKS

There is one more line on the Connected Apps page that I think is the sharpest of all.
"If you submitted feedback, or we need to address abuse or harm, human reviewers may also review some of your Gmail inbox or Photos library media."
Not just the chat.
Some of your Gmail inbox.

The Privacy Hub explains what feedback includes.
When you send feedback, Google collects "your feedback," "context that can help us better understand your feedback, including the last 24 hours of your chats," and "any content included in those chats (like uploads and data from Connected Apps)."
And this applies even when your Keep Activity setting is off.
So a thumbs-down on one bad answer can send a full day of your chats, plus the email content inside them, to a review team.
The Privacy Hub says reviewed feedback is "retained for up to 3 years."
To be fair, OpenAI has a similar rule.
Its data controls page says that if you give a thumbs up or thumbs down, "the entire conversation associated with that feedback may be used to train OpenAI models," even if you opted out.
The difference is what is inside the conversation.

A chat about a recipe is one thing.
A chat where the assistant quietly pulled in your bank email is another.

DELETING DOES NOT UNDO A REVIEW

Here is the retention part, which surprised me most.
The Privacy Hub says: "Chats reviewed by human reviewers (and related data like your language, device type, location info, or feedback) are not deleted when you delete your activity. Instead, they are retained for up to three years."
The reason Google gives is that reviewed chats are disconnected from your account, so they are no longer "yours" to delete in the normal way.
The Connected Apps page adds: "You can delete your Gemini Apps activity to prevent it from being used for future product improvement, unless it has already been reviewed by trained reviewers."

It also says: "Disconnecting an app or deleting data in a connected app doesn't delete any data from Gemini Apps Activity."
So three things are true at once.
If you delete an email from Gmail, copies already pulled into Gemini chats are not deleted by that.
If you disconnect Gmail from Gemini, your old Gemini activity stays.
If a chat was already picked for human review, deleting your activity does not pull it back.

The default auto-delete for Gemini activity, according to the same page, is 18 months.
You can change it to 3 months, 36 months, or never.

WHO IS AFFECTED, AND WHO IS NOT

This is the part where I want to be careful, because the headline can make it sound bigger than it is.
This applies to consumer Gemini, meaning personal Google accounts using the Gemini app or https://t.co/vpeCsB8XYH.
It applies when you have connected apps like Gmail or Drive through Personal Intelligence.
Google's Privacy Hub says some connected apps, like Google Workspace, become unavailable when Keep Activity is off.
So the human review path for your email runs mainly through people who have Keep Activity on and Workspace connected, plus anyone who sends feedback.
Work and school accounts follow different terms.
Google's Privacy Hub says: "If you have a work or school Google Account, your use of Gemini Apps may be subject to different data handling terms."
Google's Workspace help page for Gemini inside Gmail, Docs and Drive says that feature "doesn't use your content to train or improve Gemini or other generative AI models."

So there are really two different Geminis here.
Gemini inside Gmail, the side panel that helps you write and summarize, which Google says does not train on your content.
And the Gemini app, which can reach into your Gmail through Connected Apps, where the rules above apply.

That is the heart of the confusion.
One Hacker News commenter put it bluntly, saying there is "way too much nuance to what's going on."
I agree.

When a privacy rule needs a diagram to understand, most people will not get it right.
There is also a regional difference.
A French tech site, MACCUS, reported that Personal Intelligence is not offered in the European Economic Area, Switzerland or the UK.
I could not confirm that on Google's own page during this research, so treat it as reported, not confirmed.
If you are in India, the US or most other places, assume these rules can apply to you and check your own settings.

WHAT THE VIRAL POST CLAIMS, AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY VERIFIED

The Hacker News post linked to a GitHub repository by an anonymous account.
The author claims Gemini pulled Gmail and Drive content into chats without being asked, even without typing a tag like @Gmail or @Drive.
https://t.co/H2whNn87yX, which wrote about the repository on November 10, says the author described four outcomes from similar prompts.
Nothing retrieved.
A short count or summary.
Partial quotes of two to four sentences, sometimes with personal or account details.
Or the full document or email pulled into the chat.
Those tests are one person's tests.
Digiton, a site that covered the story on November 9, said it could not reproduce them.
I did not test this myself either, and I am not going to present it as fact.
So here is the clean line between claim and fact.
Claimed by one anonymous tester: Gemini sometimes pulls in whole files you never mentioned.
Confirmed by Google's own help page: connected data can be reviewed by humans, including outside service providers, and what is reviewed "may just be the email or file."
Confirmed by Google's own blog note: the 2023 promise of no human review now has an exception.
You do not need the anonymous tests to have a privacy question.
Google's own pages are enough.
WHY AI COMPANIES WANT HUMANS TO READ CHATS
It is worth understanding why this happens at all, because it is not pure villainy.
AI models make mistakes.
Someone has to look at real answers and decide which ones were wrong, unsafe or useless.
Google's page says reviewers "assess if Gemini responses were low-quality, inaccurate, or harmful" and "suggest better responses."
That human judgement is one of the main ways chatbots get better.
Reviewers also look for abuse, like scams and attempts to misuse the tool.
So human review is standard across the industry.
Google's Privacy Hub says, even for ordinary Gemini chats, "A subset of chats are reviewed by human reviewers."
The question is not whether humans read some AI chats.
They do, at most big AI companies, under various settings.
The question is what flows into those chats.
When the chat only holds what you typed, you control what goes in.
When the chat can reach into your email by itself, you no longer fully control what goes in.
That is the real shift.
GOOGLE IS NOT THE ONLY ONE
A balanced view needs the other companies too.
OpenAI's data controls page says that on personal ChatGPT Free, Plus and Pro accounts, "data sharing is enabled by default."
You can switch off a setting called "Improve the model for everyone."
OpenAI says its business, enterprise and education workspaces are not used for training by default.
Anthropic changed its consumer terms on August 28, 2025.
Claude Free, Pro and Max users were asked to choose whether their chats can be used to train future models.
If you allow it, Anthropic says it keeps that data for five years.
If you do not, it keeps the existing 30-day period.
Anthropic also says it does not sell user data to third parties.
So every major lab now treats consumer chats as possible training material, with some way to opt out.
What makes the Gemini story stand out is the reach.
ChatGPT and Claude can also connect to email and files in various ways today.
But Google owns the email, the drive, the photos, the calendar, the maps and the phone software all at once.
No other AI company starts with that much of your life already sitting on its own servers.
When Google connects its AI to its own apps, it is not asking to visit your house.
It already holds the keys.
YOUR INBOX IS FULL OF OTHER PEOPLE
This is the part that I think gets missed in most discussions.
When you connect your Gmail, you are not only sharing your own data.
You are sharing the emails other people sent to you.
Your doctor did not agree to have their message read by an AI training pipeline.
Your friend who sent a personal photo did not click any button.
The client who mailed you a contract did not opt in.
Your child's school did not consent when it emailed a report card.
Google's own Privacy Hub acknowledges this, in a section about European law.
It says that to respond to you, "we process personal data about others that you've given Gemini Apps (such as when you ask Gemini Apps to retrieve information from Google Workspace or Google Photos)."
Photos work the same way.
The Connected Apps page says Photos data "is used to infer your interests, relationships to people in your photos, and where you've been, including by associating your face with corresponding location data and timestamps."
That is not only your face.
It is everyone in your camera roll.
Privacy has always been a group project.
AI assistants make that more obvious, because one person's yes can expose many people who never got asked.
WHY "DE-IDENTIFIED" IS NOT THE SAME AS "SAFE"
Google says reviewed data is disconnected from your account and personal information is reduced.
I believe that is a real process.
But here is a simple analogy, and it is only an analogy.
Removing the name from an envelope does not help much if the letter inside starts with your first name and ends with your phone number and address.
Emails are full of names, signatures, addresses, account numbers and order numbers.
Automatic tools can strip a lot of that.
Whether they catch everything in every message is something Google has not shown publicly in detail.
That is why Google's own warning matters so much.
If Google were fully confident that reviewers could never see confidential details, it would not need to tell people not to connect apps that contain them.
THE BIGGER PATTERN: PERSONAL AI RUNS ON PERSONAL DATA
Step back and the direction of the whole industry becomes clear.
The race this year is no longer only about which chatbot is smartest.
It is about which assistant knows you best.
Google calls its version Personal Intelligence.
Anthropic recently launched a personal finance feature that connects Claude to bank and card accounts through Plaid.
Apple's new CEO is reportedly pushing to make Siri act more like an agent, according to Bloomberg.
Every one of these products gets better when it can read more of your life.
And every company needs real examples to improve them.
That creates a quiet pressure.
The most useful assistant will be the one with the most access.
The most access means the most private data passing through systems that humans sometimes check.
I do not think the answer is to refuse all of it.
These tools can save real time.
Finding a booking in a messy inbox in five seconds is genuinely useful.
But the trade should be clear before you make it, not explained in a footnote three years later.
WHAT YOU CAN DO TODAY
Here are practical steps, based on what Google's own pages say.
Settings menus change often, so if a label looks different on your phone, search the Gemini help center for the same words.
Step one: check whether you connected anything.
Open Gemini, go to Settings, and look for Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps.
See whether Google Workspace, Photos, Wallet or Contacts are switched on.
Many people clicked yes on a pop-up months ago and forgot.
Step two: disconnect what you do not use.
If you never ask Gemini about your email, there is no reason to keep Gmail connected.
Remember that disconnecting stops future access, but does not delete past Gemini activity.
Step three: decide on Keep Activity.
Google says turning off Keep Activity stops your future chats from being used to improve its AI, unless you send feedback.
The trade-off is that Workspace connected apps become unavailable while it is off.
Chats are still kept for 72 hours so Gemini can respond and for safety, according to the Privacy Hub.
Step four: think before you press thumbs up or thumbs down.
On a chat that touched your email, files or photos, feedback can send that content, plus the last 24 hours of chats, to a review team.
If a sensitive answer was bad, it is safer to just start a new chat.
Step five: use temporary chats for sensitive questions.
Google says temporary chats "are not used to train Google's AI models" and are not used to improve its AI with human reviewers.
Step six: change your auto-delete period.
The default is 18 months.
You can set it to 3 months.
Just remember that anything already reviewed stays for up to three years regardless.
Step seven: keep work and personal separate.
If your company gives you a work Google account, use that for work questions, since Google says different terms apply to work and school accounts.
Step eight: apply the same check to every AI app.
In ChatGPT, look at Data controls and "Improve the model for everyone."
In Claude, look at Privacy Settings and the model training choice.
If you connect any assistant to email, banking or files, assume a human might one day see part of it.
Then decide what is worth it.
WHAT I THINK GOOGLE SHOULD DO
If Google wants people to trust a personal AI, here is what I think it owes them.
Put the human review warning on the connect screen itself, in one plain sentence, not on a help page.
Show a small notice in the chat whenever Gemini pulls in an email or file the user did not name.
Let people connect Gmail for answers while switching off human review and training for that data, as a separate choice.
Tell people when a chat of theirs is selected for review.
Publish how many reviewers are outside contractors, and what checks they pass.
And when a promise changes, email the people who relied on the old promise.
A footnote on a three-year-old blog post is not notice.
It is a record.
WHAT I WILL WATCH NEXT
Does Google respond publicly to the Hacker News thread and the GitHub claims?
Does anyone independently confirm or disprove that Gemini pulls in files the user never mentioned?
Do privacy regulators ask questions, especially where Personal Intelligence is offered?
Does Google split "help me with my email" from "use my email to improve your AI" into two different switches?
If Google makes the switches clearer, I will say so plainly.
WHAT THIS IS REALLY ABOUT
This story is not really about one help page.
It is about what a privacy promise is worth when the product changes underneath it.
In 2023 the promise was one sentence and easy to understand.
In 2026 the exception is a paragraph, plus several help pages, plus a feedback rule, plus a three-year retention rule.
The product got more powerful.
The promise got more complicated.
And complicated promises protect companies better than they protect people.
An AI that knows your life can be the best assistant you have ever had.
It can also be the biggest window into your life that anyone has ever built.
The difference is not the model.
It is who gets to look through the window, and whether you were told.
Convenience is a feature.
Consent is a promise.
And a promise that changes in a footnote was never really a promise at all.
So tell me:
Did you know human reviewers could see parts of connected Gmail or Drive data?
Have you checked your Gemini connected apps today?
Would you trade some privacy for an assistant that can search your whole inbox?
Where is your line?

text:
YOUR EXCUSES MAY BE VALID, BUT OPPORTUNITIES WON'T ALWAYS WAIT FOR YOU.

Some people say they want to make money, grow their careers, and take advantage of opportunities, but when those opportunities finally come, they are not ready to take action.

Let me share a recent experience.

I shared a job opportunity with some active students in my Google Ads Masterclass (GAM) community.

The company was offering good pay and attractive incentives. They were looking to hire just one person, and I wanted to give my students the opportunity first.

Guess what happened?

I received responses like:

- "The pay is good, but I don't think I'm qualified enough for the role."

- "The offer is good, but can they pay me before I start?"

- "I would love to take the job, but there's no electricity in my area."

- "I need to change my phone before I can start. Please ask them to give me until the end of the month."

I understood that everyone had their personal challenges, but the company had a business need that required an immediate solution.

So, I moved on and hired someone who was ready to get started immediately.

Two weeks later, guess what?

Some of the same people who had given me different reasons for not taking the opportunity started reaching out to say they were now ready.

Unfortunately, the opportunity had already been filled.

And honestly, this experience taught me something important.

Being qualified is one thing. Being ready to take action when an opportunity comes is another.

I'm not saying your challenges are not real. I understand that life happens. You may need better equipment, stable electricity, more confidence, or even additional preparation.

But you must understand something about the tech industry and business world generally.

Things move fast.

Companies have problems they need to solve. Business owners have targets to meet. Clients need results. And when someone needs a solution, they may not have the luxury of waiting one month for you to get ready.

Sometimes, the opportunity you keep postponing is the same opportunity someone else is praying for.

I initially didn't want to share that job opening publicly because the company needed just one person. But moving forward, whenever similar opportunities come up, I'll share them with the GAM community and across my social media platforms.

My priority will be to connect opportunities with people who are qualified, interested, and ready to take action.

Here is my message to you:

Don't spend so much time waiting for perfect conditions that you miss the opportunities that could change your life.

Prepare yourself. Build your skills. Work with what you have. Improve as you go.

And when an opportunity comes, don't let unnecessary delays make someone else take the seat you were qualified to occupy.

P.S.: Your excuses are valid, but will you let them stop you?

🚨 THE AI HARDWARE COLD WAR: Why China risked a nation-state espionage operation for Nvidia Blackwell silicon, and why the $177 dip is the most misunderstood valuation dislocation in modern market history.

A forensic breakdown of the Megaspeed probe, TSMC packaging chokepoints, the CUDA monopoly, and the $200B hyperscaler CapEx wall 🧵👇

---

### PROLOGUE: THE MIDNIGHT EMAIL THAT SHOOK SILICON VALLEY

On an ordinary trading week, the semiconductor industry was rocked by a revelation that read more like a Tom Clancy espionage manuscript than a corporate governance disclosure. 

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (alias Huang Lei), a key Chinese investor operating out of Singapore-based data center operator Megaspeed. Almost concurrently, United States national security agencies initiated an aggressive probe into whether Megaspeed acted as a sovereign proxy hub—funneling illicit, embargoed Nvidia AI clusters across Southeast Asian transshipment corridors straight into Beijing’s state-backed AI labs.

Wall Street reacted with predictable, short-sighted panic. The stock plunged toward the $177 handle. Retail investors panicked about board governance, supply-chain sanctions, and potential export control retributions. Pundits proclaimed the "end of Nvidia’s sovereign monopoly."

They missed the entire geopolitical signal.

Ask yourself the foundational question: 
Why would foreign operatives and nation-state shell corporations risk secondary financial sanctions, federal asset freezes, and an international intelligence crisis just to secure physical Nvidia silicon?

The answer has nothing to do with corporate romance, and everything to do with the brutal, unyielding physics of advanced semiconductor manufacturing. 

China isn't smuggling Nvidia chips because they want faster servers. They are smuggling them because Beijing’s domestic fabs have slammed into an insurmountable 5-year physics barrier—and sovereign state survival in 2026 depends entirely on compute density.

Here is the unredacted truth about what is happening behind the scenes in the AI Hardware Cold War.

---

### PART 1: INSIDE THE MEGASPEED NETWORK & THE PROXY COMPUTE CORRIDORS

To understand the Megaspeed probe, you must first understand how modern technological embargoes are actually fought.

When the US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) tightened total processing performance (TPP) and performance density thresholds below 4,800 points, they effectively banned direct shipments of A100, H100, B100, and B200 accelerators to Chinese entities. Even modified compliance chips like the H20 and H800 faced impending regulatory constriction.

Beijing's hyperscalers—Baidu, ByteDance, Tencent, and Alibaba—faced a compute starvation event.

Enter the transshipment network:
1. Shell entities incorporate across neutral commercial hubs: Singapore, Dubai, and Malaysia.
2. These entities place legal procurement orders for enterprise-scale Blackwell and Hopper clusters, citing local cloud hosting and regional data center expansion.
3. Megaspeed emerged at the nexus of this architecture: a high-tier Singapore data center infrastructure provider with deep ties to mainland institutional capital.
4. Once high-density HGX systems arrive in Southeast Asia, compute is either:
   - "Leased" remotely via obfuscated API proxy layers, bypassing IP filters via enterprise VPN tunnels; OR
   - Physically decapped, recrated as generic networking equipment, and smuggled via commercial maritime routes through intermediary ports into Shenzhen and Shanghai.

The personal controversy surrounding Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was seized upon by Western counter-intelligence because Megaspeed was operating at the precise chokepoint where Nvidia enterprise hardware meets sovereign state evasion.

Nvidia’s board audit was swift, ruthless, and conclusive: zero national security IP was compromised, no proprietary CUDA architectural RTL source code was leaked, and Jensen Huang’s executive leadership remained completely intact.

Yet the controversy shed daylight on a stark geopolitical reality: Nvidia compute has become the 21st-century equivalent of enriched uranium.

---

### PART 2: THE PHYSICAL SILICON CHOKEPOINT (TSMC CoWoS vs. SMIC DUV)

Why can't China simply fabricate its own equivalents? Why hasn't Huawei’s Ascend 910B or 910C solved the problem?

Pundits who don't understand lithography often make the naive claim: "China built a 7nm phone with SMIC, so they will build datacenter AI chips next."

This shows a fundamental ignorance of semiconductor physics.

#### 1. The Reticle Limit & Advanced Packaging (CoWoS-L)
A datacenter accelerator like the Nvidia Blackwell B200 is not a single monolith chip. It is a massive dual-die architecture packing 208 billion transistors manufactured on TSMC's custom 4NP process. 
- These two reticle-sized dies are stitched together across a 10 TB/sec high-speed interconnect known as the NV-High-Bandwidth Interface (NV-HBI).
- Blackwell requires TSMC’s Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate with Local Silicon Interconnect (CoWoS-L)—an ultra-advanced 2.5D packaging methodology utilizing passive silicon bridges embedded within an organic substrate.
- It sits surrounded by 192GB of lightning-fast HBM3e memory delivering 8 TB/sec of memory bandwidth.

#### 2. The SMIC Multipatterning Yield Nightmare
China’s premier foundry, SMIC, lacks Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines due to Dutch export restrictions on ASML’s Twinscan EXE systems. 
- To achieve 7nm or theoretical 5nm geometries, SMIC must resort to Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) immersion lithography with Self-Aligned Quadruple Patterning (SAQP).
- Quadruple patterning requires four distinct exposure, etching, and deposition steps for a single layer. With every additional exposure pass, defect density multiplies exponentially.
- While SMIC can accept a 15% to 25% yield for a tiny 100mm² smartphone processor (Huawei Kirin 9000s) because the state subsidizes the scrap, building an 800mm² datacenter AI processor on SAQP results in catastrophic yields: below 5% to 8%.

#### 3. Benchmark Reality Check: B200 vs Huawei Ascend 910B
Let's look at hard architectural benchmarks:
- FP4 Dense Tensor Compute: Nvidia B200 hits ~9,000 TFLOPS vs Huawei Ascend 910B's zero native FP4 support.
- FP16/BF16 Compute: B200 delivers 2,250 TFLOPS vs Ascend 910B's ~320 TFLOPS (a 7x raw compute deficit).
- Memory Bandwidth: Blackwell hits 8,000 GB/sec (8 TB/s) vs Ascend 910B’s 1,200 GB/sec.
- Thermal Design Power (TDP): Blackwell pulls 1,000W to 1,200W for an entire dual-die node, whereas equivalent Huawei clusters consume nearly 3.2x the power per effective token generated.

To match a single 32,000-GPU Blackwell cluster, Huawei would need roughly 140,000 to 180,000 Ascend units. The power substations required to energize such a cluster do not exist, and the mean-time-between-failure (MTBF) of interconnect cables makes training runs of that scale mathematically impossible due to constant hardware crashes.

This physical packaging wall is why state actors risk espionage. They cannot fabricate the silicon at home.

---

### PART 3: THE SOFTWARE MOAT NOBODY CAN REPLICATE (CUDA, NCCL, & cuDNN)

Silicon is only 30% of Nvidia's moat. The remaining 70% is invisible software engineering that has been compounding uninterrupted since 2006.

Hyperscalers and venture funds frequently fund "Nvidia killers"—custom ASICs, NPUs, AMD Instinct MI300X accelerators. Yet when Fortune 500 engineering teams sit down to train or serve models at frontier scale, they crawl back to Nvidia within quarters.

Why?

#### 1. The Kernel Optimization Trap
Over twenty years, millions of academic researchers, PhD students, and AI labs wrote hundreds of millions of lines of code specifically against Nvidia’s CUDA API. Every fundamental mathematical primitive—cuBLAS, cuDNN, TensorRT, Cutlass—is hand-tuned down to the register allocations of Nvidia streaming multiprocessors (SMs).
- When you run a model on AMD’s ROCm or Huawei’s CANN, developers routinely encounter silent mathematical precision drifts, unsupported PyTorch operator bugs, and memory leaks.
- Debugging custom Triton kernels or ROCm compiler crashes can stall an entire engineering organization for months. Time-to-market is existential; spending $15M more on Nvidia GPUs is cheaper than delaying a model release by 6 months.

#### 2. The Distributed Interconnect Moat (NCCL)
AI at scale is no longer a single-GPU problem; it is a distributed systems communication problem. 
Training a 1.8-trillion-parameter MoE model requires tens of thousands of GPUs exchanging petabytes of activation gradients simultaneously.
- Nvidia built NCCL (Nvidia Collective Communications Library). NCCL tightly couples with NVLink switches (1.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth per GPU) and Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking.
- When an AllReduce or AlltoAll collective communication primitive is executed across an Nvidia cluster, hardware-level offloading handles the synchronization with zero CPU bottleneck.
- On competitive hardware relying on standard Ethernet or immature collective libraries, up to 40% to 55% of total compute time is spent idle, waiting for inter-node packet retransmission (tail latency).

You cannot replace CUDA simply by releasing an open-source translation layer. CUDA is not a driver; it is the universal operating system of modern machine intelligence.

---

### PART 4: THE $177 DIP — VALUATION DISLOCATION VS HYPERSCALER CAPEX REALITY

When sentiment collapsed to $177 following headlines of the Megaspeed probe and corporate leadership noise, market participants conflated temporary governance gossip with structural business decay.

Let's look at the financial math that Wall Street momentum traders ignored.

#### 1. The $200B+ Hyperscaler Balance Sheet Guarantee
Nvidia does not rely on consumer discretionary spending or cyclical enterprise PC cycles. Its primary customers are four of the most cash-generative corporate fortresses on earth:
- Microsoft: $55B - $65B+ annual AI CapEx
- Alphabet (Google): $48B - $52B+ annual CapEx
- Meta Platforms: $38B - $42B+ annual CapEx
- Amazon (AWS): $60B - $75B+ annual CapEx

Combined, Tier-1 hyperscalers have formally committed over $200 Billion in data center infrastructure spending. When Satya Nadella, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sundar Pichai were asked during earnings calls whether they were over-investing in compute, their responses were unanimous:
*The risk of under-investing in frontier compute far outweighs the risk of over-investing.*

If you under-invest, your platform becomes obsolete. If you over-invest, you own the foundational infrastructure that powers the global economy for the next 15 years.

#### 2. Blackwell Is Sold Out for 12 to 18 Months
Every single Blackwell production run coming out of TSMC’s fabs in Hsinchu and Tainan is 100% pre-booked across the entire calendar year. Customers are paying cash upfront and committing to long-term take-or-pay energy contracts simply to secure delivery slots.

#### 3. Forward Multiple Realities
At the $177 level:
- Nvidia traded at approximately 28x to 32x forward consensus EPS.
- For context: consumer staple conglomerates selling soda and toothpaste trade at 24x forward earnings with 3% organic growth.
- Nvidia was delivering 65% to 75% gross margins with top-line growth exceeding 60% year-over-year.
- Consensus Wall Street price targets among tier-one semiconductor analysts (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein) maintain price targets between $300 and $400 over a 24-month horizon.

Selling Nvidia at $177 because of a personal relationship probe or a third-party Singapore smuggling ring was a classic liquidity dislocation—a textbook opportunity where transient headlines collide with unmovable balance sheet fundamentals.

---

### PART 5: THE STRATEGIC PLAYBOOK FOR AI FOUNDERS & ENTERPRISE LEADERS

If you are an enterprise CIO, an AI startup founder, or a tech allocator, what does the AI Hardware Cold War mean for your operational roadmap?

#### Rule 1: Hedge Against Hardware Heterogeneity
Do not write monolithic bare-metal code locked to single-vendor low-level primitives unless you are training frontier base models. 
- Build on higher abstraction compilers: PyTorch 2.x, Triton, and vLLM.
- Keep inference workloads portable across multi-cloud clusters to prevent vendor hold-up pricing.

#### Rule 2: Token Economics Over Raw FLOPS
Raw GPU counts are vanity; cost-per-token-served is sanity.
- Transition your inference architecture to FP4/FP8 quantization architectures immediately. Blackwell's 4x throughput improvement on low-precision inference means organizations that optimize models for FP4 will run workloads at 70% lower operational expenditure than competitors clinging to FP16.

#### Rule 3: Sovereign Compute Is the New Oil
Expect export controls to tighten further, not loosen. 
- If you are building globally, understand that compute sovereignty is becoming localized. Data residency laws combined with US export restrictions will force enterprise deployments into regional sovereign clouds (Europe, Japan, India, Middle East). 
- Align with infrastructure providers that have direct, compliant allocations of TSMC-packaged silicon.

#### Rule 4: Capitalize on Generational Macro Mispricings
When the market offers you a premier monopoly asset with 75% gross margins, an unbreakable software moat, and sold-out product pipelines at a deep valuation discount due to geopolitical gossip, you don't panic. 

You read the balance sheets. You study the physics of the silicon chokepoints. And you allocate with conviction.

text:
It is an absurd, tragic comedy of our modern notion of liberty. Even under our free speech laws, open calls for the "killing of infidels" or the collapse of Western society are granted full legal protection. 

When Thomas Jefferson helped lay the groundwork for the First Amendment, he envisioned a safe harbor for individual conscience —never anticipating the sheer, inconceivable lunacy of a system protecting the very ideologies actively preaching to conquer us, kill us, or reduce us to dhimmis.

It’s the ultimate punchline for our enemies, who openly boast: "Use democracy to destroy democracy and Western Civilization."

Yet history shows that Jefferson himself bumped into this exact wall of absurdity. In 1786, while serving as U.S. Minister to France alongside John Adams, he asked Tripoli's ambassador why Barbary pirates were plundering American merchant ships without provocation. The ambassador offered no geopolitical excuse; he simply cited religious doctrine regarding non-believers, declaring it their divine right and duty to wage war and enslave captives.

While Europe chose the cowardly route of paying off the pirates, Jefferson refused to play the fool. As President, he launched the First Barbary War (1801–1805), sending the U.S. Navy and Marines to answer religious piracy with naval cannon fire.

Jefferson was a fierce defender of individual freedom of conscience —explicitly framing his Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom to protect the civil rights of all people, including Muslims, Jews, and non-believers. 

But he drew a hard, pragmatic line between personal faith and militant political aggression. For Jefferson, freedom of thought was sacred, but the Constitution was never meant to be a suicide pact that subsidizes its own destruction.

The tragic farce of Western civilization today is that in our rush to prove how open-minded we are, we risk leaving the front door unlocked for those who have explicitly promised to burn the house down.

Connecticut voter registration via DMV and related channels
Connecticut has a form of automatic/motor-voter registration at the DMV, but it still relies on self-attestation of citizenship rather than documentary proof. 

Here is the current process and what the data shows.
How DMV registration works
•When someone applies for, renews, or replaces a Connecticut driver’s license, learner’s permit, or non-driver ID, they are offered (or prompted for) voter registration.
•The applicant must check a box and affirm under penalty of perjury that they are a U.S. citizen, a resident, of age, and otherwise eligible.
•If the person indicates they are not a U.S. citizen, the voter-registration portion stops.
From the 2024 EAVS data brief, Motor Vehicle Department transactions accounted for 27.7% of registration transactions received between the 2022 and 2024 general elections (732,283 total transactions statewide).

Article Title
Engineering the Laser-Proof Sky: Heat-Dissipating Materials for Next-Gen Airborne Defense

Full Article Text
In an era where directed-energy weapons are moving from laboratories to the operational edge, protecting high-value airborne assets—future Air Force One variants, combat aircraft, or unmanned platforms—requires more than reflective coatings. A sustained 100-kilowatt continuous-wave beam deposits hundreds of watts of heat into even a high-reflectivity surface. Conventional optics fail not from poor reflection, but because the residual absorbed energy has nowhere to go before temperatures spike, coatings delaminate, and surfaces distort or melt.

The Real Challenge Is Heat, Not Light

No mirror is perfectly reflective. Even the best commercial laser mirrors absorb 0.1–1 percent of incident power. At 100 kW that is 100–1,000 W concentrated in a small spot—enough to destroy uncooled gold-on-silicon optics in seconds to tens of seconds. Survival depends on how rapidly that heat is conducted away from the illuminated zone and removed from the system.

Materials That Dissipate Rather Than Merely Reflect

Single-crystal diamond, with thermal conductivity approaching 2,200 W/m·K, offers a step-change. Harvard researchers etched golf-tee-shaped nanostructures into CVD diamond to create monolithic metasurface mirrors with greater than 98 percent reflectivity. Under a 10 kW continuous-wave beam focused to a 750-micron spot—intensity high enough to cut steel—the diamond surface showed no damage, no morphological change, and maintained reflectivity. Conventional multilayer dielectric mirrors failed under the same conditions. Diamond does not eliminate absorption; it simply moves the heat so fast that local temperature rises remain manageable.⁠Nature

Copper remains the industrial workhorse. Oxygen-free copper mirrors with internal cooling channels routinely handle tens of kilowatts continuously in laser manufacturing. Gold or dielectric coatings raise reflectivity while copper’s ~400 W/m·K conductivity spreads heat to the coolant. For aerospace, the engineering question becomes how to capture this performance at flight weight.

Aerospace Engineering Opportunity

Laboratory success does not automatically translate to aircraft. Large-area diamond fabrication, resistance to vibration and thermal cycling under high-g maneuvers, and integration with existing aircraft thermal-management loops are open problems. Hybrid architectures—diamond heat-spreaders bonded to actively cooled copper or silicon-carbide substrates, deployable or rotating panels that spread load in both space and time, and adaptive optics that correct residual distortion—offer practical paths. Mass, power, and reliability budgets remain the binding constraints; materials advances only become mission capability when aerospace engineers design the thermal, structural, and systems architectures that keep the platform flying.

The next generation of laser-resistant surfaces will not be pure mirrors. They will be multifunctional thermal systems: highly reflective where the beam strikes, aggressively conductive beneath, and continuously cooled or heat-sinked into the vehicle. Directed-energy threats are real and advancing. The engineering response is equally real—rooted in thermal physics, materials innovation, and the systems discipline that aerospace engineers already practice every day. Those who solve the heat problem will define the survivability of future airborne platforms.

text:
♊️
Analysis of the Quoted Post by Eric Sammons
Eric Sammons writes:
Forgiving your enemies is hard. I'd even say impossible without the grace of God. If you've never been betrayed, or truly and viciously been attacked by someone, you don't realize how hard it is. As Christians, it's our duty to do so, but let's not pretend it's easy.
Elaboration
Sammons addresses the psychological and spiritual weight of interpersonal betrayal and the traditional Christian mandate to forgive. His argument rests on an experiential premise: that true, deep-seated forgiveness in the wake of vicious attacks requires an external or transcendent source of strength ("the grace of God") because human emotional instincts naturally lean toward self-protection, resentment, or retribution. He distinguishes between theoretical or superficial forgiveness—which is easy to offer when no real stakes are involved—and existential forgiveness, which is forged under the pressure of genuine injury.
Fallacies Involved
Appeal to Emotion (Argumentum ad Passiones): Sammons relies heavily on the emotional resonance of being "truly and viciously attacked" and "betrayed." While it illustrates his point, it shifts the focus from an objective evaluation of forgiveness to a subjective appeal to the reader's sympathy or shared experience of pain.
No True Scotsman (Implicit): By asserting that someone who has "never been betrayed" cannot realize how hard it is, he attempts to gatekeep the validity of the judgment based on lived suffering, implying that critics or observers who find it simple either lack real experience or aren't facing genuine trials.
Analysis of the Reply by Dennis Jordan
Dennis Jordan replies:
These Christians cannot stop hating on one another, yet claim they are forgiving 😂 They use their faith as a shield and a cudgel.
Elaboration
Jordan shifts the critique from the difficulty of the theological concept to the hypocrisy of the practitioners. He observes a common sociological and rhetorical phenomenon within insular ideological or religious communities: high moral ideals (like forgiveness and charity) being preached simultaneously with fierce internecine conflict, factionalism, and mutual hostility. His use of the metaphor "shield and cudgel" points to instrumentalized faith—where religious language is deployed defensively to deflect criticism (shield) and offensively to attack ideological opponents (cudgel) while wearing the guise of righteousness.
Fallacies Involved
Hasty Generalization (Secundum Quid): Jordan takes the behavior of specific individuals or factions within a religious group and applies it categorically to "These Christians" as a monolith, ignoring those within the tradition who genuinely strive for reconciliation without public posturing.
Ad Hominem / Tu Quoque: Instead of engaging with Sammons' specific premise—that forgiveness is an arduous psychological hurdle requiring transcendent backing—Jordan attacks the perceived character and internal consistency of the group Sammons represents, dismissing the argument by pointing to the hypocritical behavior of its members.
Straw Man (Slight Distortion): Sammons explicitly acknowledges that forgiveness is hard and struggles to exist without divine grace, explicitly warning against pretending it is easy. Jordan's reply acts as though Christians are claiming it is easy or that they have mastered it, when Sammons' original post actually argued the exact opposite.

text:
A typical day for a general-population inmate in a U.S. federal prison (Bureau of Prisons / BOP) is highly structured, early-starting, and punctuated by multiple counts. Exact times vary by facility, security level (minimum/camp, low, medium, high), and the individual institution’s rules, but certain elements are national policy.⁠Federalcriminaldefenseattorney

Fixed National Elements
At least five official counts every 24 hours. The 4:00 p.m. count is a stand-up count (inmates stand and remain silent until cleared). An extra 10:00 a.m. stand-up count occurs on weekends and holidays. No movement is allowed during counts.⁠

Three meals a day (two of them hot), with no more than 14 hours between dinner and breakfast.Able-bodied sentenced inmates are generally required to work.
Recreation must be offered at least 10 hours per day across morning, afternoon, and evening periods.
Phones operate roughly 6:00 a.m.–11:30 p.m. (local access rules apply; monthly minutes are limited, typically up to 510).

Sample Weekday Schedule (Medium or Low Security)
This is a composite based on common BOP practices and inmate accounts. Camps are more open; higher-security units are more restricted.

~5:00–6:00 a.m.
Overnight counts have already occurred (often around midnight, 3 a.m., and 5 a.m.). Lights come on or a wake-up is announced. Inmates get up, use the toilet/sink, make their bunks, and get ready. A morning count is conducted.
~6:00–7:30 a.m.
Breakfast (“main line”) is served in the chow hall (or sometimes on trays in higher-security settings). Food is basic institutional fare—oatmeal, grits, eggs, cereal, toast, fruit, etc. Many inmates eat quickly and return to the unit to clean their area before work call.
~7:30 a.m. – mid-afternoon
Work call. Most inmates report to assigned jobs (kitchen, laundry, maintenance, grounds, warehouse, orderly work, or UNICOR/Federal Prison Industries factories making products such as furniture or textiles). Others attend education classes, vocational training, substance-abuse programs (RDAP), or other scheduled call-outs.
Lunch is typically served around 11:00 a.m.–12:30 p.m. There is usually a midday count. After lunch, work or programming continues. Recreation (yard, gym, weights, basketball, walking track, etc.) is often available in scheduled blocks.
~3:30–4:00 p.m.
Yard recall. Everyone returns to their assigned housing unit or location for the 4:00 p.m. stand-up count—one of the most important of the day. Inmates stand silently by their bunks until the count clears institution-wide.
~4:15–6:00 p.m.
Dinner is served. Afterward, mail may be distributed.
Evening (post-dinner to ~9:00–10:00 p.m.)
This is the main free-time window in the housing unit: watching TV in common areas, playing cards or board games, reading, writing letters, using the phone or TRULINCS email system, showering, or socializing. Some evening recreation or programs may be available. An evening count occurs (often around 9:00–10:00 p.m.).
~10:00–11:00 p.m.
Lights out or lockdown in most facilities. Nighttime counts continue while inmates are in their bunks. The cycle repeats.

Key Realities of Daily Life
Counts interrupt everything. Missing or interfering with a count is a serious disciplinary issue. Movement is controlled. Especially at medium and higher security, inmates move during designated “moves” rather than freely.

Work is central. Pay is low (often a few dollars to a couple dozen dollars per month depending on grade and facility). Housing varies widely. Open dorms at camps; cubicles or cells at low/medium; much more restricted at high-security or in Special Housing Units (SHU).

Commissary (canteen) is important for buying extra food, hygiene items, and supplies with the money inmates earn or receive from outside. Weekends usually have less formal work, an extra morning count, and more recreation/program time, but the overall structure remains.

Noise, limited privacy, strict rules, and boredom are consistent themes across inmate accounts. The precise schedule for any specific facility is published in that institution’s Admission & Orientation (A&O) handbook, which the BOP posts on its website for most prisons. Security level and whether an inmate is in general population, on a work detail, in programs, or in restricted housing dramatically changes the day.⁠
This is a generalized picture drawn from BOP policy and common practices; individual experiences differ.

text:
Late into the night, past midnight.

After speaking with countless people, enduring the inevitable political discussions that always surface at these gatherings, and taking part in the celebration itself, exhaustion had finally set in. All you wanted was to head home and rest.

St. Louis had left the party earlier. You'd kept her waiting while you handled a few last matters, but at last the two of you made your way to the car. To your surprise, she offered you the driver's seat, despite the fact that it was her vehicle.

She leaned slightly toward you, studying your face.  
"Tired, Commander-kun?"

"A little", you answered, settling back into the seat. "At least it's now over".

St. Louis's fingers brushed lightly over your forearm, the touch soft against the fabric of your tuxedo. Her gaze was unmistakably mischievous.  

"The night is still young" she murmured. "It would be such a waste for it to end so soon… especially now that we finally have some time to ourselves, don't you think?"

She held your eyes and made a slow, deliberate gesture with her right hand... her invitation was clear.

You understood. Without another word, you fastened your seatbelt and started the car, pulling away from the party and into the quiet streets beneath the moonlight.

"This is going to be a long night…" you thought as you pressed the accelerator.

St. Louis's hand came to rest gently over yours. You returned the gesture, lacing your fingers with hers. In the rearview mirror you caught the soft, almost sweet smile she wore.

You'd almost certainly wake up exhausted the next morning, but, it would be the kind of exhaustion that left no doubt the night had been worth every minute.
