BRITAIN'S EARLY-RELEASE POLICIES ARE UNDER FIRE: A repeat robbery offender who KICKED, ROBBED, and TERRORIZED her boyfriend in his 70s is reportedly BACK ON THE STREETS after serving just ONE-THIRD of her 27-month prison sentence!!

And her elderly victim told the court that the relentless abu$e had left him so depressed and isolated that he wanted to GIVE UP ON LIFE.

Katie Bland, now 32, of Halifax, West Yorkshire, was sentenced in August 2025 after pleading guilty to robbery, as$ault by beating, fraud, and blackmail following a violent attack on her elderly partner.

The incident happened on January 6, 2025, after an argument between Bland and the man, who was in his 70s.

According to prosecutors, the victim had left his home to escape the confrontation, but Bland continued calling him, demanding money and verbally abusing him.

Around 4 p.m., she tracked him down at Halifax bus station, where she grabbed him by the collar of his coat, threw him around, and demanded cash while insulting him and calling him a "dirty dog."

The pensioner initially offered her £20, but Bland insisted on taking his bank card.

When he refused, he offered to withdraw money from an ATM instead.

Rather than stop, Bland became increasingly aggressive, kicking the elderly man as they traveled and continuing to demand access to his money.

A female passenger witnessed the assault and attempted to intervene.

Bland turned on the woman, grabbed her by the scarf, and threatened to "knock her jaw off" if she didn't stay out of the confrontation.

She then continued assaulting her boyfriend.

Before police could intervene, Bland managed to use his bank card to withdraw £40.

But the physical attack was only part of what the victim had endured.

During sentencing at Bradford Crown Court, prosecutor Nathan Davis read a statement describing the elderly man's ongoing emotional suffering.

The victim said Bland subjected him to daily abuse, pressured him for money to purchase drugs, and had driven away his friends.

He explained that he had become so frightened of her unpredictable behavior that he dreaded returning to his own home.

"I wake up and don't know how she is going to be. I get abused daily," he told the court.

He also described experiencing the worst depression and anxiety of his life, saying her treatment had pushed him to the point where he wanted to give up on living.

And this wasn't Bland's first encounter with the criminal justice system.

The court heard that she had previous convictions and was ALREADY UNDER A SUSPENDED SENTENCE FOR ANOTHER ROBBERY when she attacked the pensioner.

Her attorney argued that Bland had been heavily dependent on drugs at the time and had since participated in prison courses intended to address her substance use and behavior.

The defense also told the court that Bland acknowledged her actions were unacceptable, wanted to change her lifestyle, and had family members willing to support her after prison.

Recorder Gordon sentenced her to 27 months behind bars.

But reports now circulating claim Bland HAS ALREADY BEEN RELEASED after serving approximately nine months, roughly one-third of her sentence, and is living in the Halifax area.

Her exact release date and the legal basis for her reported release have not been independently confirmed.

The case has renewed relevance because of major changes to Britain's sentencing laws.

On October 1, 2026, new provisions of the Sentencing Act 2026 took effect in England and Wales, allowing many prisoners serving standard fixed-term sentences to be released after completing just ONE-THIRD of their custodial terms.

Previously, many prisoners in that category were required to serve 40% or 50% of their sentences before automatic release.

The British government introduced the changes amid a prison overcrowding crisis, arguing that earlier release combined with supervision in the community would help manage prison capacity while maintaining public safety.

Prisoners released under the system remain subject to licence conditions and can be returned to custody if they violate those requirements.

Certain serious offenses are excluded from the new one-third release rules, but critics have warned that some violent offenders and domestic abusers remain eligible.

Even Britain's Domestic Abuse Commissioner has publicly expressed concern about the number of perpetrators who could qualify for earlier release.

The government has responded by pointing to additional probation supervision, electronic monitoring, and safeguards for domestic abuse cases.

Bland's reported release has not been directly linked to the October legislation, and authorities have not publicly confirmed which release provisions applied to her case.

But the broader controversy raises serious questions about how Britain's sentencing system handles repeat offenders convicted of violence against vulnerable victims.

text:
SCP-195: A “Medicinal Whiskey”

SCP-195 was sold to slavecatchers in the American South before the Civil War. The men selling it claimed it could sharpen the drinker's mind. It really did improve their senses, which helps explain why they chose people who made their living tracking down other human beings.

The effects that followed were much less useful to the customer.

At first, drinking it feels like drinking a comparable amount of very rough whiskey or moonshine. After a period that varies from person to person, the drinker becomes more aware of their surroundings. Taste, touch, smell and the other senses become more sensitive.

Along with that heightened awareness comes reduced impulse control and an exaggerated fight-or-flight response. Foundation tests found a substantial increase in violent behavior. The person has more sensory information coming in and less restraint over how they react to it.

Several of the most violent test results are expunged. The surviving material says affected subjects were capable of extreme violence and appeared to enjoy it. The report also names a research assistant, Renfield, who received a posthumous citation for going beyond the requirements of duty. Whatever happened during that research was serious enough for further testing of those capabilities to be judged unnecessary.

The initial effects eventually wear off, and subjects generally appear to return to normal. There is a redacted exception to that statement, so the file doesn't give us every outcome. But even the apparent recovery doesn't last.

Within a month, everyone who has consumed it develops fatigue and a general feeling of listlessness. Scans show ulcer-like wounds forming in the stomach and lungs. Those wounds keep spreading until the person dies.

Their skin and muscles also begin to break down, particularly around areas subjected to movement or stress. That deterioration continues as well. The published entry doesn't offer a cure or describe a subject who recovered from the later stage.

So there are two periods of danger. First, the drink can make somebody more violent while giving them sharper senses. Then, after those effects seem to have passed, the physical damage becomes apparent. The article says consuming any quantity triggers the process. It doesn't identify a harmless dose.

The Foundation found out about it through a case in Alabama. A historian's son had been helping catalog items in an antebellum house, where he discovered the whiskey. He was later arrested and sentenced for a murder, but the details and his age are redacted.

His case initially attracted only minor local coverage. The Foundation became interested when he was admitted to a hospital and informants noticed the unusual deterioration of his skin and organs. Investigators traced it back to the house and recovered an opened case of the bottles.

Seventeen bottles are now in Foundation custody at Site-1279. The item is classified Euclid, even though the locker happens to be in the site's Safe-class storage section. Access requires written authorization from at least two Level Four personnel and a security escort.

Staff also have to wear protective equipment and respirators. That precaution is based on an untested possibility that evaporated whiskey could expose somebody through inhalation. Whether breathing its vapor actually causes the same effects is still unknown.

More bottles may still exist. Recovery personnel are told to watch for matching bottles and labels and to use protective equipment if they find any.

The two salesmen are where the history gets stranger. Accounts describe one as unusually tall and blond, and the other as dark-haired with a stoop. Both had strikingly bright eyes and wore matching clothing, although the relevant detail about that clothing is redacted.

Historical sources say they were often driven out of town once people discovered the side effects. Those same sources record the pair being hanged on at least two occasions. The report never explains how the same salesmen apparently survived long enough for that to happen more than once.

The final addendum links their descriptions to information the Foundation has now, but too much is removed to identify them confidently. The surviving text indicates that they remain uncaptured and that capturing them is a high priority. The rest of that connection is hidden from the reader.

There's an obvious temptation to read the whiskey as some kind of punishment for the people it was sold to. The article never confirms that motive. The product also made those buyers more dangerous to the people they were pursuing before it began destroying their bodies. Whatever the salesmen intended, the harm wasn't limited to the people who took a drink. And the Alabama case shows that an old bottle could keep doing damage long after its original customers were gone.

The Berlin Wall was one of history's most powerful symbols of division and oppression. But its story is also one of survival, courage, hope, and resistance, and a testament to what people are willing to do in their pursuit of democracy and freedom.

The Berlin Wall: A World Divided, the internationally acclaimed exhibition currently making its North American premiere at Union Station, offers fascinating insights into one of the most defining periods of the 20th century while also exploring the deeply personal human stories behind one of history's most enduring symbols of division.

To commemorate the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall, tickets to the exhibition are just $10 each through Sunday, November 15, with the goal of making this extraordinary experience accessible to as many people in our community as possible.

text:
One of my favorite things about living in Japan is how you can walk into a restaurant, spend less than ¥500, and get a genuinely satisfying meal in just a few minutes.

And when it comes to Japanese fast food, few things beat a good bowl of gyudon (牛丼).

For those unfamiliar, gyudon is a simple dish of thinly sliced beef and onions simmered in a slightly sweet, savory sauce and served over a bowl of steamed rice. Nothing particularly fancy, but it’s one of those meals that always hits the spot.

What’s interesting is that Japan has three major chains that have built entire businesses around this one dish: Yoshinoya, Sukiya, and Matsuya.

And believe it or not, people here have pretty strong opinions about which one is best.

Yoshinoya (吉野家) is the original. Founded in 1899, it’s been serving beef bowls for well over a century. Of the three, I’d say Yoshinoya feels the most traditional. It’s straightforward Japanese comfort food. You come in, order your bowl, eat, and you’re back out the door before you know it.

Sukiya (すき家) is the largest of the three in Japan and probably the most interesting when it comes to variety. You can get your standard gyudon, but they also offer all sorts of toppings, from cheese and kimchi to green onions and eggs. It’s a little less traditional, but that’s part of the appeal.

Then there’s Matsuya (松屋), which actually calls its beef bowl gyumeshi (牛めし). What I like about Matsuya is that it feels a bit more like a complete meal. You get a complimentary bowl of miso soup when dining in, and their menu goes well beyond beef bowls, with curry and various set meals.

The funny thing is that all three are incredibly affordable, with a regular beef bowl costing around ¥480–¥500 these days.

Coming from the US, where a basic fast-food meal can easily run you $12–15, it’s still pretty amazing to me that you can sit down in Tokyo and have a hot meal for roughly $3.

I’ve lived in Japan for years, and these places have been a constant throughout my time here. Whether it’s grabbing a quick lunch between errands, eating after a long day at work, or finding something open late at night, there’s almost always a gyudon shop nearby.

And while Japan gets plenty of attention for its sushi, ramen, and high-end restaurants, I think places like these deserve just as much appreciation. They’re a huge part of everyday life here.

Personally, I think the best way to experience gyudon is to try all three and decide for yourself.

So for those of you living in Japan, or who’ve visited, I’m curious.

Yoshinoya, Sukiya, or Matsuya? Which one gets your vote?

text:
🪔 The Legend of King Bali & The Cosmic Steps of Vamana 🪔

Today marks Balipratipada (also celebrated as Bali Padyami or Diwali Padva), one of the most spiritually profound days of the Diwali festival. 

While many associate Diwali solely with the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya, today honors a story of ultimate surrender, righteousness, and a king who won the heart of the Divine.

Here is the rich history behind today’s celebrations:

✨ The Golden Reign of King Mahabali -
King Mahabali was an Asura (demon) king, but unlike others, he was incredibly wise, generous, and a devout worshipper of the divine. Under his rule, the earth flourished with unprecedented peace, equality, and prosperity. However, his growing power and influence over the three realms deeply worried the Devas (gods), who feared losing their celestial kingdom.

✨ The Descent of the Vamana Avatar -
To restore cosmic balance, Lord Vishnu manifested as Vamana, a young, dwarf Brahmin. Vamana approached King Bali during a grand sacrificial ritual and made a seemingly humble request: just enough land as could be measured by three of his footsteps. Known for his unyielding generosity, King Bali smiled and granted the request, ignoring warnings that this was no ordinary Brahmin.

✨ The Three Cosmic Steps -
Suddenly, the dwarf Brahmin expanded into the cosmic giant Trivikrama.
•With his first step, he covered the entire Earth.
•With his second step, he claimed the skies and heavens.
•With no room left for the third step, King Bali bowed his head in complete humility and offered it to the Lord.
Placing his foot upon Bali’s head, Vishnu pushed him down to Patala (the netherworld).

✨ The Eternal Boon & The Return - 
Impressed by Bali's absolute surrender, devotion, and adherence to his word, Lord Vishnu granted him a timeless boon. Bali was allowed to return to Earth once a year to ensure his people were happy, prosperous, and well-governed. This annual return is what we celebrate today!

🏡 How It Is Celebrated Today:
•Rangoli & Effigies: 
Homes are decorated with beautiful clay or rice-powder images of King Bali and his wife, Vindhyavali, welcoming his benevolent spirit back into our households.

•Diwali Padva: 
In Western India, it marks a deeply personal celebration of love, where husbands present special gifts to their wives.

•New Beginnings: 
Businesses open fresh account books, stepping into the traditional New Year (Vikram Samvat) with prayers for wealth and wisdom.

May the story of King Bali remind us to practice generosity, humility, and unwavering faith. 

Wishing you all a blessed, happy, and prosperous Balipratipada! 💫✨

text:
Only point I’ll concede here is Nebraska looking at the Big Ten for a while. But the main reason they were looking is they felt like Texas was trying to call all the shots. They didn’t like that they got separated from playing their main rival, OU, every year.

LHN doesn’t get announced in January 2011 without immense discussions all throughout 2010. Why would ESPN offer this network to Texas? Everyone not wearing burnt orange glasses could have told you it would be a failure for ESPN financially. Unless the point was really a bribe for Texas not to do the PAC-16 deal.

Texas running off Nebraska and talk of a PAC-16 conference made everyone on edge and had them looking in 2010. This undoubtedly had A&M looking at the SEC, but they said they were 50/50 on the SEC in 2010.  But the LHN drove that to 100% immediately. Missouri was left out of the PAC-16 plot so they were ready to go to SEC and not wait it out. Colorado saw how unstable everything was and wanted out.

All of this was caused by Texas not acting like good conference partners. They didn’t seem to want to pull up a chair settle in with us. Unequal revenue sharing was a major red flag and sign of an unhealthy partnership.

So yeah, the original Big 12 breaking up was pretty much all Texas’ fault. Now you’re in a conference where you share revenue anyways, there’s still plenty of bottom dwellers you’re carrying, and you’re still traveling a lot. You have very little history with the legacy SEC outside of Arkansas.

Honestly, Texas was bitching about money, but doesn’t even need it. Another complaint was being in the Big 12 hurt recruiting. Well, in the NIL era, you could buy a team and crush the Big 12. Not so easy in the SEC.

And yeah, conference balance is a good thing. It’s good for the strong teams and it gives weaker teams a spot and shot every now and then.

text:
I had a burial this afternoon (long story) and so was praying the Office of the Dead while I was on my morning walk through the cemetery. The responsories after the readings are generally amazing, and genius, and heart-wrenching. Here is a sample of one reading with its responsory:
----------------------
Lection VI – Job 14:7–12
For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down,
that it will sprout again,
and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
Though the root thereof wax old in the earth,
and the stock thereof die in the ground;
yet through the scent of water it will bud,
and bring forth boughs like a plant.
But man dieth, and wasteth away:
yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
As the waters fail from the sea,
and the flood decayeth and drieth up:
so man lieth down, and riseth not:
till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake,
nor be raised out of their sleep.

Responsory – Redemptor meus vivit
℟ My redeemer liveth, and at the latter day I shall rise.
* And my bones shall be renewed again, and in my flesh I shall see my Lord.
℣ Praise the Lord, O my soul. While I live will I praise the Lord: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being.
* And my bones shall be renewed again, and in my flesh I shall see my Lord.
----------------------
But what sorts of things do you sing at a funeral when you have a praise band? What words do you have to offer that aren't trivialized, puerilized, neutered, gutted by the way in which they are carried along?

I was at a funeral a few years ago, and sat next to a family member whose Lutheran church had been an enthusiastic adopter of the praise band/wannabe megachurch nonsense. We sang "Let Us Ever Walk with Jesus," among other hymns, at the service, and later she said, with some confusion and the faint traces of a dawning horror, "I don't think my grandkids know any of those hymns." It may have been decades since she came across them, but she still knew them. But her kids? Less so. Her grandkids? Not at all.

The first generation to throw out their inheritance will probably be all right, for the most part. They have a solid foundation, even if they aren't building much on it. The next generation will be a bit of a mix, with some carried along by simple institutional inertia, and others seeing the shallowness of this new faith and drifting (or running) away. But the third generation? They will see the vacuousness clearly, assume that this empty shell is the Christian faith, and not only walk away, but try to tear it all down. These are the "exvangelicals", the deconstructionists, the ones whose parents laid their foundations on sand and were *shocked* when it all came crashing down.

But it didn't happen overnight. And it didn't have to happen at all.

Which way, Missouri?

text:
The Twelve Months Sanctified by Prayer: November, Month of the Souls in Purgatory by M. L'ABBE A. RICARD, D.S.G. Translated from the French. 1877 November 12 THE GREATEST OF THE WORKS OF MERCY.
.
Prelude.
.
Let us transport ourselves in spirit to the judgment-seat, and hear the just Judge say to the elect, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave Me to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave Me to drink : I was a stranger, and you took Me in: naked, and you covered Me: sick, and you visited Me: I was in prison, and you came to Me."
.
Meditation.
.
Charity towards the souls in Pur­gatory comprises in itself all the works of mercy which have just been enumerated, and also greatly surpasses them in merit; for in fact the Christian who delivers a soul from Purgatory, and who opens heaven for him, gives him not only the crumbs from his table, but the bread of angels and all the delights of paradise, for which he hungers to such a degree that no torment is equal to this pain. He gives him not only a glass of water, but the entire fountain of that water which springs to eternal life, of that water for which he thirsts so ardently that he burns day and night without being able to procure the least refreshment. He does not harbour him as he would have done a passing stranger, but he introduces him into the blissful abode for which he sighs, and whose entrance was closed to him from the time of creation. He clothes him not in a perishable garment, but in a robe of immor­tality which will eternally preserve him from cold and heat. He visits to assist him, not during a slight attack of fever, but amidst the ardour of pitiless flames which torment him with­ out allowing him any repose. Finally, he descends into his prison to break his chains, and give him the glorious liberty of the children of God.
.
Resolution.
.
Offer up something to-day, for the most suffering soul in Purgatory.
.
Aspiration.
.
Come, ye blessed of My Father. (Gospel according to St. Matthew xxv. 34.)
.
EXAMPLE: ST. AUGUSTINE'S REPRIMAND.
.
St. Augustine strongly reproved the temerity of a writer of his time, who said that we ought not to fear Purgatory, since the torments suffered there would not last for ever. " What does it signify," he said, "how long a time I shall spend there, so that I enter heaven at last;" and St. Augustine says in answer to this: "Let no one speak thus, for the fire of expiation will be more terrible than any suffering in this world, however dreadful we may imagine it to be."
.
Senno . VI . de Sandis.

text:
The Twelve Months Sanctified by Prayer: November, Month of the Souls in Purgatory by M. L'ABBE A. RICARD, D.S.G. Translated from the French. 1877 November 11 YOU DID IT TO ME.
.
Prelude.
.
Our Lord Himself invites us to in­tercede for the souls in Purgatory. Let us listen reverently to Him, and after spending a few minutes in lovingly considering His infinite goodness, let us meditate on one of the most powerful motives which could excite our devotion to the souls in Purgatory.
.
Meditation.
.
The motives on which we have already meditated must. if our soul is Christian and full of faith, have made a great impression. Today we shall meditate on another motive, which, if it leaves us cold and insensible, will show that we do not even deserve the name of Christian, and that we have not an atom of faith.
.
God, Whose majesty is immense, Whose goodness and liberality are infinite, God Whom we have so often offended, and Who has obliged us, in a thousand ways, to pay Him every homage, God, I say, has vouchsafed by an inconceivable prodigy to accept all the good which we do to man as if it was done to Himself. His Son has assured us of it when He said, "Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these, My least brethren, you did it to Me." It is as if He said : All the works of mercy which you have exercised towards My brethren have been as agreeable to Me as if you had done them to Me. I am not the less obliged for the help given to the soul of one of My brethren than if you had delivered it from Purgatory, and sent it to heaven. How then can we neglect anything which pleases the Son of God so much? Can we be influenced by a more powerful motive?
.
Resolution.
.
Remember sometimes that Our Lord considers as done to Himself the help which we give the souls in Purgatory.
.
Aspiration.
.
"You did it to Me." (Gospel according to St. Matthew xxv. 40.)
.
EXAMPLE: MARY OF THE ANGELS (Maria degli Angeli).
.
A very edifying life has been published of Mary of the Angels, a Carmelite beatified by his Holiness Pius IX. Here are some extracts from it:
.
"It is quite certain that this blessed soul pos­sessed an heroic charity and devotion to the souls in Purgatory, and two causes conspired to give her these sentiments. First, it was her love of God. Nothing is dearer to God than these souls which the flames of Purgatory cleanse from every stain, and Mary of the Angels did not forget this, and therefore as deep as was her love for her divine Master, so deep also was her desire of delivering those souls which she knew He loved so tenderly. Secondly, it was her charity towards her neighbour. A super­ natural light had shown her the sad condition of those souls, and the unspeakable torments which they suffer, and this knowledge had so excited her compassion in their favour that she left nothing undone to procure their deliverance. She spared neither prayers, fasting, nor penances, to attain this holy end, and she tried also to in­ spire the same feelings in her sisters and secular­ persons.
.
As there is no work holier or more beneficial to the souls in Purgatory than the sacrifice of the Mass, Mary of the Angels was careful to have it often offered up for the repose of their souls, and for this end she held out her hand to the rich, and occupied herself in pious labours. When she filled the office of prioress, she employed herself in working altar-linen and ornaments, which she sent to some priest or church, asking for sole payment that Masses should be celebrated for the holy souls; she inspired her sisters with the same generous feelings, and induced them to employ themselves in the same manner. During one of her priorships, as she was praying one night for the souls in Purgatory, she yielded to an impulse of fervour, and promised to have five Masses celebrated for their intention every month.
.
In the morning, she made known her promise to her assistants,. who remarked that her desire could not be accomplished, because of the extreme poverty of the house. God then came in a wonderful manner to the help of the generous prioress. During the day, a stranger came to seek her, and told her that it was his custom to have a great many Masses celebrated, and that he felt himself inspired to give her an alms, so that she could have five celebrated every month, leaving her also entire liberty with regard to the application of the holy sacrifice."

text:
🍂 A Golden Autumn Escape: Ginkgo Trees & Silver Reeds in Dongshan

There’s a special kind of magic in Suzhou in November. Along the shores of Taihu Lake, golden ginkgo leaves shimmer in the sunlight, while silvery reed plumes sway gently in the autumn breeze. It's the kind of scenery that makes you want to slow down and stay a little longer.

For a peaceful autumn escape, head to Mianfo Temple (眠佛寺) in Dongshan. Tucked away among the hills and woodland, this quiet mountain temple feels worlds away from the bustle of the city. Follow the winding paths through bamboo groves and trees dressed in autumn colors, with fallen leaves beneath your feet and sunlight filtering through the branches.

At the temple, golden ginkgo trees frame the traditional architecture, creating a beautiful contrast against the deep blue autumn sky. The occasional sound of birds, the gentle rustle of leaves, and the warmth of the afternoon sun make this little corner of Dongshan feel like a world of its own.

And don't miss the reed fields along Taihu Avenue, near Suzhou Garden Expo Park. Stretching for kilometers along the lakeside, the tall reeds turn into a sea of silvery white in late autumn. Walk along the embankment, watch the plumes dance in the breeze, and take in the open views of Taihu Lake. With the lake on one side and golden reeds on the other, every turn offers a picture-perfect moment.

Some of autumn's loveliest moments are found away from the crowds. Whether you're wandering through a quiet mountain temple or standing by the lake among swaying reeds, Dongshan is a beautiful place to embrace the softer side of the season.

📍 Where to go:
• Mianfo Temple, Dongshan
• Taihu Avenue, near Suzhou Garden Expo Park

🍁 When to visit: November, when the ginkgo leaves turn golden and the reeds are at their seasonal best.

Save this little autumn escape for your next trip to Suzhou!

text:
𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗼𝗻 𝗧𝗶𝗽𝘂 𝗦𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗮𝗻
*****
A Persian manuscript in the British Library in London and other documents help correct an error in Tipu Sultan’s birthdate. The ensuing research also offers a fresh insight into the mind of the Mysore ruler.
- 𝘕𝘪𝘥𝘩𝘪𝘯 𝘎. 𝘖𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘢𝘳
- Frontline, Aug 28, 2021

THE year 2015 saw the Congress government in Karnataka under Chief Minister Siddaramaiah promulgate an order to celebrate November 10 as Tipu Sultan Jayanthi in honour of the 18th century ruler of Mysore who remained, until his death on the battlefield, the last holdout among India’s numerous rulers to resist the growing clout of the British East India Company. This date, based on the Hijri calendar, was provided by a contemporary biographer, Meer Hussein Ali Khan Kirmani, who mentioned the birthdate of his former employer and ruler of Mysore in his book Nishan i Haidar: Maroof ba Tarikh i Tipu Sultan.

The book was written a few years after the death of Tipu Sultan and translated into English by Col. W. Miles for the Royal Asiatic Society in 1842. November 10, 1750, was supposed to be the Julian calendar equivalent and November 20, 1750, the Gregorian calendar equivalent of the Islamic Hijri date, 20 Zi-hijjah, 1163, mentioned by Kirmani.

In the din of the political outcry that followed the marking of Tipu Sultan’s birthdate, even unto the cancellation of the commemoration by Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa when the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in 2019, Kirmani’s words at the end of his preface to his work were forgotten: “ What he [Kirmani] hopes from the truly learned, the generous concealer of errors, is, that, if they at any time should peruse this book, they will not dwell on the want of arrangement, or of elegance, in the language and sentences, but, by the favour of correction, lay an obligation on him, which he is ever ready to acknowledge.”

𝗢𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝟯𝟭 𝗰𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗶𝗿𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗮𝘆
It was this ‘error’ that could be corrected by way of a discovery at the British Library in London. This is the story of that discovery and the ensuing research that not only helped correct an error but offered fresh insight into the mind of Tipu Sultan. The fact that scholars and politicians of all shades had been fighting over a birthday commemoration without verifying the accuracy of that date and allowing a two-century-old error to continue reflects the damage the study of history suffers when it is caught in contemporary politics.

The British Library has in its collection a Persian manuscript, titled Fateh-al Mujahideen, with the seal and signature of Tipu Sultan. It is a military manual that Tipu Sultan prescribed to his army commanders. The fourth chapter in this manuscript contains a list of important dates on which the army was commanded to fire gun salutes. One such special day was the birthday of Tipu Sultan. This part of the document was translated into English by the Persian and Islamic scholar Adnan Rashid from London as:

“Happy celebration for the birth-date of God’s blessing, may he live long, fourteen of month Zakiri year 1165 Hijri every year on the mentioned date after ten hours upon day-rise thirty-one canon-fires commence. The celebration/ceremony should be performed by all the people of the city….”

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘂𝗱𝗶 𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗿
The mention of the Hijri year 1165 in the context of Tipu Sultan’s birthdate attracted attention because it was commonly held that Tipu Sultan was born in the Hijri year 1163. The next challenge was to relate the month Zakiri with the English calendar. There is no such month in the Islamic Hijri calendar. This month figures in the calendar Tipu Sultan created for use in Mysore. He named it the Mauludi calendar. Maulud in Arabic means ‘birth’. Tipu Sultan marked the birth of the Prophet in 572 CE as the first year of his calendar. +

text:
People, Media Can Celebrate Tipu Jayanti Themselves; Govt Will Extend Support: U.T. Khader

Bengaluru

Ahead of the annual #TipuJayanti observance on November 10, Minister for Minorities Welfare Waqf U.T. Khader stated that citizens, civic organizations and media houses are entirely free to celebrate the occasion independently, questioning why the public relies solely on official state sponsorship.

Addressing reporters who questioned whether the state government would officially organize celebrations for November 10, the minister addressed the recurring political controversy and urged community members and civic bodies to take the initiative.

'If the government has to do everything, why do you just sit and wait? Can't you do it yourselves? Did we say no?' Khader asked, recalling the fallout from past observances. He pointed out that while the previous #Siddaramaiah-led administration introduced official state celebrations,which were subsequently scrapped under the #BJP  government,little public defense was mounted for the government amidst heavy political backlash.

'When Siddaramaiah faced issues and was being heavily criticized for it, did anyone stand up and speak in his favor?' #UTKhader asked. 'All I told our people was: what was the point of granting it only to spark unrest and controversy?'

Emphasizing that private and community commemorations face no restriction, U. T. Khader called on households, social clubs, civic groups and media houses to lead the charge on November 10. He specifically challenged broadcast news channels to air half-hour documentaries highlighting #TipuSultan's history and message of communal harmony rather than expecting the state machinery to carry the sole responsibility.

Responding to a reporter's contention that it remains the government's duty to conduct the anniversary, U. T. Khader clarified that the administration has not abdicated its role, noting that official steps would be decided after taking ground realities into account.

'The government will do it,it has done so in the past, and everyone knows what transpired back then,' he said. 'We will assess the situation and act accordingly. But it's not like only the government must celebrate it. Local organizations and institutions everywhere can do it. In fact, everyone should come forward and whatever cooperation is needed from the government, it will be fully extended.'

text:
WHERE WAS THE NEED FOR THIS EXPERIMENT!

The 4 then and now the 4+2 !

The Agniveer 4+2 model is projected as a “youthful” force with reduced pension liability.

In practice it compresses formal training, delays the regular service clock, creates multi-category units at the lowest ranks, and operates on policy rather than statutory amendment.

A structured note on the gaps.
#Agniveer #Agnipath

HR & Training 

Formal training remains compressed at approximately 24–31 weeks (BMT + AMT).

The +2 extension does not restore the foundational content that was curtailed.

On-the-job training therefore proceeds on a thinner base, particularly in technical arms.

Junior leadership and NCO roles later rest on this shallower foundation plus a 4–6 year lag before the regular promotion clock begins.

Operational

Units at the lowest ranks now carry three concurrent categories: regular soldiers, 4-year Agniveers, and those on the +2 extension.

Leave entitlements, pay progression and career timelines differ.

Personnel perform identical tasks and share identical operational risk under different conditions of service. 

This generates internal comparative friction.

Battle readiness is not synonymous with chronological youth. Physical and medical standards already exist and can be re-validated.

The scheme alters training depth, leadership density and unit cohesion — the factors that determine whether a section or team is actually ready.

Legal

No amendment has been made to the Army Act or the Army Rules to create the Agniveer rank or modify the statutory meaning of enrolment.

The scheme operates through Cabinet policy and terms accepted at the time of enrolment under the unamended Act.
Differential death and disability benefits for identical operational tasks and harm remain under challenge before the Bombay High Court under Article 14. The matter is still at the High Court stage.

Fiscal

The +2 extension is a voluntary offer, not a mandatory continuation.
Pension liability begins only on absorption into the regular cadre (at the end of year 4 or year 6).

Over a 20-year horizon the fiscal outcome is a partial and delayed reduction in future liability, not its elimination.

It is secured through lower pay and leave during the Agniveer period and through the operational costs identified above.

India faces genuine resource constraints.
The same exchequer simultaneously funds large loan write-offs, political freebies and leakage in other schemes.

Pension pressure is real.

Whether the training, cohesion and readiness of the fighting force should be the residual from which savings are extracted is a question of priority.

Capital allocation for the Armed Forces is a function of assessed threat and required preparedness.

The design exchanges a prospective and limited fiscal gain for structural effects on training depth, NCO competence, unit equity and legal clarity.

These are precisely the conditions that will be tested when battle readiness is required in war.

GOVT MUST CONSIDER STATUS QUO ANTE 2022. 
#Agniveer #Agnipath

text:
AGNIPATH SCHEME: WHAT HAVE WE DONE TO THE INDIAN ARMED FORCES?

Everything was functioning reasonably well. The Indian Armed Forces have never failed this nation. Whether in war, counter-insurgency operations, safeguarding our borders, tackling internal security challenges or responding to natural disasters, our Armed Forces have always stood firm, demonstrating unparalleled courage, professionalism and commitment.

Then why was the Agnipath Scheme introduced? What was the compelling necessity?

Four years of service, followed by uncertainty about the future, and now discussions about extensions and revised engagement periods. What exactly are we trying to achieve? Have we reduced one of the finest military institutions in the world to an experimental establishment where the future of young soldiers is governed by short-term employment arrangements and changing policy decisions?

The Armed Forces are not ordinary government departments. A soldier is not made combat-ready merely by completing four years of training and service. Military ethos, discipline, regimental traditions, unit cohesion, operational experience, mutual trust and leadership are cultivated over years of dedicated service. These are the foundations of military effectiveness and cannot be developed overnight.

The real question is: What was the underlying vision behind this scheme, and was its long-term impact on the operational effectiveness, combat preparedness, institutional continuity, regimental traditions and future of India's youth adequately assessed before its introduction?

What is even more disappointing is the silence of those who should have been raising these fundamental questions. Those who understand military service, military traditions and the realities of life in uniform have a responsibility to speak up. Institutional silence cannot be allowed to replace professional debate.

The future of our youth and the institutional strength of the Indian Armed Forces cannot be treated as subjects for policy experiments.

Instead of inspiring confidence among young aspirants, have we created an employment dilemma for an entire generation that dreams of serving the nation in uniform?

Our Armed Forces have earned their reputation through decades of sacrifice, professionalism and dedication. They deserve policies that strengthen their fighting capability, preserve their institutional character, uphold military traditions and protect the dignity, security and future of those who serve.

The question is not whether the Armed Forces should adapt to changing times. They must. The real question is whether the changes being introduced genuinely strengthen our military capabilities or compromise the very foundations on which our Armed Forces have been built.

This is not merely an employment issue. It is a question of national security, military preparedness, institutional integrity and the future of India's defence forces.

Silence is not an answer. The nation deserves a serious debate, accountability and clear answers.

text:
@MayorToddGloria, serious question. Why are we committing nearly 49 acres of valuable publicly owned land to a development where 2,000 of the 4,254 homes are income restricted, instead of aggressively competing to attract engineers, advanced manufacturing, technology companies, and highly paid professionals who could strengthen San Diego’s economy for generations?

I genuinely support redeveloping the Sports Arena property. But I question whether we’re thinking ambitiously enough about what this land could become.

San Diego already has extraordinary advantages in aerospace, defense, biotechnology, robotics, autonomous systems, and scientific research.

We should be building an economic environment that attracts the world’s best engineers, researchers, entrepreneurs, and innovative companies.

Imagine a modern district with high quality market rate apartments, beautiful public spaces, research facilities, engineering offices, technology startups, and businesses creating thousands of highly paid jobs.

Those workers would spend money locally, support restaurants and small businesses, generate economic activity, and contribute to a stronger tax base.

Instead, we’re dedicating approximately 47% of the proposed housing to income restricted units while allocating only a relatively small amount of space to commercial development.

I understand affordable housing serves working families, and those residents contribute to our economy too. But we need to distinguish helping individual households from maximizing the long term economic productivity of a uniquely valuable public asset.

Why not focus more aggressively on creating opportunities for San Diegans to earn higher incomes in the first place?

Why not attract employers that can offer careers in aerospace engineering, artificial intelligence, advanced robotics, biotechnology, and other industries with substantial growth potential?

Why not create a district that encourages new companies to establish headquarters, employ local graduates, and invest in San Diego?

I understand California law imposes affordable housing obligations on certain public land developments. But that still leaves an important question.

What is the legally required minimum, and what economic tradeoffs did the city evaluate before committing to 2,000 restricted units?

I would like to see a serious comparison between this proposal and alternatives with more market rate housing, substantially greater commercial activity, and dedicated space for high paying industries.

Show us the projected tax revenue, permanent employment, average wages, private investment, infrastructure expenses, and financial returns over the next 30 to 100 years.

Your administration projects thousands of permanent jobs from this development. What percentage will actually be high paying technical and professional positions, and how do those projections compare with other possible uses of the property?

I don’t want San Diego to become a city where we simply accept that ordinary residents cannot afford to live here and respond exclusively with income restricted housing.

I want us to become a city where far more residents can afford housing because we’ve created a stronger, more productive economy with substantially better career opportunities.

Affordable housing addresses one consequence of our economic challenges. Better education, stronger industries, greater productivity, and higher incomes address other parts of the problem.

Those objectives should be evaluated together.

San Diego has the talent, universities, defense presence, and geographic advantages to become an even more significant center of American engineering and technological innovation.

We should be thinking on that scale.

Mayor Gloria, can you demonstrate that the current agreement produces greater long term public value than a more commercially ambitious alternative?

If the numbers support your decision, publish the comparison.

CALLER: My husband and I were gifted a quarter of a 680-acre ranch in Colorado. His parents, his uncle, and his little brother own the other three shares. They want to sell. We want to keep it, but we can't afford to buy them out. How do we do this peacefully?

DAVE RAMSEY: First, you and your husband write his grandfather a letter of gratitude for a quarter of a beautiful piece of ground.

CALLER: Okay.

DAVE RAMSEY: Second, respect their right to sell what they own. Pretend the next-door neighbor put a piece of ground up for sale. You'd have no entitlement to it. You can be sad someone's going to build on it, but they don't have to sell it to you, and they don't have to hold it because you want it.

DR. DELONY: Is there any problem with parceling it out so you keep your share?

CALLER: Honestly, I'm not sure. We keep going around and around on it.

DAVE RAMSEY: Here's the problem with forcing the issue. Three owners have 75% of the vote. If you refuse to sell, they can take you to court, and a judge can make you sign. And I'd bet there are no partnership documents. Was it deeded to an LLC or to four individuals?

CALLER: Four individuals, I think.

DAVE RAMSEY: Then grandpa isn't sophisticated, and that's a mess. So skip the fight. Offer to have a surveyor divide the 680 acres by four. Take your quarter, and let them sell the rest.

DR. DELONY: And before anyone gets angry, get a real valuation. You guessed a million. It could be $600,000. It could be $5 million.

CALLER: Won't they say parceling it out means everyone makes less?

DAVE RAMSEY: They might. Hard feelings are okay. Just keep them in their place. If they're grateful and not entitled, they won't mind the split. And if you're grateful and not entitled, you won't mind them selling.

CALLER: I think we'd be fine if everyone outvoted us.

DAVE RAMSEY: You got 175 free acres of prime hunting land. You didn't earn it. You hit the DNA lottery. I'd take that today.

DR. DELONY: Notice what this conversation already told you. 680 acres isn't making it one more generation. Somebody in this group is going to break it up.

A ranch deeded to four people with no paperwork.
Three owners who want out.

One couple who wants to stay. Peace isn't getting everyone to agree.

It's gratitude, no entitlement, and a surveyor.

There are very few things Democrats and Republicans still agree on.

The Red Scare is one of them.

For Democrats, Nvidia is the perfect target for tighter AI regulation and greater political control over frontier technology.

For Republicans, after a bruising midterm defeat, a sufficiently dramatic “Chinese spy” scandal offers exactly the kind of national-security villain that can redirect the conversation.

And Jensen Huang?

He is almost too perfect for the role.

Chinese-born.
Taiwanese-American.
CEO of the company sitting at the center of the AI revolution.
A man who has openly opposed Washington’s most aggressive chip restrictions on China.
A businessman whose commercial interests do not always align neatly with America’s geopolitical obsession.

So suddenly:

an affair becomes counterintelligence,
a Chinese woman becomes an “asset,”
business lobbying becomes a national-security plot,
and Nvidia becomes the stage for another round of American political theater.

Democrats want leverage over AI.
Republicans want a China villain.

And Huang happens to stand exactly where both narratives intersect.

Bipartisanship is alive and well in Washington.

It is called the Red Scare.

text:
China responds to the claim that a “Chinese female spy” exploited Jensen Huang:

The “Chinese spy” allegation is purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.

Translation:

Stop concocting spy-themed erotic fiction.

The funniest part of this story is the logic.

We are told that China was so desperate for Nvidia chips that it allegedly needed to deploy a female intelligence asset to get close to Jensen Huang and influence his lobbying in Washington.

Jensen Huang did, in fact, spend years urging Washington to loosen chip restrictions on China.

And then Washington loosened them.

So what did Beijing do?

Around 600,000 H200 chips are now sitting in Hong Kong because China has not approved large-scale imports.

Jensen Huang himself has complained that Nvidia went from roughly 95% of China’s advanced AI-chip market to 0%.

So let me understand this:

China was supposedly desperate enough to run a spy operation around Nvidia’s CEO—

but once the chips became available, China decided it would rather keep building its own ecosystem than become dependent on Nvidia again?

That is a very strange definition of “desperation.”

Maybe the problem with this story is not China.

Maybe it is the story.

text:
The U.S. wants two incompatible things from China at the same time.

It wants China dependent on Nvidia and the American AI stack.
It also wants to make sure China never gets enough cutting-edge compute to surpass American models.

So Washington restricts the best chips, then acts surprised when Beijing treats those restrictions as a forced industrial policy for domestic substitution.

And here is the part nobody can ignore anymore:

Without access to the most advanced chips, homegrown Chinese models are already on par with cutting-edge models from the United States.

That tells you that chip supremacy was never the same thing as intelligence supremacy.

The U.S. tried to use semiconductor controls to preserve dependence.

Instead, it gave China the strongest possible incentive to build an AI ecosystem that no longer needs permission from Washington.

That may turn out to be the most expensive strategic mistake of the entire chip war.

text:
Kazakhstan Pitches AI, Minerals Deals to US Investors, Pledges Legal Safeguards

Kazakhstan is courting US companies with projects in manufacturing, data centers and critical-minerals processing, while promising stronger legal protection for foreign capital, as Central Asia's largest economy seeks to reduce its reliance on oil.

American companies have invested about $50 billion in Kazakhstan over the past two decades, Deputy Foreign Minister Ardak Zebeshev said at a Kazakhstan-US B20 business roundtable in Washington on Monday, according to Telegram channel Finmentor/kz. The focus is now shifting toward economic diversification, localized production and technology transfer, he said.

Zebeshev outlined four priority areas:

• Industry and localization: deeper integration into global supply chains, citing PepsiCo Inc.'s $360 million snack plant and a $160 million pet-food project by Mars Inc.

• Digital infrastructure and AI: data centers, cloud services and regional AI capacity, including newly launched cooperation with US-based Firebird

• Energy and critical minerals: beyond long-standing partnerships with Chevron Corp. and Exxon Mobil Corp., the government wants investment in minerals processing and metallurgy to help diversify global supply chains

• Transport and logistics: expansion of the Trans-Caspian corridor and local production of rail equipment, including a $4.2 billion agreement between national railway Kazakhstan Temir Zholy JSC and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corp.

The government also flagged a large program to build schools, hospitals and other social facilities in 2027, which it said would create opportunities for US suppliers of technology, equipment and construction services. Investors are offered a one-stop-shop service, tax and customs incentives, and access to an investment headquarters chaired by the prime minister to resolve complex cases.

At the same event, First Deputy Prosecutor General Zhandos Umiraliyev said the Prosecutor General has been given the role of investment ombudsman, backed by a new Committee for the Protection of Investors' Rights. The committee coordinates government agencies, fast-tracks investor complaints and helps restore violated rights.

Prosecutors will also oversee decisions by state and quasi-state bodies that affect investors, with prior notification and approval required in cases set by law.

Officials said the goal is to make Kazakhstan a regional manufacturing and investment hub for US business, with access to wider Central Asian markets.

Source: Telegram channel Finmentor/kz, by Arman Bataev, Managing Director at OD Consulting, financial expert and auditor (ACCA).

text:
You Won the Election. Now Govern for Everyone.

Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and the responsibility of governing a divided nation.

Winning an election is one thing. Governing is another.
Following the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, Democrats have secured control of both chambers of the United States Congress. Newly elected lawmakers are arriving in Washington for orientation, photographs, interviews, and preparations for the 120th Congress, which begins in January 2027.

There is excitement. There are expectations. There are promises.

Among the proposals being championed by the Democratic Socialists of America are Medicare for All and the abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, commonly known as ICE.

These are substantial policy ambitions. They concern healthcare, immigration, public spending, law enforcement, and the relationship between government and the people it serves.

But beyond the headlines and campaign slogans, a more fundamental question deserves attention:

What does it mean to govern a country whose people do not all agree with you?

The newly elected Democrats are not entering Congress solely to represent Democrats. They are entering a national legislature whose decisions affect Republicans, independents, people who supported them, people who opposed them, and people who never voted.

That includes Americans who identify with MAGA, Americans who reject MAGA, and Americans who want nothing to do with either political camp.

Their disagreements do not make them any less American.

And their questions do not become irrelevant because their preferred candidates lost.

An Electoral Victory Is Not Universal Consent

An election establishes who has been chosen to exercise public authority. It does not establish that every voter endorses every policy proposed by the winning party.

Nor does a congressional majority automatically represent agreement on every issue among the lawmakers who compose it.

Democrats are not politically identical. Republicans are not politically identical. Independents are not a single ideological constituency.

A voter might support a Democratic candidate because of concerns about healthcare costs while disagreeing with that candidate's immigration position.

Another might vote Republican because of immigration enforcement while opposing aspects of the party's economic agenda.

Still another might vote primarily to hold an incumbent administration accountable.

These distinctions matter.

A political party can win an election without winning public agreement on every proposal associated with its platform.

The authority to legislate is not the same as universal consent to legislate in any particular way.

Representation does not require elected officials to abandon their convictions or satisfy every demand from opposing voters. Democratic government necessarily involves disagreement, negotiation, and decisions that some citizens will oppose.

But elected officials should be prepared to explain what they propose, why they propose it, how it would operate, and what consequences the public should reasonably expect.

That responsibility does not disappear when the question comes from the opposing party.

Medicare for All: What Happens After the Promise?

Consider Medicare for All.

For its supporters, the proposal addresses a fundamental concern: access to healthcare should not depend on a person's income, employment, or ability to purchase private insurance.

That concern is substantial.

But recognizing the problem is only the beginning of designing a solution.

The Medicare for All Act introduced in the House in April 2025, H.R. 3069, offers one legislative model. It proposes comprehensive national health insurance, enrollment mechanisms, a Universal Medicare card, and a two-year transition toward national coverage.

That is more specific than a campaign slogan.

Yet legislation of this magnitude raises questions that must be answered before implementation.

Who qualifies for coverage?

How will residents be enrolled?

What happens to people who already receive Medicare or Medicaid?

What happens to employer-sponsored insurance?

Will people continue seeing their existing doctors?

How will hospitals, nurses, physicians, pharmacists, and other healthcare professionals be compensated?

How will the government finance the program?

What will happen to workers employed in the private health insurance industry?

And how will patients obtain treatment if administrative systems fail during the transition?

These are not necessarily objections to universal healthcare.

They are questions about whether the proposed system can deliver what its advocates promise.

Imagine a woman waking up on a Tuesday morning with severe abdominal pain.

She has no money in her pocket. She needs medical attention.

Under the proposed system, where does she go? Does she need to complete an application? What identification must she present? Can she visit the nearest hospital? Who pays for the examination, diagnostic tests, medication, and treatment?

If she requires surgery, who authorizes it? If the hospital has insufficient capacity, what happens next?

The answers should not require a patient to understand the complexities of congressional legislation.

A functioning healthcare system must translate legislative promises into accessible services.

And there is the financial question.

Eliminating premiums, deductibles, and copayments for covered services does not eliminate the cost of providing those services.

The costs must be financed through public revenue and other arrangements established by law.

Supporters argue that a single-payer system could reduce administrative expenses and strengthen the government's ability to negotiate healthcare prices.

Critics raise concerns about taxation, federal expenditure, transition costs, provider compensation, and government administration.

Both the proposed benefits and the projected costs require examination.

The question is not merely whether healthcare should be accessible. It is whether the proposed financing and administrative arrangements can make that access reliable and sustainable.

Abolishing ICE: What Exactly Is Being Abolished?

Now consider the call to abolish ICE.

The United States has a responsibility to administer its immigration laws and protect people within its jurisdiction.

It also has a responsibility to ensure that enforcement agencies operate lawfully, respect due process, and remain accountable for misconduct.

Those obligations are not mutually exclusive.

An immigration enforcement agency can have legitimate responsibilities while also facing serious allegations of misconduct.

Acknowledging one does not require dismissing the other.

In January 2026, Representative Shri Thanedar introduced H.R. 7123, the Abolish ICE Act.

The legislation proposes ending the agency within 90 days of enactment, restricting funding for its functions, and transferring its assets and liabilities to the Secretary of Homeland Security.

Its findings contain serious allegations concerning ICE operations, detention practices, and enforcement conduct.

Those allegations deserve appropriate investigation and scrutiny. But the proposed abolition also raises questions about what happens to the agency's existing functions.

Who executes lawful removal orders?

Who investigates cross-border criminal networks and human trafficking?

Who assumes responsibility for ongoing investigations?

What happens to people already in immigration detention?

What happens to the agency's personnel, records, facilities, and contractual obligations?

What protections would govern any replacement enforcement structure?

And what prevents the same problems from reappearing under a different agency name?

These are not questions that belong exclusively to Republicans.

They are questions of public administration, legal responsibility, and institutional accountability.

ICE is not the entirety of America's immigration system. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, immigration courts, and other federal agencies have distinct responsibilities.

But the existence of those institutions does not automatically establish that they could absorb ICE's responsibilities without legislative changes, additional resources, or operational planning.

Abolishing an agency is one decision.

Determining how the government will continue performing necessary functions is another.

If an agency has become incapable of operating within appropriate legal and ethical boundaries, abolition may be proposed as a remedy.

If reform is proposed instead, its advocates must explain why reform would succeed.

Either approach requires evidence, safeguards, and an implementation plan.

Changing an institution's name or eliminating its organizational structure does not, by itself, resolve the problems that made change necessary.

Immigration Enforcement and the Rights of Individuals

Immigration discussions often become dominated by descriptions of violent criminals, traffickers, and other dangerous individuals.

Serious crimes require investigation and appropriate legal consequences.

But an immigration violation is not automatically a violent criminal offense.

An allegation is not a conviction.

And a person facing removal proceedings does not cease to possess legal rights.

A government must be capable of addressing genuine threats without treating every immigrant as a threat.

It must also be capable of protecting communities without placing enforcement personnel beyond accountability.

The questions are therefore broader than whether ICE should exist.

What kind of immigration enforcement system does the country require?

What powers should its officers possess?

What limitations should govern those powers?

What remedies should exist when authorities act unlawfully?

And what standards of evidence should determine whether a person is detained or removed?

These questions deserve detailed answers regardless of which political party controls Congress.

Governing People Who Did Not Vote for You

This is where the responsibility of representation becomes especially important.

A Republican constituent may strongly oppose Medicare for All.

That person is entitled to ask how the proposal would affect taxes, insurance coverage, medical treatment, and household finances.

A Democratic constituent may oppose current immigration enforcement practices.

That person is entitled to ask how the government will prevent wrongful detention, discrimination, and excessive use of force.

An independent voter may support universal healthcare while also supporting strong immigration enforcement.

That person should not have to choose a political identity before receiving a serious explanation of either policy.

The responsibility of elected officials is not to agree with every constituent.

It is to exercise public authority within constitutional limits, remain accountable, and engage seriously with the people their decisions affect.

There is an important difference between rejecting an argument after examining it and dismissing the person who raises it.

Political disagreement should not automatically become evidence of ignorance, malice, or disloyalty.

A policy should be capable of withstanding legitimate scrutiny even when that scrutiny comes from its strongest opponents.

And the same standard applies to Republicans.

When Republicans hold power, they are responsible for governing people who voted Democratic, independent, or otherwise.

They cannot reasonably demand that their opponents respect electoral outcomes while treating those opponents as irrelevant to public governance.

The obligation is reciprocal.

Representation Is Not a Reward for Political Loyalty

Public representation is not a reward distributed according to political loyalty.

Citizens do not acquire greater entitlement to public services because they voted for the winning party, nor do they lose their rights because they supported the opposition.

A vote is not a purchase order for government favors.

Government assistance should be determined by legitimate public needs, transparent eligibility criteria, and the law—not by partisan allegiance.

Someone who supported the losing party may qualify for housing assistance, medical care, or another public benefit.

Someone who supported the winning party may not qualify for the same assistance.

That difference is not necessarily evidence of unfairness.

The relevant question is whether the eligibility rules are legitimate, transparent, and applied consistently.

Public resources are not the personal property of elected officials or political parties.

They are resources entrusted to government for public purposes.

And beyond the distribution of immediate assistance, governments should be concerned with the conditions that enable people to exercise greater control over their own lives.

Access to education. Meaningful employment. Fair wages. Healthcare. Housing opportunities. Economic mobility.

The ability to earn, save, invest, purchase property, travel, and make decisions without depending on political connections or favors.

This does not mean public assistance is unnecessary.

People may require support because of disability, illness, unemployment, disasters, poverty, or other circumstances.

A responsible government can provide immediate assistance while also working to expand long-term opportunity.

These objectives need not compete.

But there is a meaningful distinction between public support administered as a right or legitimate benefit and assistance distributed as a reward for political allegiance.

The purpose of public policy should not be to make citizens dependent on political favor. It should be to establish conditions in which people can exercise meaningful choices about their lives.

And that principle brings us back to Medicare for All.

If healthcare becomes a universal public benefit, access must not depend on whether a patient voted Democratic, Republican, independent, or not at all.

The same principle must govern immigration enforcement, legal protections, and the administration of public services.

The state must not confuse political allegiance with entitlement to fair treatment.

Congress Is Not a Campaign Rally

Campaigning and governing require different forms of responsibility.

A campaign seeks support.

A legislature must evaluate proposals, negotiate competing interests, authorize expenditure, establish legal obligations, and oversee government performance.

A campaign slogan can be repeated in seconds.

Implementing a national healthcare program may require years of administrative preparation.

Abolishing an enforcement agency can be proposed in a sentence.

Reorganizing its functions may involve legislation, personnel transfers, court proceedings, budgets, investigations, and continuing legal obligations.

These complexities do not make reform impossible.

They make planning essential.

And congressional majorities do not eliminate the constitutional structure within which legislation must operate.

The House and Senate must act through their respective procedures. The president retains constitutional powers, including the veto. Courts may review legal disputes. Federal agencies must operate within statutory authority.

The newly elected Democratic majorities will therefore encounter institutional constraints as well as political opposition.

The challenge is not simply to announce what they want.

It is to determine what can be enacted, how it can be administered, and how the results will be measured.

Accountability Must Extend Beyond the Announcement

Every major policy proposal should be accompanied by a credible explanation of its intended outcomes and the mechanisms for achieving them.

For Medicare for All, that means explaining enrollment, financing, provider payments, transition arrangements, and access to care.

For ICE abolition, that means explaining which responsibilities will end, which will continue, who will assume them, and how lawful enforcement and individual rights will be protected.

And for both proposals, it means establishing accountability.

What happens if implementation costs exceed projections?

What happens if people lose access to essential services during a transition?

What happens if a replacement immigration agency repeats the abuses attributed to its predecessor?

Who investigates failures?

Who reports the findings?

Who has the authority to correct them?

And how will the public know whether the policy is achieving its stated objectives?

These questions should not be treated as inconvenient interruptions to political momentum.

They are part of the responsibility that comes with exercising public power.

The Country Does Not Belong to the Winning Party

The November elections changed the balance of power in Congress.

They did not eliminate the political diversity of the United States.

Millions of Americans will continue to disagree about immigration, healthcare, taxation, government authority, and the appropriate role of public institutions.

Some will welcome the new congressional majority.

Others will oppose its priorities.

Many will judge individual proposals rather than identify completely with either party.

Their lives will continue beyond the election results.

They will go to work, raise children, pay bills, seek medical care, travel, operate businesses, and make decisions about their futures.

For most people, government is not experienced primarily as a campaign speech.

It is experienced through the institutions, services, laws, and decisions that shape everyday life.

The success of governance therefore cannot be measured solely by electoral victories, legislative announcements, or political applause.

It must also be examined through implementation, accountability, constitutional protections, and the actual consequences of public policy.

A majority gives elected officials authority to pursue a legislative agenda.

It does not relieve them of the obligation to justify their decisions.

It does not make legitimate questions from political opponents irrelevant.

And it does not transform partisan loyalty into the measure of citizenship.

You won the election. Now show the country how you intend to govern.

Not only for those who voted for you.

Not only for those who agree with you.

But with an understanding that the power you now exercise belongs to a constitutional government whose responsibilities extend to everyone.

Rebuild Magazine | Where Consciousness Meets the Headline
                      —Kerina F. Murray

text:
Every Indian investor should move at least 50% stock portfolio abroad. I will give you 3 good reasons why:- 

1) Diversification is the basic rule of investing. This is not about being bullish/bearish on the Indian market. 

Anything can happen to any market, including India. 

So being diversified especially in volatile times is basic common sense. 

2) Risk-reward:

Unless Indian market structurally gives 5% more USD terms compared to other markets, there is no sensible reward you're getting for taking higher units of risk. 

India= still an emerging market= higher risk. 

3) Succession planning:

If you truly believe that you will get richer. And, will sit on a huge portfolio, you need to starting thinking 20 years from now. 

In 20 years, you will be rich with let's say 10Cr. 
All that money stuck in India. 

You decide you want to move abroad. 
And, you plan to pull this wealth out. 

Yeah, good luck. 
You will have insanely hard time pulling this money out. 

It is better you start building a portfolio outside today. 
Saving in Euros, USD gives you (& your kids) more options. 

It is always 10X easier to move money from outside India (to India). Than from India to outside India. 

You will only realize this once your portfolio grows big.

🇹🇷 Korku endeksi VIX'in 22,31'e gerilemesi, piyasanın uzun süredir beklenen rahatlama sinyalini verdiğinin en somut göstergesi oldu. S&P 500 yüzde 2,35, Nasdaq ise yüzde 2,74 yükselişle güçlü bir seans kapattı. Asya cephesinde KOSPI yüzde 4,53 ile öne çıkarken Nikkei yüzde 2,80 kazanım sağladı; BIST de yüzde 2 artışla bu küresel tabloya dahil oldu. Dikkat çekici olan, yükselişin tek bir bölgeyle sınırlı kalmaması; rallinin koordineli ve geniş tabanlı bir görünüm sergilemesiydi. ABD hisse senedi fonlarına para girişinin sürdüğü veriler de bu tabloyu destekler nitelikte. Teknoloji tarafında ise farklı bir hava esti: Goldman Sachs verilerine göre hedge fonlar geçen hafta teknoloji hisselerini belirgin biçimde sattı. Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkında yönetim kurulu bağımsız soruşturma başlattı; bu gelişme hisseyi baskı altına aldı. Yapay zeka şirketi Anthropic'in halka arz yol gösterisinin bu hafta başlaması da piyasanın yakından takip ettiği konular arasında. Makro tarafta ise gözler bugün açıklanacak Ekim ayı enflasyon verisinde; "inatçı" bileşenlerin ne söyleyeceği, kısa vadeli beklentiler açısından belirleyici olabilir. Sektör döngüsünde teknolojiden savunmacı alanlara kısmi rotasyon işaretleri görülürken genel risk iştahı toparlanma eğilimini koruyor. Bugünkü enflasyon verisi ve Anthropic gelişmeleri, haftanın geri kalanında piyasaların gündemini şekillendirecek kritik iki başlık olarak öne çıkıyor.

The S&P 500 gained 2.35% and the Nasdaq climbed 2.74%, closing out a notably strong session on Wall Street. In Asia, the KOSPI led with a 4.53% advance while the Nikkei added 2.80%; Turkey's BIST also joined the broader move with a 2% gain. What made this rally particularly noteworthy was its coordinated, multi-regional character rather than a move confined to a single market. Continued inflows into U.S. equity funds provided further confirmation of improving risk appetite. On the technology front, however, the picture was more nuanced: Goldman Sachs data showed hedge funds were selling tech stocks at a brisk pace last week. Nvidia came under additional pressure after its board announced an independent investigation concerning CEO Jensen Huang. Meanwhile, AI company Anthropic is set to begin its IPO roadshow this week, adding another layer of interest to the tech narrative. The most closely watched macro event today is the release of October's inflation data, with particular attention on whether the "sticky" components show any sign of easing. Partial rotation signals from technology toward more defensive sectors were visible, even as the broader recovery trend remained intact. October CPI and the Anthropic roadshow developments look set to define the market's agenda for the remainder of the week.

text:
Mountain Outdoor Sports Exchange Symposium Explores New Paths for Industry Integration

The Mountain Outdoor Sports Exchange Symposium was held in Xingyi City, Guizhou Province on November 8, under the theme of “Upgrading Mountain Outdoor Sports and Fostering Sports–Tourism Integration”.

Some local practices offered valuable experiences into the development of mountain outdoor sports. In Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, events such as the Wanfenglin Marathon and the International Bridge Skydiving Invitational have grown into distinctive brands, helping the local tourism sector expand into diverse offerings including event management, educational experiences, and wellness-oriented long-stay travel.

International experiences have also offered new perspectives for the industry's development. Zurich University of Applied Sciences proposed developing a four-season economy, strengthening coordinated planning and putting environmental protection first. The Nepal Mountaineering Association recommended enhancing China–Nepal guide exchanges and conducting joint rescue training and route assessments. In the U.S. state of Utah, the national park entrance fee revenue is reinvested in local communities.

During the round-table discussions, the participants exchanged views on issues including the safety responsibilities, professional talent cultivation, the orderly opening of outdoor resources and the cultivation of event IPs.
