Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting [47, 48, 3, 26, 22, 49]. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb [24, 41], layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically [39, 9, 44]. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g-wave altermagnet CoNb4Se8, obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H-NbSe2. We resolve the spin-split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal Γ–K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near T0≈50 K to 60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.*** These authors contributed equally.Altermagnetism, recognized as the third elementary type in the classification of non-relativistic spin-group symmetries, is defined by the coexistence of zero-net magnetization and the lifting of Kramers degeneracies, which lead to distinctive transport phenomena [29, 31, 48, 40]. These degeneracies are shaped by opposite spin sublattices, interconnected through rotational symmetry in real space [47, 55, 24]. Distinct from both ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, this newly identified phase has sparked considerable interest, presenting new challenges for the development of spin-based technologies with potentially groundbreaking properties. The absence of net magnetization offers an advantage over conventional ferromagnetic technologies by mitigating stray magnetic fields. Simultaneously, the lifting of spin degeneracies, coupled with momentum-dependent spin-locking, facilitates efficient spin-filtering. Moreover, contrary to traditional collinear antiferromagnets, altermagnets intrinsically break time-reversal symmetry, giving rise to phenomena such as the anomalous Hall effect, highlighting their potential for novel electronic applications [12, 46, 14, 18].This rapidly evolving field presents compelling opportunities to extend this phenomenology to two dimensional (2D) material systems [56, 30]. 2D and thin-film altermagnets, along with their layered analogues, are particularly intriguing, envisioned as altermagnetic counterparts to graphene and graphite. [39]. While significant progress has been made, the high symmetry of most 2D antiferromagnets prevents the stabilization of the altermagnetic phase [2, 4, 25] and scalable layer-by-layer synthesis methods remain scarce [58], highlighting the need for innovative approaches. Building on the prediction of altermagnetism through site-ordered cobalt intercalation of the superconducting polymorph 2H-NbSe2 [39], we employ a combined theoretical and experimental approach to demonstrate its altermagnetic band splitting and spin texture.The altermagnetic ground state of CoNb4Se8 was predicted, and its A-type order determined by neutron diffraction, by Regmi et al. [39]. Dale et al. reported spin-resolved photoemission evidence for nonrelativistic spin splitting, which they distinguish from a relativistic splitting near K by its nodal structure and temperature dependence [9], and Sakhya et al. spin-integrated spectra consistent with it [44]. In both works, however, the spin-split branches are not resolved separately in the spectra and are identified through the comparison with DFT, so that the spin signal cannot be assigned to specific bulk bands from the data alone. Here we resolve the two branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw spin-integrated data (Fig. 2c–g), measure their spin polarization at these experimentally identified momenta, show that it is finite and reversing along Γ–M, where any relativistic σz is forbidden by symmetry, and compatible with zero along the nodal Γ–K direction, where it vanishes in the bulk, and show its reversal between two regions of the sample, consistent with time-reversal domains. Finally, we report a weak low-temperature anomaly near T0≈50 K to 60 K, observed in magnetometry, in temperature-dependent micro-ARPES as a renormalization of the bandwidth, and in ultrafast reflectivity as a sign change of Δ​R/R. Its microscopic origin remains open.📷Figure 1:Surface-dependent crystalline and electronic structure. a. Schematic of CoNb4Se8 formed by 2H-NbSe2 planes linked by Co atoms in a 2×2 reconstruction. b. LEED data (25 eV, ∼120 K) showing the 2×2 reconstruction: the orange circles indicate the 2×2 features, while the blue circles are the primitive ones. c–d. Schematics showing the possible surface terminations (Se and Co) after cleaving. e. Se-termination (characterized by triangular tiling) and f. Co-termination, measured by STM, and their corresponding Fourier transforms. g. micro-ARPES spatial map acquired by measuring the Se 3d and Co 3p core levels; yellow corresponds to Co-terminated regions. h. Core levels acquired from the two different surface terminations (curve colors matching the circle colors in g); the highlighted spectral features are attributed to surface replicas for the Co-termination. i–j. Corresponding Fermi surfaces and (E, k) dispersions, collected at 25 K with p-polarized photons at 47.5 eV (black indicates high intensity in the ARPES scale).
Single crystals of CoNb4Se8 were synthesized using the chemical vapour transport (CVT) method; all the data presented in the following have been acquired on samples from a single growth batch. Their composition and phases were monitored by X-ray diffraction (XRD), magnetic susceptibility, specific heat capacity, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements (Supporting Information Figs. S1–S4 [1]). The crystal structure depicted in Fig. 1a reveals Co-intercalated NbSe2 planes, which doubles the unit cell of the system, giving a 2×2 modulation. Such a 2×2 modulation is clearly visible at room temperature, as confirmed by XRD data (Supporting Information Fig. S1), and persists in the altermagnetic phase, as revealed by low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) (Fig. 1b, and Supporting Information Fig. S1). This confirms that the unit cell doubling is an inherent feature of the crystallographic structure. Both our bulk (XRD) and surface (LEED) diffraction probes show exclusively the 2×2 superstructure on top of the primitive 1×1 NbSe2 pattern, with no detectable 3×3​R​30∘ reflections, i.e., the structural fingerprint of a CoNb3Se6-type sublattice [28, 27, 36, 52]. Any Co1/3-type ordered intergrowth must therefore lie below the detection limit of these probes and be structurally disordered. We can therefore rule it out as the origin of the sharp dispersive features observed throughout our (micro-)ARPES dataset, which instead arise unambiguously from a well-ordered 2×2 phase consistent with stoichiometric CoNb4Se8. Spectroscopic measurements further reveal 2×2 backfolded electronic features, whose intensity diminishes progressively from 150 K and vanishes at higher temperatures (Supporting Information Figs. S8-S9). This temperature dependence may originate from surface-related effects or, more trivially, from thermal broadening reducing the spectral resolution. Nevertheless, these changes do not affect the central conclusions of this study, which are drawn from bulk-sensitive observations.Similar to other intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) [11], CoNb4Se8 cleaves to reveal two distinct surface terminations, each displaying markedly different electronic properties. Figs. 1c–1d present schematics of these two terminations, which were experimentally distinguished using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The Se-terminated surface, which appears to be the cleanest, exhibits the characteristic triangular tiling of the 2H-NbSe2 polymorph (Fig. 1e). In contrast, the Co-terminated surface is typically more disordered yet remains clearly distinguishable from the Se-terminated surface (Fig. 1f). Additional STM data are provided in Supporting Information Fig. S3.We used angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with few-micron spatial resolution (micro-ARPES) to validate these observations. Fermi surfaces for each surface termination were acquired by mapping the surface composition through Se 3d and Co 3p core level measurements (Fig. 1g). Spatially resolved maps indicate that each homogeneously terminated region spans approximately 20 µ​m laterally. According to our data in Fig. 1h, the Se-termination (blue curve) exhibits surface replicas of the 3d core levels, whereas Co-terminated regions (red curve) show distinct spectral features, including an additional peak at lower energies possibly formed by a different coordination of Co-Se atoms. It is important to note that the cleaving process can introduce random surface vacancies, which are readily identifiable in the core level spectra and may locally degrade the ARPES signal. In any case, the altermagnetic phenomena discussed here are of bulk origin and remain unaffected by either surface terminations or surface disorder.The Fermi surface maps, along with the energy and momentum (E, k) dispersions along the Γ−M direction (Figs. 1i–1j; black indicates the presence of electrons), reveal a complex and rich electronic structure. For both terminations, the intensity displays a pronounced threefold symmetry, accompanied by multiple petals and back-folded features. As shown in Supporting Information Fig. S8, such a modulation is evidenced by the replication of Γ-point features at the M-point. The Co-termination is overall the most prevalent and dominates high-resolution ARPES measurements with larger light spot sizes, as seen in the Supporting Information Figs. S6-S12. In any case, our study reveals a bulk phenomenology, thus terminations do not affect the results we present. For simplicity, we accordingly restrict our analysis to data obtained from this termination and we move to the characterization of the magnetic phase.📷Figure 2:Fermiology, DFT, and spin splitting. Fermi surfaces at bulk Γ (51 eV, a.), A (75 eV, b.), and an intermediate point near kz=π/2​c (55 eV, c.). d. Zoom-in on the splitting, with and without DFT calculations. The arrows indicate sections were the bands are prominently separated. e. Top: (E, k)-spectra at 44 eV (nominal kz near A; see Supporting Information, Section VIII), where matrix elements favor the split branches (see Supporting Information for additional energies), using p- (LH, left) and s-polarized (LV, right) light. Bottom: same (E, k)-spectra with overlaid DFT calculations. f. DFT spin-polarized 2D Fermi surfaces of CoNb4Se8 at kz=0 , kz=π/c, and kz=π/2​c. g. MDCs at the Fermi level from e., highlighting multiple split bands. h. DFT spin-polarized bands of CoNb4Se8 unfolded in the large Brillouin zone of (1×1) NbSe2 along M−Γ−M for kz=0, kz=π/c, and kz=π/2​c, with spectral weight PK→​m defined in Eq. 2. i. spin-ARPES at opposite k-points (55 eV p-polarized, as in c.), showing EDCs at ks​1 and MDCs at the Fermi level (insets).
CoNb4Se8 crystallizes in the centrosymmetric space group P63/mmc, No. 194. The A-type collinear antiferromagnetic order along c reduces the magnetic space group to P6′3/m′m′c, and the corresponding non-relativistic spin space group is generated by combining the crystallographic operations of 6/mmm with the spin operations that relate the two opposite-spin Co sublattices, in agreement with the spin-group assignments of Refs. [47, 48, 43] for this class of compounds, and with the symmetry analyses recently reported on the same compound [28, 9]. Operations that preserve the Co sublattices (the threefold rotations, inversion, the mirrors perpendicular to ⟨100⟩ and the twofold axes along ⟨100⟩) are combined with the identity in spin space, whereas those that exchange them (the {6001|00⁤12} screw, the mirror {m001|00⁤12}, the c glides perpendicular to ⟨1​1¯​0⟩ and the twofold axes along ⟨1​1¯​0⟩) are combined with a spin flip. In Litvin notation the spin space group is P-163/-1m 1m -1c ∞m1, the same as for the NiAs-type altermagnets MnTe and CrSb [47, 24, 41]; the full analysis is given in Supporting Information, Section VI and Table S3 [8, 54, 20]. From the general classification of space groups and their associated allowed altermagnetic spin-splittings [43], it follows that the lowest-order non-relativistic spin-split form factor compatible with the spin group of 2×2 reconstructed CoNb4Se8 is the g-wave harmonicΔs​(𝐤)∝kz​ky​(3​kx2−ky2),(1)whose nodal manifold consists of the two high-symmetry planes kz=0 and kz=π/c together with the three vertical mirror planes containing the Γ–K high-symmetry lines. The splitting therefore vanishes in the kz=0 and kz=π/c planes (as required by the antiferromagnetic Kramers degeneracy at those planes) and along the directions where the angular factor ky​(3​kx2−ky2) is zero, while it reaches its maximum at intermediate kz (such as kz=π/2​c) and at general k-points off the high-symmetry directions. The role of kz is thus pivotal: the breakdown of Kramers degeneracy manifests in the electronic structure away from bulk high-symmetry points. Photon-energy-dependent measurements are therefore required to select kz, and fine photon-energy steps are used to tune the photoemission matrix elements and to select favorable kz windows. The large c-axis lattice constant of CoNb4Se8 (see Supporting Information Fig. S1 and discussion) means each photon energy probes multiple kz values simultaneously, leading to partial spectral broadening [33]. Nevertheless, varying photon energy enables modulation of matrix elements and band intensities, which significantly enhances the detection of subtle spectral features. This capability is exemplified in the Fermi surface maps obtained at different photon energies, in Fig. 2a–c (see also Supporting Information Figs. S10–S12, where photon energy measurements with fine step are reported). Owing to the large c axis, each photon energy integrates over a kz window (Δ​kz≈0.2 Å) comparable to the Γ–A distance (π/c≈0.25 Å); the maps in Fig. 2a–c are centred near bulk Γ, near A and at an intermediate kz, respectively. The nodal structure is therefore identified through spin-resolved observables that are independent of kz (the null along Γ–K) or protected by symmetry against kz broadening (the reversal at opposite momenta; Supporting Information, Section VIII).While all Fermi surfaces share common features, i.e., hexagonal flower-like central contours and elongated ‘spindles’, the map in Fig. 2c reveals a clear splitting in the electronic band structure, which complement and refine the picture emerging from prior ARPES work on the same compound [9, 44]. In particular, the altermagnetic splitting is directly visible in our raw spin-integrated photoemission data, as resolved contours in the Fermi-surface maps at intermediate kz (Fig. 2c, also highlighted by arrows in Fig. 2d), and as two distinct peaks in the corresponding momentum distribution curves (MDCs) at the Fermi level (Fig. 2g). The combination of micro-ARPES with a ∼4 µ​m beam spot, fine photon-energy mapping in the range from 25 eV to 75 eV, and systematic light-polarisation control further allows us to address individual single-termination regions, select favorable kz windows in which the g-wave splitting is symmetry-allowed, and tune the photoemission matrix elements so that the otherwise nearly degenerate branches become unambiguously visible.We note that in the Fermi surfaces, some of the spectral features appear as filled patches of intensity rather than contours as expected from density functional theory (DFT) calculations. This is attributable to photoemission matrix elements, which strongly vary with both geometry and photon energy. For the same reason, matrix element effects cause the splitting to be more or less evident at nominally the same kz=π/2​c, but different photon energies.The experimental Fermi surfaces align with DFT (Fig. 2f and Fig. S13) in capturing the fermiology across the kz planes. The spin-splitting of the Kramers-paired bands at multiple momenta show remarkable agreement. This agreement is further highlighted in Fig. 2d, where the spin-up (red) and spin-down (blue) bands from the DFT calculations coincide exactly with the experimental data. There is a similarly strong match between the DFT calculated (E, k) distributions across different kz values and acquired micro-ARPES data, as shown in Fig. 2h, where blue and orange curves correspond to Γ and A points, respectively (see also Supporting Information Fig. S14 for DFT-calculated (E, k) spectra in the Γ–K direction). In order to display a simpler representation of the electronic dispersion for comparison with micro-ARPES measurements, we have mapped the spin-polarized electronic eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the bulk altermagnetic 2×2 CoNb4Se8 supercell (SC) into the bigger Brillouin zone of the 1×1 NbSe2 primitive cell (PC) via an unfolding scheme [38]. The thickness of the bands in the unfolded electronic dispersions is proportional to the spectral weight:PK→​m​(k→i)=∑n|⟨K→​m|k→i​n⟩|2,(2)which is the probability of finding a set of PC states, |k→i​n⟩, contributing to the SC state, |K→​m⟩ [38], where m and n are band indices and i runs over the number of K→ vectors.Notably, while eigenvalues for kz=0 and kz=π/c are spin-degenerate (as expected for an antiferromagnetic system), DFT results for kz=π/2​c (rightmost panel in Fig. 2h, where the red/blue colors are used to highlight spin-up/down bands) provide a precise benchmark for finding where Kramers degeneracies are lifted, identifying CoNb4Se8 as a g-wave altermagnet and enabling a one-to-one correspondence with the experimental data. text:
Time, and the inevitable imperatives of time and timing, spare no man.

Joey Archer wins a 10-round unanimous decision at the Pittsburgh Civic Arena to raise his record to 45-1, in Sugar Ray Robinson's 199th and final (174-19-6) fight, on November 10, 1965.

From Martin Kane writing in the November 22, 1965 issue of Sports Illustrated:

The plan had been for Sugar Ray Robinson to work up through the ranks once more and thus earn his way into what would have been his 16th middleweight championship fight. Only Sugar Ray, and perhaps some of his idolatrous entourage, believed in the plan. He had won that 160-pound championship five times, more than any other man, and the welterweight title once, and he thought that at the age of 45 he could do it again. He must have believed it or else he would not have fought nine times last year and 13 this year, losing to nonentities in the Altoonas of boxing and winning against unknowns, taking his lumps on each occasion for a $1,000 purse here, $2,000 there. A great mystery was made of why he bothered with the travail of training, put up with the one-night stands in tank towns or endured those inglorious lickings he took from fighters who will never fight in Madison Square Garden, Yankee Stadium or Las Vegas.
He did not need the money. The Internal Revenue Service recently turned over to him $344,000 it had withheld, against taxes, since 1957. Robinson owns property in Cleveland and Chicago, having sold his Harlem holdings. He has contracts to make two movies, one a Western, the other a war picture. He is well-fixed financially. In the end, you had to believe that he was striving honestly for a title fight.
He came surprisingly close to getting it. Last week Joey Archer, a fine boxer with but a modest punch, stood between Sugar Ray and an opportunity to meet the middleweight champion, Dick Tiger. If he were to defeat Archer, the No. 1 contender in most ratings—and one good left hook would do it—Sugar Ray would all but surely have earned a sixth chance at the middleweight crown despite his 45 years. So, on a Wednesday night in Pittsburgh, he faced the blue-eyed, broken-nosed Archer before a crowd of 9,023, many of them oldtimers who fondly remembered Robinson in his glory days, and among them a sprinkling of younger men who wanted to see what the legend was about.
Robinson weighed 160 pounds, Archer a pound less. Under the lights of the television cameras at the weigh-in ceremony the tiny, well-healed scars at the outer corner of each of Sugar's eyes could be seen. But there were no other marks to show for his 25 years of prizefighting and 198 bouts. Outwardly his body was as sleek as ever and his waist as trim. What remained inside would be seen that night.
Archer is a superior boxer. He has a classic jab, some effective feints and good footwork. He has lost only once in 47 fights. He has been knocked down but once, too, in one of his early matches, and then only his knee touched the canvas.
As soon as the fight started it became clear that both men intended to follow the same plan—but for quite different reasons. Robinson came out intent on winning early, presumably because he has learned that his aging legs no longer serve him well in the late rounds. Archer's strategy was much the same, for he wanted to press Robinson at all times, and thus drain Sugar Ray of whatever stamina he had as quickly and thoroughly as possible.
With both men charging at each other, it started as an interesting fight and it remained one, even though there was little doubt about the result after the first few rounds. What had happened to Robinson's timing showed with the first hook he threw. It was a long, powerful swing, delivered from far back, precisely the hook with which he knocked out Gene Fullmer in the 1957 title fight, except that it missed Archer's chin by five inches. A minute or so later Robinson tried the hook again and missed again. Archer jabbed and faded out of range, jabbed and faded repeatedly, once scoring prettily with a combination to body and head.
The Robinson strategy still was operative in the second round, and this time it worked a bit better. He started out with a left and right to Archer's body. Joey is one who fights back, and he drove Robinson almost to the ropes with a flurry of head punches. His older brother, Jimmy, who manages and trains him, saw that Archer's temper was showing and shouted at him from the corner. "Loose, Joey," he commanded. "Stick! Stick! Loosen up, Joey!" The moment of danger passed. Joey went back to his jab, and Sugar missed with a right and left. Those misses opened the way for Archer to land eight quick punches to the head, but all were too high to be damaging.
Now it was the third round, and Robinson still was trying for the big punch. He had one hook blocked, he landed a right to the body, and then, with a single brilliant flash of his old talents, caught Archer with a very good hook, closed with him and, as they stood toe to toe, scored with a flurry.
But that was the end. Early in the fourth, after Archer had hooked him twice and landed some light jabs, Sugar missed with a big right hand. A look of concern came over his face. Archer was jabbing and moving, and Robinson was missing with rights and lefts. Then, suddenly, Archer landed a left to the head and followed it immediately with a long right. Sugar Ray went down on the seat of his white silk trunks, rolled to his side and, dazed, took a nine-count resting on one knee. Now Sugar and everyone knew that his fight plan had failed, and so had his grand plan. The last time the light-hitting Archer had knocked a man down was in 1960.
The rest of the fight was nothing but the last steps down for a gallant Robinson. He all but hit the canvas again in the sixth and once again in the seventh, looked better in the eighth and slugged it out with Archer in the ninth. In the last minute of the 10th round men at ringside were standing and pleading, "Don't hit him again, Joey! That's enough!" As the fighters awaited the decision after the final bell tears welled into Robinson's bloodshot eyes. There was a tiny cut, a mere scratch, on his right cheekbone. His nose was ruddy from all those jabs. He was breathing heavily. His legs were leaden. He knew.
It had been a long and glorious trail for Sugar Ray Robinson, who just may have been the best fighter ever. His skills were exquisite, his punch superb, his courage unsurpassed. But, as he had just learned, there always comes a day when only the courage remains.
The soft-spoken Archer held court in his dressing room.
"He's a tough guy," Archer said. "He is one of the cagiest old guys in boxing. He feints—most fighters today can't do that. He is the greatest fighter I ever saw among the middleweights."
And in a nearby room, the bleary-eyed Robinson was refusing to concede that he had fought his last.
"I want to get a night's sleep before I make up my mind," he said.
Next afternoon at the airport, waiting for a plane to take him back to New York, Sugar Ray smiled wanly, hunched his black leather, hip-length coat about his shoulders and said that retirement was the only course open to him now.
"But we have this offer of a return bout with Archer," one of his followers protested.
"Aw, what would be the point?" Robinson said.

text:
Hollywood superstar Angelina Jolie has arrived in Manila for the 2026 ASEAN Inclusive Growth Summit on November 11. Beyond her speaking engagement, the capital offers experiences worthy of her sophisticated taste.

From world-class pearls and Filipino designer bags to heritage restaurants, here are five activities she should squeeze into her itinerary.

1. PEARL HUNTING AT GREENHILLS

Jolie could follow the footsteps of Martha Stewart, Rihanna, and Queen Sofía of Spain, who have been reported among Greenhills’ famous pearl shoppers.

The Philippines produces some of the world’s most prized South Sea pearls, particularly golden varieties celebrated for their exceptional size and luster.

Greenhills in San Juan offers everything from classic pearl strands to elaborate jewelry, making it a destination for luxury shoppers seeking beautiful pieces beyond international boutiques.

2. FILIPINO FOOD TRIP AT MILKY WAY OR CAFE JUANITA

For authentic Filipino cuisine, Jolie has two excellent choices.

Milky Way traces its beginnings to a dairy bar established in Manila in the early 1950s. Its present Makati café, opened in 2002 by Chef J. Gamboa, is celebrated for its award-winning kare-kare, crispy hito, baby crispy pata, and homemade ice cream.

Cafe Juanita in Pasig, meanwhile, was founded by physician Dr. Efren Vazquez and named after his mother. Its antique-filled interiors complement Filipino favorites such as two-way pork adobo, crispy pork binagoongan, and catfish mango salad.

3. HALO-HALO INDULGENCE AT BEBANG’S

Jolie should discover how a young Filipino brand reinvented one of the country’s most beloved desserts.

Founded in 2021 by Daymae Salumbides and Sam Karazi, Bebang’s Halo-Halo gained a following for replacing ordinary shaved ice with finely shaved frozen milk.

Its indulgent Presidential Halo-Halo has become a signature offering, while its Royal variant even features edible gold.

4. DESIGN DISCOVERY AT KENNETH COBONPUE

Interestingly, Jolie already has a connection to internationally acclaimed Cebuano furniture designer Kenneth Cobonpue.

In 2006, reports revealed that Brad Pitt purchased Cobonpue furniture, including a bed for their child.

Celebrated by TIME magazine for his mastery of rattan, Cobonpue has won international design awards and created iconic pieces including the Bloom and Yoda chairs.

His creations have appeared in prestigious international spaces, proving that Filipino furniture design belongs on the world stage.

5. DESIGNER BAG SHOPPING AT ARANAZ

For elegant Filipino-made accessories, Jolie should visit Aranaz, the luxury handbag label established in the late 1990s by Becky Aranaz and her daughters, Amina and Rosanna.

Under creative director Amina Aranaz-Alunan, the brand has transformed traditional Filipino craftsmanship into internationally recognized fashion.

Its handcrafted bags and clutches incorporate materials such as raffia and abaca, combining indigenous techniques with contemporary luxury.

For Jolie, these experiences offer something beyond conventional shopping and sightseeing: an opportunity to discover the extraordinary creativity, heritage, and craftsmanship of the Filipino people.

(✍️:Top Dagohoy)

[Shindonga] 261110 Behind the Steady Sellers of Korea’s Four Leading Ramen Brands
For Koreans, ramen is much more than a simple meal substitute. During times of hardship, it was a warm source of comfort that helped fill empty stomachs. It has long been synonymous with late-night snacks, and at times serves as a side dish for drinks, a hangover remedy, or a satisfying meal for busy modern-day consumers. These long-standing ramen brands have shared in the joys and sorrows of generations of Koreans. Behind their creation lie stories of difficult times, ingenious ideas, and dramatic turnarounds that captivated the world.
🍜[OTOKI] Jin Ramen: A Perfect Balance of Rich Broth and Fiery Spice
Winning Over Consumers with an Consumer-friendly pricing
OTOKI’s Jin Ramen, launched in 1988 ahead of the opening of the Seoul Olympics, is one of Korea’s representative ramen brands and celebrates its 38th anniversary this year. Made with a rich broth based on beef bone and brisket stock, it offers a deep, savory flavor. With the original Mild and Spicy varieties, followed by the Slightly Spicy version launched in 2025, the brand has built a diverse fan base.
As of August 2026, cumulative sales had surpassed approximately 8.8 billion packs, and Jin Ramen has firmly maintained its position as Korea’s second-best-selling ramen since 2012.
Jin Ramen, the affordable product that helped earn OTOKI its reputation as “God-TOKI.”
Jin Ramen, the brand that helped establish OTOKI’s reputation as “God-TOKI,” is particularly known for its affordable pricing. By maintaining a low and reasonable price for more than a decade, it has become synonymous with affordable, good-value ramen.
The brand has also enhanced its taste and quality by incorporating Haneulcho peppers for a clean, crisp spiciness, increasing the amount of brisket ingredients, and adding more than 10% to the quantity of toppings. Other notable features include chewy noodles that do not become soggy and a consumer-friendly adjustment to the recommended water quantity, reduced from 550 ml to 500 ml.
These strengths have helped the brand expand into various product lines, including Jin Bibim Men, while inspiring creative consumer recipes such as Jin Ramen Fried Rice.
In global markets, OTOKI has emphasized the English brand name “Jin” and pursued collaborations with BTS Jin, alongside overseas marketing initiatives, helping raise the profile of K-ramen around the world.

text:
What Makes Mysteries Relaxing? The Cozy Answer
#fiction  #dogs #cozymystery
 A mystery begins with something out of place: a missing heirloom, a suspicious footprint, a neighbor who is being awfully cagey. That may not sound restful at first. Yet anyone who has settled into a favorite chair with a cup of tea and a whodunit knows the feeling. **What makes mysteries relaxing** is not the crime itself. It is the promise that, page by page, a confusing situation can be understood.

For cozy mystery readers especially, the pleasure is wonderfully specific. We get a puzzling question, a welcoming place to spend time, companions worth rooting for, and the quiet confidence that justice will eventually have its say. The story may include a dash of danger, but it does not leave us stranded in it.

## What Makes Mysteries Relaxing for So Many Readers?

Mysteries turn uncertainty into a game with rules. In ordinary life, problems can be messy, personal, and stubbornly unresolved. A mystery offers a smaller, more manageable version of disorder. There are clues. There are motives. There is a sequence of events that can be pieced together if the sleuth - and the reader - pays close enough attention.

That structure is calming. Even when a red herring sends us down the wrong path, we trust the story to bring us back around. The author has made a promise: what seems tangled will make sense in the end. For readers carrying a busy mind into the evening, that promise can feel like a deep, contented sigh.

Cozy mysteries add another layer of comfort. They tend to keep the focus on people, relationships, community, and clever detection rather than graphic violence or lingering fear. The stakes matter, but the reading experience remains gentle enough to enjoy before bed. It is suspense with a soft blanket nearby.

## A Familiar World Gives the Mind a Place to Rest

A beloved mystery series can feel like visiting a small town where somebody always knows the best place for pie and somebody else is likely to know a secret. Readers return for the puzzle, certainly, but they also return for the setting. A historic main street, a sunny porch, a local festival, a veterinary clinic, or a gossip-prone café can become as familiar as a favorite vacation spot.

Familiarity does not make a series boring. It gives the surprises somewhere safe to land. When readers know the town's rhythms and recognize the regular cast, they can relax into the story quickly. They do not have to learn a whole new universe before enjoying the plot. Instead, they get to notice what has changed: Why is that friendly shop owner suddenly evasive? What is Daisy sniffing around the garden gate? Which detail does not belong?

This is one reason recurring characters are such a treat. A good sleuth feels like a friend with an unusual talent for ending up near trouble. The reader knows her heart, her habits, and perhaps her weakness for asking one question too many. The side characters bring warmth, comic relief, and sometimes a little harmless exasperation. Even a cranky neighbor has a place at the table.

## Clues Offer a Pleasant Kind of Focus

Many relaxing activities give the brain something gentle to hold onto. Gardening asks us to notice the soil and the weather. Knitting asks us to follow a pattern. A cozy mystery asks us to notice a detail that may become important later.

That attention is active, but not draining. Readers can form theories without having to solve anything in the real world. Was the alibi too perfect? Did the missing brooch appear in the wrong room? Why did the dog bark at that particular visitor? These questions invite a satisfying kind of concentration, one that nudges everyday worries to the side for a while.

The best mysteries play fair with this invitation. The solution should feel surprising, but it should also feel earned. When the final pieces click together, readers enjoy the little spark of recognition: Of course. The clues were there all along.

There is no need to beat the detective to the answer, either. Some readers love making a list of suspects. Others are perfectly happy to follow the sleuth and admire her work. Both approaches bring the same pleasure of moving from question to answer.

## Gentle Suspense Feels Different From Stress

Not every mystery is relaxing, and that is part of its charm as a genre. A gritty thriller may be exactly right for a reader who wants a late-night jolt. A psychological mystery can be deliciously unsettling. But when life already feels noisy or heavy, many readers prefer suspense that stays within comfortable bounds.

Cozy mysteries usually provide that boundary. The mood may grow tense when the sleuth gets too close to the truth, but humor, friendship, and a strong sense of place keep the darkness from taking over. The danger serves the puzzle rather than becoming the whole experience.

Animal characters can make that balance especially appealing. A watchful dog, for instance, may notice an unfamiliar scent, a nervous gesture, or an oddly placed object before the humans do. Canine forensics add a modern, playful twist to detection while preserving the warm heart of a cozy tale. A warm snout and sharp nose can remind us that even when people are acting suspicious, there is still room for loyalty, affection, and the occasional well-timed treat.

In the Doc and Daisy Mysteries, that blend of smart sleuthing, Florida small-town life, and a dog's observant perspective gives readers clues to consider without losing the lighthearted companionship that makes a series feel like home.

## The Ending Provides Emotional Tidiness

A satisfying mystery ending does more than name the culprit. It restores a sense of order. Questions are answered. Misunderstandings are cleared up. A person who has been overlooked may finally be heard. The community can breathe again.

That does not mean every ending needs to be perfectly tidy. In fact, the most memorable cozies often leave room for real feelings. A motive may be sad. A friendship may need mending. The sleuth may learn something that changes how she sees a neighbor or herself. Still, the central disturbance has been faced, and the truth has been given its proper place.

That emotional resolution can be deeply soothing. Real life rarely hands us a final chapter with all the loose ends tied. Mysteries let us experience closure in a few happy hours, then carry a little of that calm back into our own unfinished days.

## Why a Cozy Mystery Can Be a Wonderful Reread

A relaxing book is often one a reader can revisit, and mysteries might seem like an odd choice once the answer is known. But knowing whodunit changes the pleasure rather than ending it. On a reread, the reader gets to admire the construction. The suspicious pause, the misplaced clue, and the innocent-sounding comment all look different.

Rereading also means returning to familiar company without the pressure of surprise. It is like walking a well-loved trail with a friend who still has good stories. The mystery remains, but the path feels welcoming.

A cozy mystery will not suit every mood. Sometimes a reader wants literary fiction, a grand adventure, or a book with no villain at all. But when the goal is a little suspense without a lingering shadow, mysteries offer a rare combination: they engage the mind, warm the heart, and leave the reader in a better place than where the story began.

So the next time the day feels overfull, choose a puzzling clue, a charming town, and a sleuth with good instincts. Let the suspects fuss, let the clues gather, and let the answer wait just a few pages ahead. There is comfort in knowing that, for one cozy evening at least, somebody will follow the trail all the way home.

text:
How Fleeting Moments With Strangers Combat Loneliness | Neuroscience News

Summary:

A sociological study published in Theory and Society explores the profound psychological value of fleeting, emotionally resonant encounters between strangers. Led by Professor Joseph Hermanowicz at the University of Georgia, the research coins the term “evanescent interactions” to describe brief, unexpected exchanges of empathy, such as a reassuring smile or a supportive phrase during a moment of distress.

Far from being mere superficial pleasantries, these micro-connections validate human presence, instill a sense of belonging, and act as a critical social buffer against widespread alienation, loneliness, and institutional attrition.

Key Facts:

- Defining Evanescent Interactions: These are brief, highly emotionally charged moments where strangers exchange subtle verbal or nonverbal gestures that create an immediate “spark” of mutual recognition, validation, and shared humanity.

- Beyond Superficial Politeness: Unlike routine small talk, evanescent interactions communicate core messages of social belonging: confirming personal worth, affirming visibility, and alleviating feelings of exclusion.

- Impact on Belonging and Retention: Previous research by Hermanowicz demonstrated that the presence or absence of these micro-connections influenced whether university students persisted in their studies or dropped out due to isolation.

---

Picture navigating a crowded grocery store or farmers market with a screaming toddler tucked under your arm. Exhausted, embarrassed, and leaving empty-handed, you brace yourself for critical stares and judgmental glances from passersby.

Instead, an older stranger catches your eye, offers a warm, knowing smile, and softly says: “We’ve all been there. You’re doing great, Mama.”

In a fraction of a second, humiliation gives way to relief. You feel seen, understood, and anchored.

While these brief encounters between strangers are common in daily life, their sociological weight and psychological power have largely gone unnamed, until now. In a study published in the journal Theory and Society, Dr. Joseph Hermanowicz, professor of sociology in the Franklin College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Georgia (UGA), defines and examines the phenomenon of “evanescent interactions.”

The Anatomy of a Fleeting Spark

Hermanowicz defines evanescent interactions as fleeting, highly emotionally charged exchanges in which strangers share gestures or words that generate an instant “spark” of mutual comprehension.

Crucially, these encounters transcend routine social politeness. While holding an elevator door or uttering a mechanical “good morning” maintains baseline social etiquette, an evanescent interaction carries an emotional charge that directly targets another person’s subjective state.

“What is communicated by these evanescent interactions is essentially, ‘You’ve noticed me. You’ve confirmed my existence. You’ve communicated that I am welcome here, that I belong here, that I have a place here, that I have value,’” explains Hermanowicz.

These micro-exchanges function as social mirrors, reassuring people navigating vulnerable, stressful, or solitary moments that their struggles are shared and their presence is legitimate.

“It’s important to be pleasant and kind to people, particularly in our present times, of course,” says Hermanowicz. “But I think it’s also important to recognize that when we do have a certain deliberateness with communicating with people, we could be accomplishing something very meaningful. We could communicate to people that they are important, that they matter, that we together form a community.”

An Antidote to Social Alienation and Dropout

The protective nature of these brief connections first emerged during Hermanowicz’s earlier investigations into higher education attrition. While analyzing why undergraduate students chose to drop out or persist in university life, he uncovered a recurrent social theme.

Former students who left university environments frequently cited feeling invisible, anonymous, and unmoored within large campus bureaucracies. Many noted that a single meaningful encounter with a faculty member, staff worker, or peer who demonstrated genuine, unprompted interest in their well-being might have provided the sense of belonging required to stay.

“In the absence of such contact, they felt alienated and not noticed, which fueled or did not impede a desire to leave,” Hermanowicz notes. “So they left.”

In modern societies facing widespread public health warnings regarding an epidemic of loneliness, these low-stakes, high-impact interactions represent an underappreciated source of emotional resilience. Because modern life increasingly funnels human engagement into digital feeds and automated interfaces, spontaneous physical-world acknowledgment has become scarce, amplifying the psychological benefit of face-to-face micro-empathy.

“A lot of people are lonely. These sparks of connection can thwart feelings of not belonging in the various groups and organizations that we are a part of, whether those are friendship groups, work organizations or society more broadly,” says Hermanowicz.

Sustaining the Social Fabric

Because evanescent interactions are fleeting by definition, society often treats them as negligible background noise. However, Hermanowicz argues that they serve as the glue maintaining trust and cohesion in diverse communities.

When two strangers acknowledge each other’s humanity, whether through a shared laugh on a delayed train, a compassionate comment to an overwhelmed parent, or a gentle nod during a stressful moment, they bridge societal divides without the demands of long-term commitment.

“Evanescent interactions are crucial to social life,” concludes Hermanowicz. “Two people communicating empathy to each other and recognizing each other as important holds extraordinary consequence. It affirms our mutual place in human community.”

text:
James Gunn out at DC Studios, the new boss’s grandma test, a $300 PS6 pitch and more | The Reef Daily 
https://t.co/cO7pMHSgHa

David Corenswet as Superman in James Gunn’s Superman. Image: Warner Bros. Pictures/DC Studios

James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as the heads of DC Studios on Dec. 1, and the newest Clownfish TV episode asks what went wrong. The other new episodes cover the Marvel veteran replacing them, a script that emails Sam Altman about your unused RAM and a former PlayStation boss who wants a $300 PS6. Below that, D/REZZED has the latest James Bond screen tests, plus a few Shorts and the newest podcast episodes.

New Clownfish TV episodes

Why is James Gunn leaving DC Studios?

Officially, he and Safran are stepping down. The Hollywood Reporter story the hosts read says the pair leave their leadership roles effective Dec. 1, and Skydance, which now oversees DC after buying Warner Bros., named former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham president and chief creative officer of DC Studios. Gunn still has the Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow in post-production for next year, and both men stay on as producers on a few projects, including The Batman Part II.

Kneon doesn’t buy the “stepping down” part, since Gunn’s contract ran into next year and he kept talking up future plans. He points to the box office, putting Supergirl’s losses near $200 million. The hosts agree Gunn is great at one kind of movie, the goofy ensemble with a rockabilly soundtrack, and one of them would rather see him make Doom Patrol than Superman. They do like Latcham’s resume, which runs from Iron Man to the first Guardians of the Galaxy.

Who is Jeremy Latcham, DC’s new boss?

He’s a longtime Marvel producer, and his faith is now the internet’s favorite topic. A post from TV writer Will Landman, which the hosts read, describes Latcham as a conservative Christian who runs a faith-based writers group. In a CBN News clip played on the show, Latcham says that while making the early Marvel movies, he kept asking whether his grandmother would like them, as a stand-in for regular families outside Hollywood.

Kneon says Superman of all characters should be safe to take grandma to, and he expects the meltdowns to be loud. The hosts also run through a Cosmic Book News rumor that Gunn was pushed out early because Man of Tomorrow needs fixing. That one is Cosmic Book News’ claim, and nothing official backs it up. For a smaller DC footnote, Safran told Collider last month that more My Adventures with Superman is still up in the air.

Can you really email Sam Altman about your unused RAM?

Yes, once a day. Dexerto reported that a developer posted a script called RAM Altman on GitHub. It checks a Linux computer’s memory every five minutes, and if more than 10% is free, it emails the OpenAI CEO a note about it, capped at one message a day. It comes with eight subject lines, 10 messages and six sign-offs. It’s a reply to Altman’s comment on the Cheeky Pint podcast that it’s “quite terrible” for so much of the world’s DRAM to sit in home computers, used maybe 5% of the time. Altman later said he wants people to have as much RAM as they want, and the developer asks people not to flood his inbox.

The hosts’ take: most home RAM is busy feeding Chrome anyway. One of them has run 128 GB in his workstations for years, and nobody in the house is giving up a single stick now.

Should the PS6 cost $300?

Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden thinks so. On The Trophy Room podcast, as reported by GamesRadar+, Layden said consoles already have enough power, and that the real innovation would be to “make another PS5 for $300.” D/REZZED has more on what Layden said.

Kneon agrees completely. He says graphics hit a ceiling a while ago, and most people can’t see the difference anymore. He worries the next consoles could land at $1,000 or more, which is PC money, and he’d rather see a smaller, cheaper box built on older tech, along the lines of ModRetro’s M64, which he says sells for about $230.

For paid members

American Journalism Got OUTSOURCED to India?! Kneon looks at the Associated Press cutting most of its American photographers and video editors and moving that work to India, according to the episode, and asks how a wire service covers U.S. news from overseas. It runs about 20 minutes. Watch it on https://t.co/d3rnqvGm2C.

Robert Pattinson. Image: Harald Krichel via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

The James Bond shortlist just got two famous names. Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult have screen-tested for 007, The Hollywood Reporter and Deadline reported. They join Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner, and Amazon MGM Studios hasn’t commented. Read the story on D/REZZED.

A homebrew exploit called CivSwitch uses physical Civilization VII cartridges to open up the Switch 2, and Kotaku says 2K has reportedly started a recall, though 2K hasn’t confirmed it.

While slavery was a universal institution in the Greco-Roman world, early Christian voices—such as Gregory of Nyssa in 379 AD—offered some of the earliest full critiques of owning human beings, and early medieval Church councils began restricting the enslavement of fellow Christians.

The Transatlantic Slave Trade: Beginning in the 15th century, Catholic and Protestant church structures frequently accommodated, justified, or directly participated in the global slave trade. Popes such as Nicholas V and Paul III issued bulls in the 1400s and 1500s authorizing or regulating the subjugation of non-Christian peoples, and religious orders like the Jesuits operated plantations. In the Protestant world, the Church of England and other denominations similarly profited from or defended colonial bondage.

Pro-Slavery Interpretations: Defenders of slavery cited Old Testament regulations on servitude and New Testament passages (such as Ephesians 6:5 or 1 Timothy 6:1–2) that instructed slaves to obey masters. They also used racialized doctrines, such as the Curse of Ham, to justify the chattel slavery of African people.

In the 1600s, many slaveowners resisted baptizing or converting enslaved people. A widespread English and European legal tradition held that Christians could not be held as slaves for life. Owners feared that if an enslaved person was baptized, they might claim a right to freedom

Missionaries and owners even circulated heavily edited texts—such as the truncated "Slave Bible"—that cut out stories of liberation, like Moses leading the Israelites out of Egypt, while keeping passages about servitude

While masters initially permitted or promoted supervised, white-led services to enforce submission, enslaved and free Black people eventually carved out their own independent interpretations of the faith. They formed early separate congregations and underground "invisible institution" praise meetings that blended Christian theology with African traditions, transforming the religion into a source of spiritual survival and resistance

text:
Yes, kings such as Ahaz and Manasseh, along with ordinary people, later sacrificed children in the Valley of Hinnom (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6; Jeremiah 7:31; 19:5; Ezekiel 16:20–21; Psalm 106:37–38). The prophets treat this as exactly the abomination God had judged the nations for and had forbidden Israel to copy. Jeremiah 7:31 and 19:5 are blunt: the people did “what I did not command, nor did it come into my mind.” 

Because Manasseh did this The Lord brought the commanders of the king of Assyria against him. They “captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon” (2 Chronicles 33:11). In his distress, he “humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,” prayed, and God “was moved by his entreaty and heard his plea; so He brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God” (vv. 12–13). 

Manasseh’s story is one of the clearest Old Testament illustrations of both God’s absolute sovereignty and His preference for mercy over sacrifice. 

This is precisely the pattern expressed in Hosea 6:6 (“I desire mercy, not sacrifice”) and Micah 6:6–8. God does not delight in the blood of bulls and goats, and He certainly does not delight in the blood of children. What He desires is a broken and contrite heart (Psalm 51:16–17). Manasseh had offered the worst kind of sacrifice and still received mercy when he turned. His later reforms—removing the idols and restoring the altar of the Lord—were the fruit of that mercy, not its cause.
The story therefore undercuts two common errors: the idea that extreme sin places someone beyond God’s reach, and the idea that God is satisfied by religious performance while remaining indifferent to repentance. Manasseh’s life shows a God who is free to judge, free to humble, and free to restore—and who consistently values genuine turning to Him above any sacrificial act.

text:
The Crown and the Censer: The Melchizedek Order, Jurisdictional Succession, and the Finished Priesthood of the Son
The institutional architecture of the Sinai Covenant rested upon an unyielding statutory separation of powers. Under Mosaic Law, civil and judicial sovereignty belonged to the governing scepter—ultimately anchored in the tribe of Judah (Genesis 49:10; 2 Samuel 7:12–16)—while sacred altar duties, sacrificial mediation, and access to the Holy Place were restricted exclusively to the consecrated sons of Aaron from the tribe of Levi (Numbers 3:10; Numbers 18:1–7).

This boundary was non-negotiable. To merge the crown and the censer under the Levitical code was an act of high treason against God's statutory order. When King Uzziah, empowered by military success, marched into the temple to burn incense upon the golden altar, eighty-one priests confronted him, declaring his encroachment illegitimate. Yahweh struck him with immediate leprosy on his forehead, stripping him of temple access and royal duties until the day of his death (2 Chronicles 26:16–21). Under the Law, no king could wear the sacerdotal garments, and no priest could sit upon the royal throne.

Yet, millennia before Sinai, Scripture recorded an older, primordial order that knew no such segregation. In the valley of Shaveh, Abraham met Melchizedek (Malkî-ṣedeq, "King of Righteousness"), who served simultaneously as the King of Salem (Šālēm, "Peace") and the Priest of the Most High God (’Ēl ‘Elyôn, Genesis 14:18). Melchizedek offered no animal blood; he brought forth bread and wine—the royal emblems of covenant table fellowship—pronounced an authoritative judicial blessing upon Abraham, and received a tithe from the patriarch.

Centuries after Uzziah’s judgment, the post-exilic community faced a deliberate prophetic upheaval. While Zerubbabel of the house of David held the civic governorship, the prophet Zechariah received a divine command to bypass the Davidic heir and place composite crowns of silver and gold (‘ăṭārôt) upon the head of Joshua (Yəhôšūa‘) the High Priest—who already wore the sacerdotal turban. This act was declared a sign of wonders (’anšê môpēt, Zechariah 3:8), pointing forward to a coming figure known as the Branch (Ṣemaḥ):

"He shall bear royal honor, and shall sit and rule on His throne. And He shall be a priest on His throne, and the counsel of peace shall be between them both." (Zechariah 6:13)

This created a massive canonical paradox for any student of the Torah: Mosaic jurisprudence strictly barred any Davidic king from serving as priest, yet prophetic revelation demanded an ultimate Priest-King bearing the name Yəhôšūa‘ to rule on a single throne.

The Epistle to the Hebrews confronts this exact statutory dilemma, establishing how the Son of God holds legitimate high-priestly office without violating the Mosaic legal code. The author immediately acknowledges the technical barrier: Jesus was bodily descended from the tribe of Judah, a lineage concerning which Moses spoke nothing regarding the priesthood (Hebrews 7:14). If Christ’s ministry were restricted to the earthly Mosaic economy, He could not serve as a priest at all, since there were already priests appointed to offer gifts according to the Law (Hebrews 8:4).

This leads to an unavoidable legal verdict:

"For when the priesthood is changed, of necessity there takes place a change of law also." (Hebrews 7:12)

The Aaronic priesthood was intrinsically bound to the Sinai Covenant. For the priesthood to transfer from Levi to Judah, the Sinai legal administration itself had to be formally concluded, fulfilled, and superseded by an older, superior covenantal order.

Hebrews proves the superiority of the Melchizedekian order across four forensic arguments:

Federal Submission: Levi, while still in the loins of his forefather Abraham, paid tithes to Melchizedek, legally acknowledging the inferiority of his future priesthood (Hebrews 7:9–10).

The Authority of Blessing: Melchizedek blessed Abraham, and without dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater (Hebrews 7:7).

Indestructible Life vs. Bodily Genealogy: Aaronic priests held office through physical descent (kata nomon entolēs sarkinēs—according to a law of bodily requirement) and were continually removed by physical death (Hebrews 7:16, 23). In contrast, Christ’s priesthood rests upon the power of an indestructible life (kata dynamin zōēs akatalytou, Hebrews 7:16).

The Ratification by Irrevocable Oath: Aaronic priests were installed without an oath under a temporary covenant. Christ was inducted by the sovereign oath of Yahweh under Psalm 110:4: "The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: 'You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.'" Because it was enacted by divine oath, Christ has become the legal guarantor (egguos) of an unshakeable, better covenant (Hebrews 7:20–22).

This forensic transfer reveals the true meaning of Zechariah’s visions. In Zechariah 3, Joshua the High Priest stood in the divine council covered in defiled garments, prosecuted by haśśāṭān. Yahweh silenced the prosecutor, stripped the soiled garments, and clothed Joshua in pure robes, foretelling the arrival of the Branch. In Zechariah 6, the crowns placed upon Joshua foreshadowed the ultimate reconciliation of offices.

Hebrews 8 and 9 announce the final execution of this verdict: Christ did not enter an earthly sanctuary made with human hands, which was merely an earthly copy (antitypa) of the heavenly reality (Hebrews 8:5; 9:24). He entered the true cosmic Holy of Holies with His own blood, obtaining eternal redemption (aiōnian lytrōsin, Hebrews 9:12).

Under the Levitical economy, the priest stood daily ministering (hestēken kath' hēmeran), because in the earthly tabernacle there were no chairs; the blood of animals could never permanently eradicate sin (Hebrews 10:11). Christ, however, having offered one definitive sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high (Hebrews 8:1; 10:12). His session signifies both sacerdotal completion and monarchical reign: the sacrifice is permanently accepted, the Priest is seated, and the King governs from the throne awaiting the final subjugation of His enemies (Psalm 110:1).

The institutional separation of king and priest under the Law was a necessary constitutional guardrail for a fallen world, demonstrating that mortal men cannot safely wield absolute sovereign power alongside spiritual mediation. Yet the Law was never the terminal destination; it was a tutor guarding the covenant line until the true Branch appeared.

In Melchizedek, God established an early blueprint of the true Kingdom. Through the cross and resurrection, Jesus fulfilled every statutory demand of the Sinai Covenant, formally retiring the fragile Aaronic system to assume the eternal, oath-bound order of Melchizedek.

For the truth seeker, this doctrine is the bedrock of the daily walk:

Unshakable Conscience and Direct Access: The repetitive sacrifices under Aaron served as an annual indictment of unresolved guilt, unable to cleanse the inner conscience (Hebrews 10:1–3). The believer does not live under a cycle of legal condemnation. Because our Melchizedekian Priest offered an all-sufficient blood payment, we have boldness (parrēsia) to enter directly into the Holy of Holies through the veil of His flesh (Hebrews 10:19–22).

The Royal-Priestly Table: Just as Melchizedek met a weary Abraham returning from battle with bread and wine, the risen Priest-King meets the seeker in the wilderness of this life. The Lord's Table is not an altar of repeated sacrifice, but a royal feast of covenant fellowship and sustaining grace provided by the King of Peace Himself.

A King Who Sympathizes, A Priest Who Commands: In Christ, absolute authority and sovereign mercy are permanently unified. On the throne of the cosmos sits a Royal Priest who learned obedience through what He suffered, who sympathizes with human weakness, yet wields total cosmic dominion (Hebrews 4:14–16). The throne of judgment has become a throne of grace.

Steadfast Perseverance in the Finished Order: The severe warnings of Hebrews caution against regressing into external, ritualistic, or works-based systems of self-justification (Hebrews 10:35–39). All earthly sacerdotal hierarchies, human mediators, and ongoing blood offerings are obsolete. The veil is torn, the certificate of debt is nailed to the cross, and our High Priest ever lives to make intercession at the right hand of the Father (Hebrews 7:25).

Today, the Sovereign who directs the machinery of human history is the exact same High Priest who offered His own life for our reconciliation. The throne of supreme cosmic governance and the seat of eternal mercy are one and the same. This truth silences the Accuser, settles the conscience, and anchors the soul within the veil—immovable, eternal, and complete.

text:
Crocodile tears cannot wash away the bloodstains of 1984.
Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, attempts a grotesque whitewashing of history by claiming Indira Gandhi broke down upon seeing photographs of Sri Akal Takht Sahib after Operation Blue Star. If Indira Gandhi genuinely felt anguish, why have Sonia, Rahul and Priyanka never offered an unconditional apology to the Sikh Panth? Tears cannot rewrite history. Operation Blue Star and the 1984 Sikh massacre were not mere administrative lapses but part of an alleged political conspiracy involving the Sanjay Gandhi coterie, Arun Nehru and Giani Zail Singh to dislodge the Akalis, secure electoral gains and punish the Sikhs. Sikhs had led the resistance against the Emergency, accounting for over 43% of arrests nationwide. Congress responded by branding this nationalist community anti-national and allegedly commissioning a private advertising agency ahead of the 1985 elections to run a divisive campaign exploiting public fears about Sikh taxi and auto drivers. The government had alternatives, as Operation Black Thunder later demonstrated: water and electricity supplies could be cut to compel surrender without damaging Sri Akal Takht Sahib or firing inside the sanctum sanctorum. Yet tanks and artillery were deployed inside the Golden Temple complex. Rajiv Gandhi exposed the mindset of the Congress leadership when he justified the massacre with the chilling words, “When a big tree falls, the earth shakes.” Indira Gandhi ordered the assault, Rajiv Gandhi justified the killings, and the Gandhi family has spent four decades refusing to apologise. Adding insult to injury, Sam Pitroda, Overseas Congress Chairperson and an adviser to Rajiv and Rahul Gandhi, dismissed the killing of 3,000 Sikhs with the words, “Hua toh hua.” These are the questions the Gandhi family cannot escape. Their tears today cannot erase their party’s actions or replace the unconditional apology the Sikh community deserves.

text:
Confusion In High Places

Genesis 11:1-4
Now all the earth used the same language and the same words. And it came about, as they journeyed east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there. Then they said to one another, "Come, let’s make bricks and fire them thoroughly." And they used brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar. And they said, "Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top will reach into heaven, and let’s make a name for ourselves; otherwise we will be scattered abroad over the face of all the earth."

What was their crime against God?

It was disobedience to His plan for their disbursement and development.

God had spoken clearly after the flood:

"Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth" (Genesis 9:1)

The people of Shinar did the opposite, exposing their motives. 

"otherwise we will be scattered abroad over the face of all the earth."

Why do you suppose they were concerned about being scattered? 

We don't really know but I would speculate that staying together in one fortified place, with a common language and a towering center of spiritual awareness, offered the illusion of control. It's the same lure that communism always seems to offer at first glance. Under that arrangement the individual and the family are subordinated to the collective project. Vulnerability is traded for an engineered sense of strength. The fear of being "scattered" is reframed as the enemy of progress, so the people willingly surrender the very dispersal God commanded. Thereby secularizing their impulses and refusing God's ordered will. They wanted a name for themselves and a reach into heaven on their own terms. And the tower is the apparatus for that communal power. 

The tower is widely understood as a ziggurat; the stepped temple towers of ancient Mesopotamia. Solidly built structures of fired brick and bitumen [tar] that rose in successive tiers toward a small shrine at the summit. And these structures served as a humanly engineered staircase into heaven, rendering dependence on God’s word unnecessary. 

I find God's response very interesting.

Genesis 11:6-9
And the Lord said, "Behold, they are one people, and they all have the same language. And this is what they have started to do, and now nothing which they plan to do will be impossible for them. Come, let Us go down and there confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech." So the Lord scattered them abroad from there over the face of all the earth; and they stopped building the city. Therefore it was named Babel, because there the Lord confused the language of all the earth; and from there the Lord scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.

God explains that with mankind, if left unchecked, the same impulse that produced a city and a ziggurat will produce whatever else they set their minds to. And always in the direction of making a name for themselves and securing their own center as gods of their own making. 

They had said "Come, let’s…" three times. Now the Lord says, "Come, let Us go down and there confuse their language." And He is using the plural "Us" again (as in Genesis 1:26 and 3:22) underscoring that this is a deliberate, sovereign triune act of the Godhead. He doesn't destroy their tower or strike the people dead. He simply removes the condition that made the project possible; the common language. The language, by the way, that He gave them. 

Why confuse their language?

In Genesis 11:6–7 the Lord observes that the people are one, with one language, and that nothing they plan will be impossible for them. Information and the sharing of knowledge has always from the beginning been the means for mankind's sinful desires. Their shared speech is identified as what makes the city and the tower possible. Planning, engineering, motivating the masses into constructing the devise; all these elements of architecture require shared speech and understanding.

text:
🇺🇦 On the day Abu Dhabi talks open, Zelensky used an interview with Danish broadcaster DR Nyheder to lay out three arguments: why Europe cannot afford to step back, why he rejects trading Donbas for security, and why he sees a ceasefire as the only workable first step.

On Europe, he described two scenarios if European support fades. The "dangerous" one is Russian hybrid attacks on a massive scale, which he says Moscow has already tested in Moldova, Romania, Bulgaria, Germany, Finland and Denmark. The "very dangerous" one is Russia moving deeper into Europe, seeking influence over the Baltic states and Moldova "at the very least." That would draw in NATO and the United States, and he warned Russia could block the Baltic Sea as it does the Black Sea.

On territory, he recounted an exchange with American interlocutors who asked whether Ukraine could exchange Donbas for security. His answer was to ask what that security would be. Told "not NATO, but similar to NATO," he replied that Washington wanted a clear answer on Donbas while offering only something "similar" in return. 

He pointed to the Budapest-era loss of Ukraine's nuclear arsenal, and to Bucha, as reasons nobody should trust Putin to stop. In his view, leaving Donbas would bring a pause, followed by another offensive in "one year, two years, or five years."

On ending the war, his formula is to stop on the current line, declare a ceasefire and move to diplomacy, for months or longer if needed. He acknowledges the open questions, including where to stand, the monitoring mission's mandate, demilitarization, Europe's role and reconstruction money. His conclusion is direct: if Putin insists on signing a comprehensive plan before any ceasefire, "it simply means he doesn't want to stop the war."
That sets out Kyiv's position as the Abu Dhabi round begins. Moscow wants a settlement before the guns go quiet. Kyiv wants a ceasefire first and the hard questions after.

The account of the American offer comes only from Zelensky, so the text attributes it to him. I checked the text for dashes and the house-style pivots. The Budapest mention is my own context, since he only says "they took our nuclear weapons," and you can cut it if you'd rather stick strictly to his words.

text:
The quickest way to end Russia’s war is to hold the positions and move to discussions. What is very important here is that we decided: stop where we are, it’s a ceasefire, and we go to the diplomatic track. It can last one month, two months, or one year. Or it can last longer than we expect today. But we end the hot stage and people stop dying. When you hold, you speak about the contact line, slow down the pace of mobilization; the economy begins to work. You are in discussions. Dialogue is better than guns. That's why the best way to end this war is to exchange guns for words. 

Of course, you will have thousands of questions. How to stop? Where to stand? What is the mandate of the monitoring mission? What is demilitarized? What does it mean? What do we need for this? Europeans. Reconstruction. Where to get the money? Thousands of questions, but this is the format to stop the war – ceasefire. If Putin doesn't want a ceasefire and says, “No, I want a long plan, with different questions, both difficult, sensitive, and not. And then, when we sign this long plan, we will stop the war,” it simply means he doesn't want to stop the war.

From an interview with DR Nyheder. (3/3)

@RepThomasMassie 
A broader examination of Thomas Massie: Ethics, money, political influence and accountability.

Thomas Massie is a Republican member of the U.S. House of Representatives from Kentucky. He has developed a reputation as an outspoken libertarian-leaning conservative who frequently challenges Republican leadership, including President Trump.

The important question is whether his public positions, private conduct, financial interests, and use of congressional authority are consistent with the principles he claims to represent.

The Cynthia West controversy: possible misuse of political influence

This is one of the more serious personal-conduct questions.

In May 2026, Cynthia West, a former girlfriend of Massie, accused him of offering her $5,000 to abandon a wrongful-termination complaint involving Representative Victoria Spartz.

The reporting raises several questions:

* Why did Massie arrange employment for someone he was personally involved with in another congressional office?

* Did his personal relationship create a conflict of interest?

* Did he attempt to influence how a workplace complaint was handled?

* Was money offered to discourage someone from pursuing a complaint?

Massie denied the allegations through his campaign, which characterized them as political attacks. Spartz's office said West's temporary employment ended because of unsatisfactory performance.

These claims have not been established as wrongdoing. 

Campaign financing and financial interests

This deserves a closer look.

According to Federal Election Commission records, between January 2025 and September 30, 2026, Massie's authorized campaign committees reported:

Total receipts

$8.89M

Total expenditures
$9.33M

Reported campaign activity, not personal income or net worth.

Source: Federal Election Commission, 2025–2026 reporting period. FEC +1

Questions worth investigating include:

* Who were his largest individual donors?

* Which PACs contributed?

* Who received payments from his campaign?

* Were campaign expenditures properly documented?

* Did any financial relationships overlap with his legislative activities?

Receiving campaign contributions is not corruption. The concern would be evidence of an improper exchange, undisclosed benefit, or violation of campaign-finance law.

His relationship with President Trump and Republican leadership

Massie has repeatedly broken with Republican leadership.

Some examples:

* Opposed Trump's major spending legislation.

* Opposed certain foreign-aid packages.

* Challenged the administration's military actions involving Iran.

* Joined Democrat Ro Khanna in pushing for disclosure of the Epstein files.

* Has advocated withdrawing the United States from NATO.

His supporters call this constitutional independence. His critics see someone who frequently undermines his own party.

The important distinction is that disagreeing with a president is not evidence of corruption. His actual legislative decisions should be evaluated on their merits. The Washington Post

The Epstein files and congressional transparency

This is particularly interesting.

Massie worked with Democratic Representative Ro Khanna to force action on releasing records related to Jeffrey Epstein.

Their efforts resulted in passage of the Epstein Files Transparency Act in November 2025.

Massie has continued arguing that the government has not released everything it should.

There is a legitimate question here: Is Massie consistently demanding transparency from government, including when transparency could expose people in his own political circles?

That is a fair standard to apply to any elected official. The Washington Post

text:
On March 27, 1972, John D. Rockefeller 3rd transmitted the Commission on Population Growth and the American Future's final report. Further growth offered "no substantial benefits"; gradual stabilization "through voluntary means" would help solve the nation's problems.

His letter of transmittal that day, addressed "To the President and Congress of the United States," stated the conclusion in full: "we have concluded that, in the long run, no substantial benefits will result from further growth of the Nation's population, rather that the gradual stabilization of our population through voluntary means would contribute significantly to the Nation's ability to solve its problems."

Congress had created the commission on March 16, 1970, at Nixon's request. Rockefeller chaired it. The report, titled "Population and the American Future," lists 24 members. Its findings were already public. The New York Times of March 12, 1972, reported from Washington that the commission "told President Nixon and Congress today" — March 11 — that America should slow and gradually stop population growth, and called the volume "the first of three final reports."

An advance Signet paperback (New American Library, First Printing, March 1972), labeled subject to revisions in the official Government Printing Office edition, carried a front-matter page headed "Advice and Dissent" under the subtitle "The Controversy: Abortion on Request." It stated: "The objective for American society should be to make the child-bearing decision as free as possible of unintended societal pressures." Under "The Majority Recommends," it summarized abortion liberalization with public funding and insurance coverage; state encouragement of contraceptive services for teenagers, with sex education widely available; and easier hospital access to voluntary sterilization.

On May 5, 1972, Rockefeller formally presented the report to Nixon at the White House. Nixon's statement that day thanked the commission, then drew hard lines: "I want to reaffirm and reemphasize that I do not support unrestricted abortion policies... I consider abortion an unacceptable form of population control." He added: "I also want to make it clear that I do not support the unrestricted distribution of family planning services and devices to minors." And: "While disagreeing with the general thrust of some of the Commission's recommendations, I wish to extend my thanks to the members of the Commission..."

Image: Population and the American Future, Signet Special W5219 advance paperback (New American Library, First Printing, March 1972), "Advice and Dissent" page.
