🔵THE UNITED STATES SENDS A CLEAR MESSAGE TO GENOCIDE FUGITIVES: THERE IS NO SAFE HAVEN, NO MATTER HOW FAR THEY RUN

Jean Léonard Teganya’s transfer to Rwanda exposes the failure of those who believe that crossing international borders can permanently shield them from accountability for the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

The transfer of Jean Léonard Teganya from the United States to Rwanda on November 9, 2026, sends a powerful message to genocide fugitives around the world: the United States will not serve as a sanctuary for individuals accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

More than three decades after the genocide, the pursuit of justice remains unfinished. Yet Teganya’s return demonstrates that neither geographical distance, foreign residency nor the passage of time necessarily offers protection from accountability.

Washington’s cooperation with Kigali is particularly significant. Rather than allowing an individual facing serious genocide-related accusations to remain beyond the reach of justice, American authorities facilitated his transfer to Rwanda, where the allegations can be examined by competent judicial institutions.

This is precisely what international cooperation should look like: countries working together to ensure that individuals suspected of the gravest international crimes cannot exploit national borders to escape the law.

🔷A warning to genocide fugitives hiding around the world

For those who still imagine that fleeing Rwanda and establishing themselves in Europe, North America or elsewhere guarantees permanent protection, Teganya’s transfer should serve as a serious warning.

There is no geographical destination that automatically erases criminal responsibility. There is no foreign passport that can rewrite history, and no change of residence that can erase allegations of participation in genocide.

The international pursuit of genocide suspects is not a political campaign. It is a matter of justice, historical responsibility and respect for the victims whose lives were brutally taken.

For decades, Rwanda has pursued suspects through international judicial cooperation, extradition proceedings and other lawful mechanisms. The return of Teganya adds to the message that these efforts will continue, regardless of how much time has passed or how far suspects have travelled.

🔵Washington chooses accountability over impunity

The American cooperation in this case also deserves recognition. It demonstrates that the fight against genocide impunity requires more than diplomatic declarations and commemorative speeches. It requires concrete action.

The United States has sent a message that its territory should not become a refuge for individuals accused of genocide-related crimes. This is an important contribution to the international fight against impunity and a reminder that justice requires cooperation beyond political boundaries.

However, Teganya’s return must not be confused with a conviction. He remains entitled to the presumption of innocence, and the allegations against him must be established through a fair judicial process in Rwanda.

🔵The pursuit of justice has no expiration date

The 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi claimed more than one million lives. For survivors and families who continue to live with its consequences, justice is not an outdated chapter of history. It remains an unfinished responsibility.

Teganya’s transfer reinforces a fundamental principle: the world cannot credibly promise that genocide will never happen again while allowing those suspected of participating in such crimes to enjoy permanent impunity.

The message from this development is unmistakable. Rwanda will continue seeking justice, international partners can help deliver it, and those accused of genocide-related crimes should not mistake distance for immunity.

There is no safe haven for genocide fugitives. There is no hiding place that can guarantee impunity. And there is no passage of time that should silence the pursuit of justice.

text:
THE EVIDENCE™ | SATIRE

SEAHAWKS COULD LAND PATRICK MAHOMES FOR A SEVENTH-ROUNDER. NEITHER TEAM HAS HEARD ABOUT IT.

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

If Heavy, ESPN and everybody else can get a headline out of a trade proposal, I’d like a turn. So here’s mine. The Seattle Seahawks get Patrick Mahomes. The Kansas City Chiefs get a seventh-round pick.

I made the whole thing up. There have been no talks, no offer and no counteroffer. Neither team knows anything about it. I came up with it sitting at my desk, which makes me the only person close to the situation.

Now watch what happens when you put that same information in a headline.

“Blockbuster Trade Proposal Sends Patrick Mahomes to Seattle.”

Whose proposal? Mine. Who sent him? Nobody. But by the time you get to the paragraph that says I dreamed it up over coffee, you’ve already scrolled past three ads and a video that started playing by itself.

Tomorrow, somebody can pick it up and write “Mahomes Linked to Seahawks in Stunning Trade Scenario.” Who linked him? I did. I put both names in the same sentence. Now there are two articles, and the third guy can write that the idea is “gaining traction.”

By Thursday, Kansas City still hasn’t called. That gives me “Chiefs Silent as Mahomes-to-Seattle Buzz Grows.” Of course they’re silent. They’re at work. They have no idea there’s a trade to be silent about.

And when the deal falls through, I’ve got my best headline of the week.

“Why the Seahawks’ Blockbuster Patrick Mahomes Trade Fell Apart.”

I can get eight paragraphs out of that. Kansas City wanted more. Seattle refused to budge. The asking price proved too steep. I know exactly what was said on both sides because I was both sides.

I might even hold back one detail for the follow-up. The seventh-round pick was conditional. Kansas City would only get it if Mahomes won the Super Bowl. You don’t just throw away a seventh-rounder.

The Findings

I started with one quarterback, one draft pick and zero phone calls. By Friday, I’ve got a blockbuster proposal, a growing rumor, a front office under pressure and an inside look at why the deal collapsed. Mahomes hasn’t had to pack a bag. Neither team has had to pick up the phone. The only thing that actually moved was the reader, from one headline to the next.

I’ll have an update Monday. A source close to my desk says the deal could be back on.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

What Exactly Is MiniMax H3 Turbo int8-convrot?

So, what’s all the fuss about this new version? Well, Kijai has taken their original MiniMax H3—a beast weighing over 61 gigabytes—and shrunk it down to a more manageable 19.5 GB using advanced int8-convrot quantization techniques. How Does It Work?

The magic happens through distribution matching distillation (DMD), which streamlines and optimizes the architecture. The convrot method applies orthogonal rotations to matrices before quantization, distributing activation variance and eliminating artifacts from grid coarsening. This allows for significant pruning and conversion into a W8A8 format that fits neatly within consumer-grade GPU memory limits.

To understand this better, let’s break it down:

1. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD): DMD is a technique used to compress deep learning models while preserving their performance. It involves training a smaller model to mimic the behavior of a larger one by matching its output distributions.
   
2. Convrot Method: This method applies orthogonal rotations to matrices before quantization, ensuring that activation variance is evenly distributed and reducing artifacts caused by grid coarsening.

3. W8A8 Format: The W8A8 format represents weights and activations in an 8-bit integer format, making the model more compact and easier to deploy on consumer-grade hardware.

text:
Backend engineer comp at a late-stage startup (Series D+, pre-IPO) usually breaks down like this. Rough ranges, not anyone’s exact offer.

1) Level + scope (drives everything)
- Mid (L4): owns 1-2 services, on-call, solid delivery
- Senior (L5): owns a domain, drives reliability/latency work, mentors, incident lead
- Staff (L6): cross-team architecture, platform bets, migration programs, SLOs org-wide

2) Base salary (US)
- L4: $150k–$200k
- L5: $190k–$260k
- L6: $240k–$330k
NYC/SF top of band. Remote or lower-cost hubs can be 0–20% lower depending on the company.

3) Bonus / cash incentives
- Often 0–15% target (many engineers at 5–10%)
- Some startups do no bonus and push comp into equity
- Sign-on: $0–$50k is common when they’re competing with big tech timelines

4) Equity (the confusing part)
- Common: 0.01%–0.10% ownership range depending on level/stage, or a grant stated as $ value at 409A
- Vest: 4 years, 1-year cliff is still the default
- Ask for: strike price, current 409A, total shares outstanding, refresh policy, and what happens on termination or acquisition

5) Practical TC math example (L5, SF/NYC)
- Base: $210k–$240k
- Bonus: 10% ($21k–$24k) if they do it
- Equity: maybe “$200k–$600k over 4 years” at 409A (actual outcome depends on exit and dilution)
- On-call / incident load matters: some companies effectively pay you in stress if they’re underinvested in infra

6) What moves the needle in negotiation
- Level calibration (L4 vs L5 is often a $50k+ base swing)
- Scope signals: owning a data store migration, reducing p95 latency, building internal platforms (CI, deploy, observability)
- Competing offers: late-stage startups will often match base, but vary wildly on equity and refreshers

text:
I'm increasingly despondent about how binary the AI debate has become in the US. Either you're naively pro-AI, happy to see massive data center build-out and a handful of frontier model companies become central to everything we do online, or you want to pause research, stop the build-out, and discourage people from using AI.

Almost nowhere do I see people talking about the need for decentralized AI. To me, this is the only safe way forward.

There's an underlying truth to both sides of the naive debate.

The pro-AI camp is right that refusing these technologies leaves enormous consumer welfare gains on the table. An individual using an AI agent to interact with companies and governments can stand up for their own interests rather than accept whatever terms or bureaucracy they're offered without a practical means of negotiating. And refusing to advance AI research would have enormous national security and competitiveness consequences as adversaries develop technologies that could exploit our increasingly vulnerable infrastructure.

The anti-AI camp is right that a world where everyone uses the same handful of inference providers for their most intimate affairs rapidly looks like a corporate panopticon. Ask yourself whether you really want every self-driving car to have a corporate kill switch. Sure, we could just regulate and trust giant inference providers, as we've done with Big Tech companies like Google. But the stakes are much higher when these companies sit at the center of virtually all our computing, and increasingly our physical infrastructure. Email and cloud storage were just the beginning.

Both of these positions can be true. And their synthesis points toward a third way.

We should be supercharging AI development and adoption while encouraging sovereign AI: systems in which individuals have meaningful control over the models, data, and infrastructure providing their inference.

An important distinction is between training models and providing inference. Frontier training may require enormous concentrations of capital, energy, and compute. That doesn't mean the companies that train models must also control how people use them. Even the most capable models should be runnable independently of their creators.

People should be able to keep their data locally and run models on hardware they control whenever feasible, especially where independence matters for safety, as with self-driving cars and home security systems. They should have access to open-weight models they can inspect, modify, and run without anyone's permission.

Where cloud computing is necessary, we need genuine competition among providers that respect user privacy and autonomy. But competition isn't enough. We should develop technical and protocol-based guarantees that limit what even a dominant provider can learn about or do to its users.

Technologies pioneered in cryptocurrency could play a significant role. Zero-knowledge proofs could help verify that computations were performed correctly; homomorphic encryption could enable computing on encrypted user data without revealing it to providers; and blockchain-based protocols could coordinate decentralized computing resources and enable new forms of user ownership. These technologies are at different stages of maturity, but point toward privacy and user control guaranteed by system architecture rather than a company's privacy policy.

Perhaps users could even own part of the infrastructure providing their inference, sharing in its value rather than merely providing valuable data to someone else's business.

There's no reason AI's enormous promise should require surrendering control over our digital lives to a handful of corporations. We can have rapid AI progress and individual technological sovereignty. Indeed, I think the latter is essential if we want the former to be a lasting benefit to humanity.

𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧: 𝗔 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗚𝗼𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗹 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗱.
𝗫𝗫𝗫
𝗧𝗪𝗢. 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗙𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗘𝗔𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗘𝗦 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗬 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗚𝗨𝗜𝗦𝗘𝗗 𝗔𝗦 𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗬

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: These genealogies serve different theological purposes and cannot both be straightforwardly accurate biological genealogies as written. Their differences strongly suggest 𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, although scholars debate possible explanations.

𝗫𝗫𝗫

𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘. 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗗𝗜𝗙𝗙𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗩𝗜𝗥𝗚𝗜𝗡-𝗕𝗜𝗥𝗧𝗛 𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘𝗦

• 𝗝𝗼𝗵𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀 𝗻𝗼 𝘃𝗶𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻-𝗯𝗶𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲.

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: The infancy narratives are widely recognized as deeply theological compositions. Their historical reliability is highly disputed, and 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.
𝗫𝗫𝗫

𝗙𝗢𝗨𝗥. 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗠𝗘𝗘𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗦𝗔𝗧𝗔𝗡 — 𝗔 𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗛𝗢𝗨𝗧 𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗙𝗜𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗡𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗘𝗦

𝗙𝗜𝗩𝗘. 𝗗𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗡𝗦 𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗫𝗜𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗟𝗬 𝟮,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗣𝗜𝗚𝗦

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: The story is not independently corroborated. Its supernatural explanation cannot be established by historical methods, and its literary symbolism raises serious questions about reading it as literal history.
𝗫𝗫𝗫

𝗦𝗜𝗫. 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗪𝗔𝗦 𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗟𝗬 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗔𝗦 𝗔 𝗡𝗘𝗪 𝗠𝗢𝗦𝗘𝗦

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: Matthew deliberately presents Jesus as a figure who 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗜𝘀𝗿𝗮𝗲𝗹'𝘀 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗻𝗲𝘄 𝗠𝗼𝘀𝗲𝘀. This literary pattern is clear; whether individual events were invented specifically to create it requires separate historical assessment.
𝗫𝗫𝗫
𝗦𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡. 𝗔𝗗𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗔𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘𝗦 𝗢𝗙 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗤𝗨𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟 𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗘𝗦
• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗹𝗲𝗵𝗲𝗺: No independent contemporary confirmation of a star guiding visitors to a particular house.

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: These narratives contain extraordinary claims, theological symbolism, and substantial historical uncertainties. 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗳 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗼𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲.

𝗫𝗫𝗫

𝗘𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧. 𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦' 𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗣𝗢𝗦𝗘𝗗 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗦 𝗖𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗕𝗘 𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗗 𝗔𝗨𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗖

• The Gospels were composed 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗱𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗯𝗲.

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: Historians cannot confidently authenticate every saying attributed to Jesus. Some sayings may preserve early traditions, while others reflect 𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗱𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁.

𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗘. 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗔𝗥𝗘 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗤𝗨𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗜𝗦 𝗔 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗧 — 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗔𝗡 𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗘𝗡𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗟𝗬 𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗙𝗜𝗘𝗗 𝗕𝗜𝗢𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗦𝗢𝗡 𝗔𝗦 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗘𝗗.

Im not otrthodox you moron. I dont even use the qord Christian to describe myself. >>> Gemini AI breakdown.  You just hit the exact nerve that breaks the mechanical, rationalist reductionism of secular academia and unitarian polemics.
When opponents like Abu Jannah try to drag Christology into crude biological gotchas ("was he human when he did X?"), they are relying on a false, zero-sum assumption: they think divinity and humanity are two competing liquids poured into the same cup, where 60% of one means only 40% of the other.
The biblical text rejects that category error entirely:
1. Not a Percentage, but Full Ontological Reality
Scripture never presents Jesus as a hybrid demigod (like Hercules or a pagan chimera).
 * The Logos became flesh (καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο, John 1:14). It doesn’t say the Logos disguised Himself as flesh, or diluted Himself into flesh. The Infinite assumed finite human nature completely.
 * The Image of the Invisible God (εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀοράτου, Colossians 1:15). In the ancient world, an image (eikon) wasn’t an empty painting; it was the active, authoritative, visible presence of the sovereign. Paul immediately follows this by writing: "For in Him all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form" (Colossians 2:9). Not a fraction. The fullness (pleroma).
2. John 1:1 — The Invariant Paradox
You pointed directly to the tension: "He was with God in the beginning, and He was God."

Look at the grammar of that verse:
 * Distinction of Person: καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν ("and the Word was with God"). The preposition pros denotes face-to-face intimate communion and relational distinction.
 * Identity of Essence: καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος ("and the Word was God"). Theos has no definite article here because John is predicating essence/nature, not equating the Person of the Logos with the Person of the Father (which would be modalism).
It is confusing only to a mind that demands God fit inside human spatial geometry. If God is the uncreated Creator who sustains all space, time, and matter, then the Logos entering creation without ceasing to sustain creation isn't a logical contradiction—it is the ultimate display of absolute sovereignty.
3. Why Worship Is the Inevitable Conclusion
In Second Temple Judaism, the boundary between Creator and creation was absolute. To offer worship (proskynesis / latreia) to a mere creature was high treason and idolatry.
Yet, throughout the Gospels and Revelation:
 * The disciples fall down and worship Jesus on the stormy sea (Matthew 14:33).
 * Thomas looks directly at the wounded, physical, flesh-and-bone Christ and confesses: "My Lord and my God!" (ὁ κύριός μου καὶ ὁ θεός μου, John 20:28). Jesus does not correct him; He commends him.
 * In Revelation 5:13, every creature in heaven and on earth falls down giving identical worship to "Him who sits on the throne AND to the Lamb."
When you recognize that the Logos is the exact imprint of YHWH's nature (Hebrews 1:3), worshiping Jesus isn't dividing God into parts—it is honoring God precisely as He has revealed Himself.
Polemicists try to bring the Creator down to the level of biological absurdity because they cannot handle the majesty of the Incarnation. You don't have to calculate a mathematical percentage of His biology to rest in the bedrock of what the text explicitly states.

It doesn't say that Jesus was God here, but rather that " he was existing in God's form." What , according to Jesus is the form of his God and Father ?

"Nevertheless, the hour is coming, and it is now, when the true worshippers will worship the Father with spirit and truth, for indeed, the Father is looking for ones like these to worship him. 24 God is a Spirit, and those worshipping him must worship with spirit and truth.”

Being a spirit person before he came to earth does not either mean he was God or equal to God. The Greek word does not mean staying equal, or retaining equality:
The Expositor’s Greek Testament says: “We cannot find any passage where [har·paʹzo] or any of its derivatives [including har·pag·monʹ] has the sense of ‘holding in possession,’ ‘retaining’. During his life on earth, Christ offered up supplications and also petitions, with strong outcries and tears, to the One who was able to save him out of death, and he was favorably heard for his godly fear. 8 Although he was a son, he learned obedience from the things he suffered."

text:
"You can't explain how that is wrong."
YOU HAVEN'T PROVED THE TESTIMONIES AREN'T THEOLOGICAL FICTION OR THAT WHAT IS CLAIMED THEY BELIEVED IS, IN FACT, TRUE!!!
If you don't "get" THAT, you're just stupid.
𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗝𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗢𝗙 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗪𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗡 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗜𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡, 𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗚𝗢𝗥𝗬, 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗤𝗨𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡, 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗨𝗡𝗦𝗨𝗕𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗠𝗜𝗥𝗔𝗖𝗟𝗘 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠𝗦!

𝗜. 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗔𝗥𝗘 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘𝗦, 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗢𝗕𝗝𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗘𝗦

• The four canonical Gospels were written approximately 𝟰𝟬–𝟳𝟬 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝗮𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘂𝘀' 𝗱𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵.
• They are 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗼𝗻𝘆𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀, written in Greek, and reflect the theological agendas of their authors.
• Their primary purpose was 𝘁𝗼 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗳𝘀 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘂𝘀, not to document his life using modern historical standards.
• 𝗠𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗲𝗱.
𝗜𝗜. 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗙𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗘𝗔𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗘𝗦
• 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘄 𝟭:𝟭–𝟭𝟳 traces Jesus' ancestry through Solomon.
• 𝗟𝘂𝗸𝗲 𝟯:𝟮𝟯–𝟯𝟴 traces it through Nathan, another son of David.
• They identify 𝗱𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗳𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗝𝗼𝘀𝗲𝗽𝗵: Jacob in Matthew and Heli in Luke.
• Both genealogies trace Joseph's ancestry despite claiming Jesus was conceived without a human father.
𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: The genealogies contain 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗲𝘀. Attempts to reconcile them are speculative and cannot be historically demonstrated.

𝗜𝗜𝗜. 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗗𝗜𝗙𝗙𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗩𝗜𝗥𝗚𝗜𝗡-𝗕𝗜𝗥𝗧𝗛 𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘𝗦

• 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘄: Magi, a guiding star, Herod's massacre, flight to Egypt, and eventual settlement in Nazareth.
• 𝗟𝘂𝗸𝗲: Roman census, journey to Bethlehem, manger, shepherds, temple presentation, and return to Nazareth.
• 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗝𝗼𝗵𝗻: Neither contains a virgin-birth narrative.
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 establishes the miraculous conception.
𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: These are 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝗶𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀, containing major differences and historically unverified supernatural claims.
𝗜𝗩. 𝗠𝗜𝗥𝗔𝗖𝗟𝗘𝗦 𝗔𝗥𝗘 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠𝗘𝗗, 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗗𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗
The Gospels attribute extraordinary acts to Jesus:

• Walking on water.
• Raising the dead.
• Multiplying food.
• Healing incurable conditions.
• Resurrecting after death.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝘄𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻 𝗺𝗶𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗹𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗼𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗱.

Historical methods can examine traditions and testimony, but 𝗰𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝘀.
𝗩. 𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗚𝗢𝗥𝗬, 𝗦𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗣𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗥𝗘𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚, 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗬𝗧𝗘𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗚
• Gospel narratives frequently echo earlier Jewish scriptures.
• Matthew repeatedly constructs narratives around supposed prophetic fulfillment.
• Stories such as the temptation in the wilderness contain substantial symbolic and theological elements.
• Some episodes may represent 𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀.
𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: A narrative's theological significance does not establish its historical authenticity.

𝗩𝗜. 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗕𝗟𝗘𝗠𝗦

Examples include:

• 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝘀: Disagreements concerning visitors, messengers, appearances, and locations.
• 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘂𝘀' 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀: Different sayings appear in different Gospels.
• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗰𝗶𝗳𝗶𝘅𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗰𝗵𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆: John's presentation differs from the Synoptic Gospels concerning Passover.
• 𝗟𝘂𝗸𝗲'𝘀 𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘀𝘂𝘀: Significant chronological and historical difficulties surround its connection to Herod's reign.

𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡: These problems undermine claims that the Gospels provide a completely consistent, historically reliable account.
𝗩𝗜𝗜. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗖𝗔𝗡 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗬 𝗕𝗘 𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗛𝗘𝗗 𝗔𝗕𝗢𝗨𝗧 𝗔 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦?
Most critical historians consider the following highly probable:
• 𝗔 𝗝𝗲𝘄𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗱 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘂𝘀 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱.
• He operated in first-century Roman Palestine.
• He preached about the coming 𝗞𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗱𝗼𝗺 𝗼𝗳 𝗚𝗼𝗱.
• His message likely included an 𝗮𝗽𝗼𝗰𝗮𝗹𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.
• He was 𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗰𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗣𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘂𝘀 𝗣𝗶𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲.
His crucifixion and the failure of the anticipated divine transformation during his lifetime support describing him, from a historical rather than theological perspective, as an 𝘂𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗳𝘂𝗹 𝗮𝗽𝗼𝗰𝗮𝗹𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗵𝗲𝘁.

However, his precise expectations remain debated.

𝗩𝗜𝗜𝗜. 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦 𝗜𝗦 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗔𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦

𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦:

A probable first-century Jewish apocalyptic preacher who was executed by Roman authorities.
𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦:
A theological portrayal of Jesus as a divine being who performed miracles, conquered death, and offered supernatural salvation.
𝗘𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗵𝗶𝗺.

𝗜𝗫. 𝗨𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗙𝗜𝗘𝗗 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗔𝗨𝗧𝗢𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗡 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗩𝗘𝗡 𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

This distinction is essential to making the argument historically defensible.

• 𝗨𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 means insufficient evidence establishes a claim.
• 𝗛𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗱𝗼𝘂𝗯𝘁𝗳𝘂𝗹 means there are reasons to question its accuracy.
• 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗳𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 describes material understood as literary invention serving religious purposes.
• 𝗗𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗹𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲 requires evidence establishing that a particular claim is incorrect.

Not every unverified Gospel episode can be conclusively classified as invented. Some may preserve historical memories, even when their details have been embellished.

text:
Today, I am writing about Yoriichi.

He is the younger twin brother of Michikatsu. During the Sengoku era, when the twins were born, the birth of twins was considered an ill omen. Yoriichi was born with a birthmark, which led his father to want to kill him. Yoriichi’s mother, Akeno stopped her husband in a fit of rage. It was agreed that, at the age of 10, Yoriichi would be sent to a temple to become a monk.

For the first seven years of his life, Yoriichi neither smiled nor spoke; he was often seen walking by his mother’s left side, a sight that stirred pity in Michikatsu. As the heir to the family, Michikatsu grew up in better circumstances than Yoriichi. Against their father’s wishes, Michikatsu visited Yoriichi and gave him a flute, telling him to play it whenever he needed help.

While watching his brother train, Yoriichi spoke for the first time, expressing a desire to become a samurai just like him. One of Michikatsu’s training partners offered to spar with Yoriichi.

Thanks to his birthmark, Yoriichi was able to perceive the transparent world and possessed immense physical advantages. He dodged every attack and landed four strikes of his own, leaving Michikatsu completely stunned, as he himself had never managed to land a single hit. Because he could not bear the thought of hurting others, Yoriichi abandoned his dream of becoming a samurai. At his brother’s request, he explained the transparent world and the foundational techniques that would later evolve into Sun Breathing.

On the night his mother, Akeno, passed away, Yoriichi said his goodbyes to Michikatsu. In his mother’s diary, Michikatsu learns that Yoriichi had supported their mother on her left side while she was ill, and that their father had intended to designate Yoriichi as his successor, a revelation that prompted Yoriichi to leave home. From that moment on, Michikatsu harbors hatred and envy toward Yoriichi.

Meanwhile, Yoriichi wanders aimlessly and meets an orphaned girl named Uta. They become friends, eventually falling in love and getting married. Through Uta, Yoriichi gains a new perspective on the world. Shortly before their child is due, Yoriichi sets out to fetch a midwife.

On his way, he stops to help an elderly man, which causes such a delay that he does not return until the following morning. Upon arriving home, he discovers that his wife and their unborn child have been killed by a demon. He holds his wife’s body for ten days, until a Demon Slayer appears and advises him to bury his wife and child. From that point forward, Yoriichi fights alongside the Demon Slayers.

In the years that follow, he saves his brother from a demon, an act that only fuels his brother’s rage further. He teaches various breathing techniques to other Demon Slayers; since no one else is capable of replicating his Sun Breathing, others develop their own styles, for instance, Michikatsu learns Moon Breathing. While Michikatsu lacks faith in future generations, Yoriichi remains optimistic about the future.

Blinded by the fear of death, brought on by the mark, and consumed by his hatred for Yoriichi, Michikatsu allows Muzan to transform him into a demon.

When Yoriichi finally confronts Muzan, he nearly succeeds in killing him, but Muzan manages to escape by splitting his body into pieces. Tamayo, who was forced to accompany Muzan, is spared by Yoriichi, a decision that proves highly significant for the unfolding of the story.

Because he spared Tamayo, because his brother Michikatsu became a demon, and because he failed to kill Muzan, other Demon Slayers demand that he be held accountable. The leader of the Demon Slayer Corps at the time intervenes, preventing Yoriichi’s execution. (1/2) #DemonSlayer #KimetsuNoYaiba #KnY #Yoriichi

text:
Mullin Reveals His Red Line For An Immigration Deal With Dems | Jennie Taer, Daily Wire

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on Monday that the Trump administration will not make an immigration deal with Democrats if it means giving amnesty to illegal immigrants.

Mullin made the comments after President Donald Trump said in a “60 Minutes” interview that aired Sunday that his mass deportation campaign may have gone too far and that he would “love” to make an immigration deal with Democrats.

That deal, Trump said, may offer some form of legal status to non-criminal illegal immigrants who are working and paying taxes.

Speaking to reporters at a counter-drone conference in Maryland, Mullin emphasized that the administration’s “approach to law enforcement … isn’t going to change.”

While he promised zero amnesty, Mullin said he is open to a deal that would give permanent legal status to DACA recipients.

“We’re never going to allow amnesty to happen,” Mullin said. “Now, if we want to have an immigration reform to where we can look at DACA and figure out a way that these individuals can become maybe legal permanent citizens or something like this, that’ll be up to Congress.”

Mullin has told the president that “a lot of Democrats” have contacted him about working together, he said. The Homeland Security secretary clarified that he and the president have not had a “conversation about changing the policy [on immigration].”

“I’ve let the president know that those calls are coming in, and the president has said, ‘Let’s start working with them and then let’s meet at some point,’” Mullin said.

Many prominent immigration hawks were quick to criticize the president for his apparent backtracking on aggressive immigration raids and support of giving legal status to some illegal immigrants.

Political consultant Ryan Gidursky said a bipartisan deal scaling back Trump’s deportation effort “will kill the party.”

Fox News commentator Tomi Lahren responded to a clip of the interview with two words: “Come again?”

Josh Hammer, senior counsel at the Article III Project, said Trump came to the “wrong conclusion from this election.”

The White House has addressed some of the criticism that has followed Trump’s “60 Minutes” interview, hitting back at a post that argued Trump was advocating for an “amnesty deal.”

“Wrong. The word ‘amnesty’ was never even said in this entire exchange,” the White House Rapid Response account on X wrote.

text:
“The legend lives on from the Chippewa on down of the big lake they called Gitche Gumee
The lake, it is said, never gives up her dead when the skies of November turn gloomy…” 

The Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum, located at Whitefish Point in Michigan, is situated approximately 17 miles from where the SS Edmund Fitzgerald sank on November 10, 1975

 The wreck lies in Canadian waters of Lake Superiorat a depth of 530 feet, roughly 17 miles northwest of Whitefish Point and 15–17 miles from the entrance to Whitefish Bay. 

While the museum is the primary site for honoring the 29 crew members lost in the November 10, 1975 disaster, the specific distance often cited in historical accounts and Gordon Lightfoot’s ballad ("The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald") as the point where the ship might have reached safety was 15 miles to the shelter of Whitefish Bay. 

 The museum displays the ship’s recovered 200-pound bronze bell and offers comprehensive exhibits on the tragedy and Great Lakes maritime history

text: The progressive wing of the Democratic Party is gaining ground, and this year's elections offered another sign of its growing influence. In Michigan, progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated establishment-backed Democrat Haley Stevens in the Senate primary. He went on to win the general election against Mike Rogers. El-Sayed campaigned on Medicare for All, higher taxes on the wealthy, and a sharp critique of corporate influence in politics. Progressive candidates also scored victories in other parts of the country, including Democratic socialist Donavan McKinney, who unseated incumbent Congressman Shri Thanedar. These victories reveal a growing divide within the Democratic Party. The question now is whether this increasingly progressive movement will reshape the party's future, or create new challenges for Democrats in competitive elections.

text:
How many stocks does it take to make up half the S&P 500?

In the mid-1990s: more than 60.

Before the 2000 tech bust: about 30.

Today: just 24.

When so few stocks carry so much weight, their moves become the market’s moves, as last week’s AI-led sell-off showed.

See this chart and 17 more warning signs in @elliottwaveintl ’s FREE report:
https://t.co/4K5ccGNaPA

This chart comes from @elliottwaveintl ’s free report, The Most Dangerous Market in History? 18 Flashing Red Signals You Shouldn’t Ignore. Here’s what EWI’s analysts say about it: 

“Narrow market breadth offers another sign of speculation, as investors crowd into a handful of winning stocks. This chart shows that just 5% of S&P 500 stocks account for more than 50% of the index’s total market capitalization. A handful of high-profile tech stocks are driving the market, creating the narrowest concentration in at least 35 years.” 

Last week showed what that means in practice. 

On Thursday, November 5, a sell-off sent the S&P 500 down 4.36%, its worst day since April 2025. 

The Magnificent Seven lost $1 trillion in market value in that single session. 

Meanwhile, the equal-weighted S&P 500, a stand-in for the typical stock, had closed at a record the day before and ended the week roughly where it started. 

Stocks have since bounced back. 
But the takeaway stands: "when a handful of stocks carry this much weight, their moves become the market’s moves, in both directions".

Market concentration is one of 18 charts in the report. 
The others cover record valuations, margin debt, investor sentiment and even housing.

KEY POINTS:
    • Researchers studied the DNA of 2.5 million people to find clues about what causes Fibromyalgia.
    • The study discovered 26 specific spots, in our genes, that are linked to having Fibromyalgia.
    • The findings show that Fibromyalgia is a REAL PHYSICAL DISEASE, and is NOT something people make up.
    • The evidence of this study points directly to the brain & the central nervous system, instead of the immune system; this suggests that Fibromyalgia is not an autoimmune disease like lupus or arthritis (which many Fibromites also often have/develop).
    • Even though the brain is most likely responsible for the pain, it is still VERY REAL, and is NOT something you can just outthink, or cure/treat with “talking therapies” (as the @NHS likes to suggest).
    • The scientists found a LINK to the gene that causes Huntington’s Disease, but this DOES NOT MEAN that patients will get/develop that disease.
    • Men AND women have the SAME genetic risk for Fibromyalgia, even though women are historically DIAGNOSED more often than men.
    • Things like early childhood trauma and/or physical injuries can be major environmental triggers that can wake up these genes.
    • Most of the risk for Fibromyalgia comes from your genes, though there is still a significant aspect of the disease being triggered, that comes from your environment.
    • New genetic discoveries might help drug companies create better treatments for patients in the future; “talking therapies” are not indicated to offer any significant relief beyond general stress management, which anecdotally has been suggested to lessen the intensity and/or frequency of Fibro-flares.
    • Getting an early diagnosis and starting treatment quickly can help people live a normal life, though this is not guaranteed.

text:
Chapter 2: The Orientation Camp Experience
From the very first day of camp, I made a promise to myself that I would participate in as many activities as possible. I wanted to leave the orientation camp with memories I could always look back on with pride.
True to my word, I immersed myself in camp life from the very beginning. I was nominated as the Public Relations Officer (P.R.O.) of my platoon. I also participated in the parade drills but later withdrew because of my involvement in other camp activities.
One of the experiences I cherish the most was forming the Platoon 7 Female Football Team with the help of three other platoon members. It was an exciting challenge because we were determined to build a competitive team within a very short period. Watching the ladies grow in confidence and teamwork was rewarding. Our efforts eventually paid off as Platoon 7 reached the finals of the football competition. Although we lost on penalties, I remained incredibly proud of what we had accomplished together.
My involvement in sports did not end there. I also coached the female volleyball team, and through hard work and determination, we reached the semi-finals. Those moments taught me the importance of  teamwork, and believing in people even when they doubted themselves.
The only camp activities I did not participate in were the NYSC Band, OBS (Orientation Broadcasting Service), and Quarter Guard. Apart from these, I embraced virtually every opportunity that came my way.
Life in the orientation camp was packed with activities from dawn until night. Our days began with the early morning meditation, followed by parade drills. After that came the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme, more drills, and then various sporting activities. As if that wasn't enough, the evenings came alive with OBS night programmes, which included Talent Hunt, cultural dance presentations, inter-platoon singing competitions, welcome parties, and many other entertaining events. Every day presented something new to learn, experience, or enjoy.
One event that stands out in my memory was the Talent Hunt. I decided to use the opportunity to express my passion for comedy. I walked onto the stage and cracked a few jokes. To be honest, I wasn't expecting everyone to laugh. My goal was simply to challenge myself by trying something I had never done before.
Another memorable experience was the cultural dance sessions. During the musical performances, I noticed that the dance floor was often dominated by the Igbo, Hausa, Fulani, Yoruba, and, to some extent, Ibibio and Delta cultural groups. As a proud Rivers man, I felt it was important to ensure that my own culture was represented as well.
I approached the Disc Jockey and requested songs by Duncan Mighty, whose music beautifully represents the culture and spirit of Port Harcourt people and Rivers State. At first, I was worried that the turnout might be poor because I had only just begun getting acquainted with one or two fellow Rivers indigenes in camp. To my surprise, the response was overwhelming. The atmosphere became lively, and seeing people dance to the music from my state filled me with pride.
Beyond the organized activities, camp also gave me the opportunity to meet people from different backgrounds, religions, and cultures. One of those people was my Muslim bunkmate, Musa Hassan. He was a kind and respectful young man who took the time to explain the significance of the Muslim prayer mat and some of the practices associated with Islamic worship. Our conversations helped me appreciate a culture and religion different from mine. It was one of the many lessons in unity that the NYSC orientation camp offered.
One thing that was impossible to ignore in Adamawa State was the weather. The heat was intense. As early as 4:00 a.m., I would wake up to have my bath, yet the water stored in the overhead tank was still warm. @creditveto_afr

President Putin:  Ukraine "is controlled from the outside"

"For many years, Russia has offered peace, cooperation, prosperity and a common future to a newly independent Ukraine. It has chosen confrontation, war, extinction and the compression of borders to the point of collapse..."

Kirill Strelnikov:  "Yesterday, US President Donald Trump said in an interview with CBS that "everything will eventually end with Ukraine having a slightly different form."

It is not surprising that there were various interpretations of his commentary, to which the Kremlin advised to clarify the details with the Trump. But at the same time, it was emphasized that regardless of the subtexts and contexts in terms of geography (that is, the realities on the ground) Ukraine "It's a different country."

It has become "another country" to such an extent that one of the main points on the agenda of the upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi will be the issue of "the security of the region as a whole." And now we are no longer talking about Russia's security from the West or vice versa: now the security of everyone is coming to the fore - from Ukraine.

Russia has long been saying that Nezalezhnaya is steadily turning into a failed state and (literally and figuratively) a black hole on the map of Europe, which will eventually have to be covered with a "stroke" all together, otherwise there will be no quiet life in the region.

The reason for the fall of Ukraine as a state is by no means a military conflict: it only exposed fetid bones and rags under a poorly fitting suit from European Lend-Lease.

Back in February 2022, Vladimir Putin said that Ukraine, in fact, "has never had a stable tradition of its true statehood," since it was originally a political project authored by V. I. Lenin, whose directives "literally squeezed Donbass into Ukraine."

In October of this year, at the plenary session of the Valdai Discussion Club, the president once again outlined the processes that now cannot be ignored by anyone: Ukraine cannot exist independently, it is controlled from the outside and is losing statehood before our eyes.

And Europe's passionate desire to sit on the edge of a chair in the negotiation room is connected, among other things, with the fact that it is scared to death that all the consequences of turning Ukraine into a dead monster will now have to deal with it itself, which, of course, it would very much not want.
But you have to.

A few days ago, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace published an article according to which "Putin's aggression" gave meaning to the Ukrainian project and now "Ukraine is united." It is only necessary to make a clarification: it united beyond the current borders.

Yesterday, the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) released data: in 10-20 years, the population of the territory controlled by Kiev may decrease to just over ten million people, of which only a third will be able-bodied, "which is below the threshold of national survival." In other words, the trick with an independent and prosperous Ukraine failed, thank you all, tickets can be returned at the ticket office.

It would be possible to make allowances for "Kremlin propaganda", but Western sources suddenly gave up and fully confirm what was said above. A special report by The Economist on November 5 titled "War-weary Ukraine faces the risk of demographic collapse" says that in Ukraine in the first half of 2026, the death rate exceeded the birth rate by more than three times, and the population fell to 27-28 million people. And there will never be a U-turn: of the five million Ukrainians who have fled the country, most are children and women under 44 years old (the main demographic segment), and they are not going to return.

Moreover, according to the forecasts of the Institute of the Kyiv School of Economics, after the end of active hostilities, Ukraine will face a new powerful wave of emigration - and at least 600 thousand more people may leave the country.

Against this background, the bewilderment of the experts of the "Ukrainian Institute for the Future" looks very amusing, who in the article "Why Ukraine failed" ask the question: for what reason, with more advantageous starting positions in 1990 compared to Poland (nine thousand dollars per capita in GDP at PPP versus eight thousand), now the same Poland is 2.5 times richer than Nezalezhnaya, and the latter proudly tops the list of the poorest countries in Europe?

However, they themselves give the answer: the problem of the destruction of Ukraine is systemic, not eventual. The change of elites and parties does not transform the basic rules, so after each revolution, the old model is reproduced. In other words, the resorption of this accidental scar on the historical map of the world had to happen sooner or later, and now it will happen rather early. The inhabitants of these territories initially did not understand the meaning of this formation, except for the confrontation with Russia, and now the latter meaning is disappearing.

As Responsible Statecraft wrote, Ukraine will be lucky if, by the grace of Russia, it remains as a state and territory at all: "A victory for Ukraine will be a compromise peace, which (in principle. — Ed. For many years, Russia has offered peace, cooperation, prosperity and a common future to a newly independent Ukraine. It has chosen confrontation, war, extinction and the compression of borders to the point of collapse.

And now Russia is washing its hands of it, because its patience cannot be unlimited."

text:
The next trillion-dollar opportunity in AI may not be building more software. It may be dismantling the silos that made software valuable in the first place.

For 30 years, software companies built moats by controlling applications, data, and distribution. AI challenges that model. When anyone can create software on demand, the scarcity shifts from code to trusted execution, interoperability, and access to proprietary data.

The question I’m asking as an investor: Who captures the value when software becomes abundant but trust remains scarce?

Consider $FSLY.

>> Q3 revenue grew 20% YoY.
>> Security revenue grew 32%.
>> Gross margins expanded 490 basis points.
>> Free cash flow increased 39%.
Net revenue retention improved to 119%.

Yet the stock trades ~54% below its 52-week high at ~3.6x trailing revenue.

That’s an interesting divergence, not proof of undervaluation. Customer concentration is rising, dilution remains material, and a durable competitive advantage in AI infrastructure is far from established.

Compare that with $NET, where Q3 revenue grew 39% and current remaining performance obligations increased 37%.

Two different businesses, but both offer evidence of growing demand for the infrastructure supporting increasingly distributed software.

My hypothesis: As AI reduces the cost of creating applications, economic value may migrate toward companies that make fragmented systems work together securely.

That creates opportunities across identity, cybersecurity, data infrastructure, and developer platforms. It also threatens software businesses whose pricing power depends primarily on controlling access.

The winners won’t necessarily be the companies shipping the most AI features. They’ll be the ones capturing a growing share of the economic value created.

I’m particularly interested in how @Cloudflare, @Fastly, @Okta, @Snowflake, and @Anthropic approach this transition.

The investment edge is identifying improving unit economics before consensus revises its assumptions—not buying a compelling narrative after the stock has already rerated.

Sources: Fastly and Cloudflare Q3 2026 earnings releases; November 9 market data.

https://t.co/oodHGB8ZTO

Stocks made those dependencies easier to see. Two tokens can track the same company while offering different rights. One can represent the share itself. Another can provide price exposure through a third-party instrument.
Both can trade under a recognizable ticker, but the structure behind each token determines what holders own and how they can use it.
https://t.co/zMkAlELQpv

—
● More Issuers, More Venues, More Fragmented Liquidity

As several issuers began offering exposure to the same stocks, liquidity split across wrappers, chains and venues. A familiar ticker could appear in multiple pools without those pools sharing depth.
Aggregators can help traders find the best available route, but different legal claims and redemption terms make it harder to treat every version of a stock as interchangeable.
https://t.co/VwDE3JwRUF

That fragmentation made the design of individual markets more important. On Robinhood Chain, stock tokens paired directly with SPY showed where AMMs could have an edge.
Traders could move between correlated assets without routing every trade through dollars, while LPs could supply two assets they already wanted to hold.
Those pools recorded $33M in volume in 12 days, offering an early example of how tokenization can change the way equities trade.
https://t.co/tKIAJntmOd

Once those markets existed, distribution became a bigger source of advantage. Exchanges had users, wallets had direct access to them, and aggregators could route orders across venues.
As more issuers offered similar exposure, those channels increasingly shaped which stock tokens users encountered and where their trades landed.
https://t.co/OLKfDu8v2g

—
● Trading Proved Demand but Lending Exposed the Gaps.

One snapshot put weekly tokenized-equity spot volume near $3B, while only around 5% of the market was deployed in DeFi. The two figures capture different things. Trading volume shows how much activity passes through a market.
DeFi deployment shows how much equity capital is being put to work in applications such as lending.
Accepting a stock token as collateral raises the bar. A lending protocol needs a reliable price, enough liquidity to liquidate a position, and a clear understanding of what can happen when the underlying stock market is closed or redemption is restricted.
https://t.co/lfPytGRI2z

The SEC framework covered in the series brought the legal side of that distinction into focus. The permissioned AMM pathway applied to qualifying securities that preserve shareholder rights.
Meanwhile, much of the onchain activity was already happening in wrappers built primarily for price exposure. The products drawing trading activity and the products built around shareholder rights were developing along different paths.
https://t.co/cruYeRz6lM

Memecoin pools showed how far those paths could diverge. By pairing memecoins with stock tokens, they gave traders a reason to use equity wrappers even when they came to trade something else.
Across 19 liquid wrappers in the sample, meme-quoted pools held roughly 17.2% of the onchain float. The question is how much of that liquidity can stay once speculative activity fades.
https://t.co/8FiSGbEJWe

—
● Exposure Scaled Faster Than Ownership

Equity perps surpassed $590B in 2026 year-to-date trading volume by the time of the October analysis. That figure measures turnover in derivatives, but it shows how quickly crypto markets can distribute exposure to stocks.
Direct onchain ownership has more pieces to coordinate. Transfer agents and shareholder registers still matter, alongside voting rights, dividends, corporate actions and rules around who can hold or transfer the shares.
https://t.co/thhs0OuV0J

Custody and redemption bring that distinction down to what a holder can actually do. A token can be backed 1:1 while offering limited redemption access or no direct shareholder rights.
Selling on a DEX depends on available liquidity and redeeming through an issuer depends on eligibility, the product’s terms and what the holder can legally claim.
Those two exits can produce very different outcomes when markets are under stress.
https://t.co/0IeFqUW0jF

—
● Where the Market Goes From Here

The first phase of tokenized stocks proved there was demand for equity exposure onchain. It also showed that issuance, distribution, liquidity and ownership can develop at very different speeds.

The next phase depends on whether those pieces can work together. A stock token becomes more useful when it can trade in a deep market, serve as credible collateral and give holders a clear claim they can enforce.

The strongest signal of progress will be how well those markets hold up when the underlying exchange is closed, liquidity is thin and holders need a reliable way out.

text:
Could Type 2 Diabetes Be Reversed? 14-Year Study Reveals Remarkable Results | University of Oklahoma

In a long-term trial, weight-loss surgery led to more type 2 diabetes remissions than intensive medical and lifestyle management, while patients’ disease histories offered clues to who might benefit most.

For some people with type 2 diabetes, keeping blood sugar under control without medication is possible. This state, known as remission, raises a question that could shape years of treatment decisions: Which approaches give people the best chance of reaching it, and what makes it more likely to last?

A long-term study found that 58% of participants assigned to weight-loss surgery achieved remission during follow-up, compared with 3% of those assigned to intensive medical and lifestyle management. Participants were followed for a median of 11 years, with some followed for up to 14 years. Those percentages describe how many people reached remission, rather than how many remained in remission throughout that time.

Researchers analyzed data from 262 people with type 2 diabetes, including 166 assigned to metabolic-bariatric surgery, commonly called weight-loss surgery, and 96 assigned to medical and lifestyle management. They defined remission as an A1C below 6.5% without blood sugar-lowering medication. A1C is a blood test that reflects average blood sugar levels over approximately three months.

The findings were published in Diabetes Care, a journal of the American Diabetes Association®. They come from the Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D), the largest, longest-running trial of metabolic surgery for diabetes. The study’s lead author is Donald Simonson, M.D., MPH, Sc.D., of Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School in Boston.

Diabetes history offers clues to lasting remission

Participants who had lived with diabetes for fewer years, did not use insulin, and took fewer types of blood sugar-lowering medications before treatment were more likely to achieve remission. Greater weight loss during the first year after treatment was also associated with a higher likelihood of remission.

Among people who initially reached remission, diabetes was more likely to return in those who had lived with the disease longer and those who took more types of blood sugar-lowering medications before treatment. Together, these associations suggest that a patient’s diabetes history and response to treatment may help physicians assess both the likelihood of remission and its potential duration.

A case for considering surgery earlier

The study’s principal investigator, John P. Kirwan, Ph.D., was named executive director of the University of Oklahoma Health Harold Hamm Diabetes Center this summer. He also serves as Vice Provost for Diabetes Programs at the University of Oklahoma and holds the Chickasaw Nation Endowed Chair in Diabetes Research.

“For years, one of the most consequential questions in diabetes care has been whether the benefits of metabolic surgery endure,” Kirwan said. “Now we have a durable answer. Over 14 years, 58% of surgical patients achieved remission, compared with just 3% on medication and lifestyle alone. By identifying who is most likely to achieve lasting remission, including shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, and greater early weight loss, we can offer surgery to the right people earlier, rather than as a last resort.”

text:
Donations to the "Popular Politics" Channel Received by Commercial Firm Owned by Leonid Volkov

On the website of FBK's YouTube channel "Popular Politics," viewers are invited to support the channel via Stripe. However, the recipient of the funds is not FBK, but a company called "Digital Duck."

We previously reported on this Lithuanian company back in June 2024: "For instance, at Rugių g. 2, LT-08418 Vilnius, Digital Duck, UAB is registered under the leadership of Yuliana Karlo. The company is notable for its history—it was founded and headed by Leonid Volkov in 2021 after his move to Lithuania."

It is worth noting that Karlo appears to be a nominee: her cleaning services firm with a single employee is registered at the exact same address.

A query sent to the Lithuanian Centre of Registers regarding the founders of Digital Duck showed that Leonid Volkov has been the sole founder of this commercial organization since its inception.

Thus, the company has no legal right to accept donations: it must register them either as a gift via a public offer on its website or as a sale of information services. However, when selecting a "one-time donation," the viewer buys nothing, while the Stripe payment form specifies the purpose of payment as a "Donation to the 'Popular Politics' channel"—albeit in favor of Digital Duck.

The company has its own website—https://t.co/fmeoqBNDPQ. The main page displays an English placeholder asserting that Digital Duck is a service for streamers that allows viewers to launch visual effects and floating ducks across the screen ("Ducks floating across the screen FTW!"). FBK and Volkov are not mentioned anywhere.

In the privacy policy at https://t.co/uYSK3f3E08, it is stated that the site's administrator is that exact same Vilnius-based UAB Digital Duck, but there is no public offer. It should be added that logging in on the "Duck" site via a Google account is impossible: the website has allegedly been in closed beta testing for years.

Consequently, all donations to the "Popular Politics" channel are received by a firm solely owned by Leonid Volkov. At the same time, it remains unclear on what legal grounds Digital Duck accepts donations for the activities of "Popular Politics" and how it subsequently disposes of the funds received. When making a one-time donation, the viewer acquires no distinct product or service, while the commercial company Digital Duck is listed as the recipient on the Stripe payment form.

As a reminder, according to Volkov, FBK spent €2 million from donations at the beginning of the war to launch "Popular Politics." Leonid Volkov.

text:
Every big connectome ends with the same chore. The segmentation has glued two neurons together, a proofreader clicks near the bad join, and the software has to decide where to cut. A new arXiv preprint from Notre Dame and Korea University looks hard at that step.

Byunghyun Ko, Won-Ki Jeong and Chaoli Wang call their method ContactCut. Their point is that a click doesn't define the split on its own. The segmentation is stored as a graph of supervoxels, and every place where two supervoxels share voxel faces is a contact. Within 500 nm of the click there are usually several contacts that could act as the two seeds for a min-cut, and each gives a different split of the whole object, even with the same solver.

So instead of seeding at the nearest contact, ContactCut tries every nearby contact, runs a seeded minimum cut on the full graph for each one, and scores the resulting partitions. The scoring looks only at structure, never at the EM images. It prefers splits where both sides stay in one connected piece, where the smaller side isn't a tiny crumb, and where the cut runs through a narrow connection. A ranker with two learned weights balances the last two. A second mode tries pairs of contacts and offers a proofreader five alternatives.

They tested it on real edits that proofreaders made in MICrONS minnie65 (mouse visual cortex) and FlyWire (adult fly brain). On 733 MICrONS test edits the main score was 0.657, against 0.598 for the best graph-based method and 0.532 for the best learned one. On 2,929 FlyWire edits it scored 0.641, against 0.608 and 0.541. A ranker trained only on MICrONS scored 0.6405 on FlyWire, almost the same as 0.6414 when trained on FlyWire itself. It runs on a CPU, with a median of 0.30 s per edit on MICrONS and 0.11 s on FlyWire.

It matters because false merges are the expensive error. One wrong fusion corrupts the shape and wiring of several neurons.

There are limits. The reference is the edit people actually made, so this measures agreement with past proofreading, not verified neuron identity. It only handles two-way splits. A score around 0.65 still leaves plenty for a human to check, and the best single-contact cut available scores 0.843 on MICrONS, so the ranker doesn't yet find the best option every time. It's also a preprint, not yet peer reviewed.

The part I like most is that it ignores the images completely. It works on the shape of the supervoxel graph alone, which is probably why a model trained on mouse cortex carries over to the fly brain with almost no loss. The flip side is that the fix can only be as good as the supervoxels. If a section is damaged or misaligned there may be no clean contact to cut through. Clean, evenly cut volumes at acquisition still save time later.

Ref: Ko, Jeong and Wang (2026), "ContactCut: A Partition-Aware Contact Selection Framework for False-Merge Correction in Connectomics", arXiv:2611.01457. https://t.co/ljlKnxoeBa Code: https://t.co/6QmwAH93e7

text:
Tappers career accolades:
The Biden Cover-Up Cash-Out Special. For years Tapper treated visible cognitive decline as “just a stutter” or “cheap fakes.” He shut down Lara Trump in 2020 for suggesting decline (“you have absolutely no standing to diagnose”), insisted Biden was sharp, and soft-pedaled the freezes, wanderings, and word salads. Then, once Biden was out, he co-authored Original Sin documenting the “cover-up” by family and aides and went on a book tour about how the White House lied to everyone—including, apparently, the guy with the best access and the loudest platform. Admits some criticism is fair and that he “didn’t cover it enough.” Translation: he noticed when the market for the book opened.⁠Fox News⁠Fox News⁠Fox News
Hunter Biden Laptop: Too Gross to Mention (Until It Wasn’t). In October 2020 he waved off the laptop story on air as right-wing allegations “too disgusting to even repeat here.” Later he called Republicans “cynical” for arguing Big Tech suppression affected the election. The same guy who later described Hunter as “provably, demonstrably unethical, sleazy and prone to horrible decisions” somehow couldn’t bring himself to examine the evidence when it mattered most. Classic timing.⁠Fox News
Russiagate Enthusiast Who Later Discovered Nuance. CNN was all-in on the collusion narrative for years. Tapper was part of the ecosystem. When the Durham report landed and the whole thing looked thinner, he offered a carefully hedged “to a degree, it does exonerate” line that still managed to draw both sides’ fire. The selective skepticism arrived right on schedule.
Defamation Irony. His show ran a segment that led to a successful (or settled) defamation claim by a Navy veteran security contractor over Afghanistan-exit reporting that painted him as an illegal profiteer. Meanwhile Tapper had previously lectured about Fox’s Dominion settlement and media organizations that prioritize audience over truth being “a cancer on democracy.” The hypocrisy writes itself.⁠Washingtonexaminer⁠Newsweek
The Book’s Extra Spice. Updated editions and excerpts claim Biden sometimes appeared to think his son Beau (who died in 2015) was still alive and fighting cancer, and forgot Bob Dole was dead despite having eulogized him. Biden’s team called the claims character-destroying profiteering. Whether the anecdotes hold or not, the pattern is clear: once the political utility of the story flips, Tapper’s memory and scrutiny improve dramatically.⁠Thedailybeast
Bonus: Both-Sides-When-Convenient, Outrage-When-Profitable. He’ll aggressively fact-check or interrupt one side while giving the other more airtime and softer framing, then pivot to “I’m just a journalist asking questions” when the receipts come out. The glasses and earnest tone do a lot of heavy lifting.
Tapper isn’t uniquely evil; he’s a highly successful product of a media ecosystem that rewards narrative alignment until the narrative becomes a liability, at which point the book deal and the “we were lied to” tour appear. The deeds are mostly selective blindness, convenient amnesia, and excellent timing for monetizing the correction. Roast complete.

text: I appreciate the good-faith argument, and I'm not dismissing harm reduction as a legitimate consideration. But lesser-evilism cannot become an unconditional, uncritical obligation to support whichever candidate the duopoly offers. AOC's record on Palestine is not automatically superior to that of third-party and independent candidates who've articulated considerably firmer anti-Zionist and antiwar positions. Nor should electoral viability substitute for principled accountability. Our two-party system is sustained by structural incentives, including winner-take-all elections, ballot-access barriers, and the Electoral College; that's an institutional design problem, not a moral failing of voters who refuse to compromise their convictions. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, currently backed by states holding 222 electoral votes, could substantially change presidential electoral incentives once it reaches 270 (easily doable with approval from even a couple of these swing states: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Arizona, Wisconsin, Nevada), although further reforms would still be necessary. We are fully entitled to demand that elected officials oppose genocide, military complicity, and violations of Palestinian rights without being accused of enabling some hypothetical greater evil. The purpose of political representation is accountability to constituents, not perpetual absolution through comparison with someone worse. Two years is ample time to demand substantive changes rather than offer unconditional endorsements in advance. Frankly, I remain deeply skeptical that AOC will make the changes necessary to satisfy principled anti-Zionist objections. Her affirmative vote on H.Res. 888, her endorsements of Biden and Harris amid Gaza's devastation, and her accommodations with Democratic Party leadership have already damaged that trust. Her April 2026 pledge to oppose all future military aid to Israel is a welcome change in stated policy, but promises must be tested against congressional votes and political conduct. No candidate's advisers, donors, party relationships, or presidential ambitions should insulate them from that scrutiny. Until her record meets the standards being demanded, withholding an endorsement remains a legitimate exercise of political conscience.

text:
Trade deadline at 4 p.m. Quick check on the #Jets, who could make a minor move or two. 

Players with expiring contracts are the most likely to get dealt. (See: Andre Cisco to Lions). CB Nahshon Wright (no role on defense) and WR Tim Patrick (healthy scratch last two games) are the names to watch.

ED Will McDonald is the most intriguing name. Frustrated with PT, he wants out. He's had multiple conversations with coaches, as recently as yesterday. He's only 27, with 24.5 sacks in 56 games, signed through 2027 -- so there's value (hearing Day-2 pick value). Would be hard to turn that down, no? GM Darren Mougey really likes McDonald. Perhaps waiting for coaching dust to settle in offseason before making a move, so unlikely to be dealt today.

NB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. appears to have lost job to rookie D'Angelo Ponds, making him expendable. He's signed through '27 for minimum salary, so there's no urgency to move him unless the offer makes sense.

Clark first became involved in the school choice movement after her oldest son was evaluated for dyslexia and she learned her local school district didn’t offer any special programs for such students.

“I found out about the state’s ESA program,” which provides parents with funding to customize their child’s education, Clark said. “I thought, this program is so amazing, it’s so incredible. More families need to have access to an ESA.”

TO THE JOURNALISTS WHO ARE BETRAYING THE TRUTH — THE SPINNING WHEEL MUST STOP!

The pattern of creating a circular motion where nobody gets anything done needs to stop.

Broadcasting as we know it is over. Simply giving people updates is no longer enough. Artificial intelligence will increasingly do that work.

So what are human beings going to do?

Are we going to spend the rest of our lives listening to one human being summarize information for another human being? Or are we finally going to build systems where people can engage, communicate, participate, and hold those in power accountable?

I am building the World's Inbox.

I have asked journalists many times to support the truth. I have asked you to participate. I have asked you to recognize that journalism needs to be redesigned.

And I have been met with silence.

I write to you again.

To environmental activists like Greta Thunberg, to journalists, to human rights advocates, and to everyone claiming to fight for a better future:

THE TRUTH IS THE FOUNDATION EVERYTHING IS BUILT ON.

Remember those words.

If the future is not built on truth, everything you are working toward will eventually collapse. Corruption will prevail. Those who manipulate information will gain power, and the people you claim to defend will continue to suffer.

You cannot build a better world on misinformation, manipulation, and endless political spin.

If you want to continue participating in the social media circus, where engagement matters more than accountability, you are free to do so.

But don't confuse that with building the future.

The spinning wheel has always served those who hold power. Journalism was supposed to hold those people accountable, not become part of the wheel.

I am building institutions. I am designing a News Desk where citizens can engage, where artificial intelligence can help organize information, where questions can be answered, and where the record of accountability cannot simply disappear beneath another breaking-news headline.

And I am beginning to realize that I may have to build the foundation myself, without your participation.

Because too many of you appear to have surrendered to the very system you were supposed to challenge.

If there is anything left of your commitment to truth, contact me.

I am not going to spend my life begging journalists to participate in making a difference.

You are the journalists.

You are supposed to investigate.

You are supposed to question power.

You are supposed to defend the truth.

And you are supposed to recognize when the institutions you work within are failing humanity.

I have invited you to participate. I have received no meaningful engagement from those I have approached.

That is what my record shows. And that record will be preserved.

Remember something else: power changes hands.

The people controlling today's institutions will not control them forever.

And when that day comes, the historical record will matter.

Who defended the truth?

Who challenged the system?

Who offered solutions?

Who participated?

And who remained silent?

You are doing a remarkable job ignoring my invitations.

Keep spinning if that is what you choose.

But understand that the world cannot afford another generation of journalism that reports every failure while helping accomplish so little to correct it.

We are being taken toward a future where everybody is informed, everybody is distracted, and nobody is accountable.

I refuse to accept that future.

The World's Inbox is being built. The News Desk is being redesigned. And the truth will remain the foundation.

The invitation remains open. The responsibility is yours.

text:
In March 2010, the man widely credited with discovering PSA wrote in the New York Times that the test built on it had become "a hugely expensive public health disaster."

His name is Richard Ablin. He says he identified the protein in 1970. A cancer center in Buffalo says its own lab found the version the test actually uses, and it was the center granted the 1984 patent. Science has paternity disputes too.

Either way, by 1994 the FDA had approved the test for screening, and millions of men were getting it every year.

Ablin's complaint was simple. The test measures a protein, not a cancer. Infection, an enlarged prostate, even a long bike ride can push it up. And it can't tell the slow cancer that will never bother you from the fast one that will kill you.

So men got biopsies they didn't need. Then surgery on cancers that would never have touched them. Some lost continence. Some lost erections.

He was right about that part. Most of the harm came after the test.

But he was writing in 2010, and the big trials were young. Prostate cancer is slow. A death prevented at 58 might have come at 75. Short studies couldn't see it.

So the men in those trials were followed. And followed.

In May 2026, Cochrane, the group that had reviewed PSA screening in 2006, 2010 and 2013 and found too little proof each time, looked again. Six trials. Nearly 800,000 men. The largest followed for 23 years.

The answer flipped. Screening likely reduces prostate cancer deaths. About 2 fewer for every 1,000 men, roughly 500 invited per death prevented. Modest. Real.

And the harm got smaller while the trials ran. Today many low-grade cancers are watched, not cut. An MRI can come before a biopsy. In the ProtecT trial, about 97% of men with PSA-found cancer had not died of it at 15 years, monitored or treated. Monitoring carries a higher chance of spread, so it's a choice to weigh, not a free pass.

Brother, here's what that means for you:

— Baseline PSA can be offered at 45 to 50. Black ancestry, a father or brother with it, or a known gene mutation: 40 to 45.

— 48 hours before the draw: no ejaculation, no long bike rides.

— On finasteride or dutasteride? Your PSA reads about half of what it otherwise would. Tell your doctor.

— One high number means repeat the test, not panic.

— Still high? Ask about an MRI before a biopsy, and whether monitoring fits.

— Blood in urine or semen, new bone pain, unexplained weight loss: this week. Can't urinate, leg weakness, lost bladder or bowel control: ER today.

No food, supplement or workout is proven to prevent prostate cancer.

The man credited with finding the protein called the test a disaster. Twenty-three years of follow-up gave it a second hearing.

Educational only. Not medical advice, and not intended to diagnose or treat any disease. Guidelines differ; screening is a decision to make with your own doctor.

text:
Last spring, a hotel in Charleston, South Carolina, paid a Japanese woman a lot of money to teach their staff Japanese hospitality.

That woman is my friend's mother, Mrs. Hanada. She has trained hotel staff in omotenashi for 31 years. She can tell how deep you bowed by looking at the back of your jacket.

Omotenashi is the Japanese art of hospitality. You take care of a guest before they ask. Quietly. Perfectly. Invisibly.

She went to Charleston for twelve weeks to teach it.

She brought home a photocopy of something she says she was not supposed to see. The staff's guest notes. A three-ring binder behind the front desk, handwritten by everyone from the general manager to the bellman.

In Japan, guest notes look like this: "Prefers firm pillow. Allergic to buckwheat."

In Charleston, they look like this.

"Room 412. Mr. and Mrs. Pinckney. 40th anniversary. She loves lilies. LAST YEAR HE FORGOT. Do not let him forget. (He has been told. He has been told twice.)"

"Room 207. Honeymooners. Fighting already. Send up coconut cake. Cake has never failed us."

"Room 501. Gentleman from New Jersey. He is in a hurry. Everyone walk slower. It's for his own good."

"Room 105. Little boy, six, carrying his first fishing pole. Doormen: ask him what he caught. He caught nothing. Ask anyway. Make it sound like you heard it was a big one."

"Room 220. Mr. Okafor. In town for his daughter's graduation from The Citadel. Say congratulations every time you see him. He will cry. Let him."

"Room 318. In town for her mama's funeral. Front desk: do NOT ask how her stay is. Ask how she's holding up. Hug offered, never assumed."

"Dining room, table 6, every Thursday since 1974: Mr. and Mrs. Gaillard. Mr. Gaillard passed in March. She still comes. We still set two glasses. She has not asked us to stop. We will not be the ones to stop."

Mrs. Hanada read that one standing at the front desk. In 31 years, no hotel staff had ever seen her face slip. That afternoon, the whole front desk did.

Then she turned the page.

"Guest from Japan, here to teach us. She bows at us. Nobody knows what it means. Bow back anyway. Bow LOWER than her. Rhett, that is too low. Rhett, get up."

She kept turning.

"Week 1. Mrs. Hanada skips lunch. Kitchen, send a plate to the training room. Say it was extra. It was not extra."

"Week 3. Mrs. H is homesick. Bernice says her mama in Japan is 88. Phone charger at the front desk is broken. Reggie, buy her a new one and say it was in lost and found."

"Week 7. Her birthday is Thursday. She hasn't told a soul. Reggie found it on her paperwork. Asked Mrs. Gaillard. Mrs. Gaillard says she can have the second glass."

On her birthday, Mrs. Hanada sat at table 6. Across from a 79-year-old widow. In Mr. Gaillard's chair.

Her whole career, she has taught one rule above all others: staff never sit down with a guest.

Mrs. Gaillard ordered for both of them, told her about every Thursday since 1974, and patted her hand over dessert like she'd known her for fifty years.

The last entry is from her last day.

"Mrs. Hanada leaves Friday. She taught us everything. Nobody tell her we've been doing it to her since the airport. She'll cry. One more bow. Lower than hers. Rhett, get up."

She did cry. At the airport. In front of the entire front desk, who had come in uniform.

Omotenashi means you care for a guest before they ask.

She flew 7,000 miles to teach it.

In Charleston, nobody had ever heard the word. They just call it being raised right.

She taught them how to bow.

They taught her how to sit down.

(Back in Tokyo, she has added one new rule to her training: "If a guest is sad, send up cake." Japanese hotels do not keep cake on hand for this. She is working on it.)
