Why Architects Trust Premium Wood Brands for Signature Projects
Benjamin Baker📷
a few seconds ago
9 min read
A beautiful detail can fail fast when the material behind it is inconsistent. A rainscreen wall, a tight soffit, a shaded deck, or a long run of vertical siding only looks effortless when every board behaves the way the drawings assume it will.That is why premium wood brands matter on signature projects. They help close the gap between design intent and field reality. For architects working on modern homes, hospitality spaces, mixed-use projects, and civic buildings, the material package is not a finish selection made at the end. It is part of the architecture.Premium brands bring tighter grading, clearer documentation, more predictable availability, and better technical support. Those factors become even more valuable in places with demanding climate conditions, including Texas, where heat, sun, humidity, wind-driven rain, and sharp seasonal shifts can expose weak product choices.📷Premium wood performs best when the material choice supports the architectural detail.Premium wood protects the design intent
Architect-led projects often depend on restraint. A wall plane may be simple. A deck may be flush with the interior floor. A soffit may turn down and continue as siding. Those moves leave little room for poor material behavior.Commodity lumber can work well for many uses, but it is often not consistent enough for high-visibility architectural details. Variations in grain, moisture content, milling, and grading can turn a crisp elevation into a patchwork. The issue is not only appearance. Movement, checking, cupping, and inconsistent fastening can create callbacks and change orders.Premium wood brands reduce that risk by giving specifiers more control. The best suppliers document what the product is, how it should be installed, and where it performs best. That allows the design team to specify with more confidence.A strong premium product package usually provides:Consistent gradingBoards arrive closer to the expected appearance, grain pattern, and defect allowance.
Reliable millingProfiles, dimensions, and edges match the detail set more closely.Performance guidanceInstallation requirements help the contractor protect the product in real conditions.
Better finish compatibilityClearer recommendations reduce finish failures and uneven https://t.co/De5JnzQPRo coordinationA dependable source helps avoid last-minute substitutions that weaken the design.The value is simple. The material behaves more like the drawing.Texas projects make material discipline more important
Texas construction asks a lot from exterior materials. The challenge changes by region. A Gulf Coast project may face salt air and heavy moisture. A Hill Country home may deal with intense sun, temperature swings, and wind-driven rain. North Texas can see freeze-thaw cycles, hail exposure, and long dry spells. Central Texas work often combines heat, UV exposure, pollen, dust, and sudden storms.Wood can perform beautifully in these conditions, but it has to be chosen and detailed with discipline. Species, grain orientation, drying method, coating, ventilation, and fastening all affect long-term results.This is why architects often look beyond the nearest lumber rack. They need a partner who understands the region, not only the product catalog. They need to know whether a board is appropriate for a shaded rainscreen, a full-sun deck, an exposed ceiling, or a protected entry.The common problems are familiar:The specified product is not stocked locally.
The available substitute has a different grain, color, or movement profile.
Lead times do not match the construction schedule.
The installer receives boards without clear handling or fastening guidance.
The finish system is selected too late.
The owner expects a uniform appearance from a material that will naturally weather.On a standard project, those issues are frustrating. On a signature project, they can damage the architecture.Honest material expression depends on predictable products
Many contemporary Texas buildings draw from regional modernism. The architecture often favors shade, natural ventilation, simple forms, stone, metal, glass, and wood that looks like wood. In that context, material honesty is not a slogan. It is a design method.If a wall is clad in cedar, the grain, color, and shadow lines are visible. If a ceiling is lined in hemlock, the surface carries the room. If a deck wraps a pool courtyard, every board becomes part of the daily experience of the home.That kind of architecture rewards authentic materials, but it also exposes every inconsistency.Premium products support this approach because they are designed for repeatable results. The goal is not to erase the natural character of wood. The goal is to select character intentionally. Clear grain cedar, vertical grain hemlock, thermally modified boards, and high-quality engineered decking each create a different architectural effect.The right choice depends on what the detail is meant to do.ApplicationMaterial priorityWhy it mattersVertical sidingStable grain and clean profilesLong elevations reveal movement and mismatched boardsSoffits and ceilingsConsistent color and straightnessOverhead surfaces catch light across the full board lengthDeckingSurface durability and slip-conscious detailingFoot traffic, sun, and moisture stress the material dailyRainscreen claddingVentilation and fastening guidanceBackside drying helps protect the assemblyEntry accentsVisual grade and finish qualityHigh-touch areas shape first impressionsArbor Wood and TimberTech solve different architectural needs
Premium brands are not interchangeable. Each one fits a different design problem. That is why architects often compare natural wood, modified wood, and engineered alternatives early in the specification process.Arbor Wood and TimberTech, for example, serve different parts of the material conversation. Arbor Wood is often considered when the project calls for the warmth, grain, and authenticity of real wood. TimberTech is often selected when the design requires a high-performance decking or exterior surface with lower maintenance expectations than many traditional wood options.Both can belong in a serious architectural specification, as long as each is used for the right reason.Arbor Wood supports natural grain and refined detail
Architects choose premium natural wood when the material itself is central to the design. Vertical grain cedar and hemlock can bring quiet texture to a modern façade, especially when paired with stone, steel, concrete, or large areas of glass.Vertical grain material is valued because the grain pattern tends to appear straighter and more consistent than flat grain boards. It can also offer better dimensional behavior in certain applications when properly detailed, dried, finished, and installed.Clear grain cedar is often used where warmth and visual clarity matter. Hemlock can offer a lighter, more subtle appearance, which works well for ceilings, soffits, and clean interior-exterior transitions. The appeal is not that every board looks identical. The appeal is that the variation feels controlled and intentional.A good premium wood partner should help answer questions such as:Which profile best supports drainage and drying?
Should the boards be factory finished or site finished?
What fastener type and spacing does the product require?
How should the material be stored before installation?
What level of color variation should the owner expect over time?Those questions can decide whether a wood detail ages gracefully or becomes a maintenance problem.TimberTech supports performance where exposure is high
There are places where natural wood may not be the best fit for the owner’s expectations. A full-sun pool deck, a hospitality terrace, or a heavily used outdoor living area may call for a more controlled surface.Engineered decking products can help when durability, color retention, and maintenance planning are central to the project. TimberTech products, like other high-quality capped composite or PVC options, are often chosen for decks, stairs, and exterior living areas where predictable performance matters.The design decision should still be architectural. Board width, color, texture, edge detail, fascia treatment, and fastening method all affect the final result. An engineered board can look refined when it is detailed with the same care as stone or millwork. It can also look generic if it is treated as an afterthought.The best outcomes happen when the decking system is selected before the details are complete, not after framing has started.📷Side-by-side samples make grain, color, and profile decisions easier to judge before construction.A reliable material partner reduces change orders
Architects do not only specify materials. They manage risk. The wrong material source can create problems long after the drawings are issued.A local yard may have general framing lumber and commodity boards, but not the grade, profile, or quantity that a custom project requires. A national supplier may offer the product, but lack understanding of Texas exposure conditions, local installation habits, or the urgency of a custom home schedule.The ideal partner sits between those extremes. They can source premium brands, confirm lead times, coordinate quantities, explain product limitations, and help the builder protect the material on site.That matters because many wood-related failures begin before installation.Boards may sit uncovered in the sun. Bundles may absorb moisture from the ground. Factory ends may be cut and left unsealed. A rainscreen may be value engineered out of the assembly. A stain may be applied before the wood is ready. Each choice can weaken the result.A strong material partner helps prevent those failures by supporting the project team early. They do not replace the architect’s specifications or the contractor’s responsibility, but they make both easier to execute.Specification clarity is the difference between premium and expensive
A product is not premium simply because it costs more. It becomes premium when it supports the project’s design, performance, and maintenance goals.That distinction matters. An expensive board used in the wrong exposure can still fail. A beautiful species with the wrong finish can disappoint the owner. A high-performance deck board with a poorly resolved edge can weaken the architecture.Clear specifications help avoid those outcomes. A strong exterior wood or decking specification should identify:Species or product line
Grade and grain orientation
Profile and dimensions
Finish type and number of coated sides
Fastener type, spacing, and exposure
Ventilation or rainscreen requirements
Storage and acclimation instructions
Mockup requirements
Approved substitution process
Maintenance expectationsMockups deserve special attention. A small physical mockup can reveal color variation, shadow lines, fastener visibility, and finish appearance before the full order arrives. For high-end residential and commercial work, that early review can save weeks of conflict.Different species carry different design signals
Wood selection is also a language. Cedar suggests warmth and regional familiarity. Hemlock can feel quiet and refined. Redwood carries a distinct color tradition in exterior architecture. Douglas fir can feel structural and direct. Ipe suggests density and durability, though it requires careful sourcing and detailing. Pine can be useful, but it needs the right treatment and expectations.A single project might compare trex, Texas cedar, pine, redwood, doug fir, ipe, and hemlock before the final choice becomes clear. The right answer is rarely based on appearance alone. Availability, sustainability goals, exposure, budget, finish strategy, and owner maintenance tolerance all shape the decision.Architects build better specifications when they ask three questions early:What should the material look like on day one?
What should it look like in three years?
Who will maintain it, and how often?The third question is often the most important. Some owners love the idea of natural weathering. Others expect a stable color with minimal intervention. Both goals can be valid, but they lead to different products.Premium brands support better conversations with owners
Signature projects succeed when expectations are clear. Materials like wood change with light, age, moisture, and use. Premium brands do not remove that reality. They make it easier to explain and manage.Owners respond well to tangible comparisons. A sample board, a finish mockup, and a simple maintenance plan can do more than a long written disclaimer. When the material source can provide consistent samples and product guidance, the architect has a stronger basis for discussion.This also helps during construction. If a substitution is proposed, the team can compare it against documented criteria instead of relying on a vague claim that another product is “similar.” Similar color is not enough. Similar performance, profile, grade, fastening, warranty coverage, and availability all matter.That level of control protects the owner’s investment and the architect’s design.The best specifications start before the finish schedule
Wood decisions should not wait until the finish schedule is nearly complete. They affect wall assemblies, framing depth, waterproofing, deck structure, transitions, flashing, and maintenance access.Early coordination helps answer practical questions:Does the cladding need a ventilated cavity?
Will the deck framing accept the selected fastening system?
Do doors and thresholds account for board thickness?
Are corner details designed for the actual profile?
Can replacement boards be sourced later?
Does the finish strategy match the construction sequence?When these items are resolved early, the finished project feels calm and intentional. When they are pushed late, the field team is forced to improvise.Premium wood brands give architects better raw material, but the result still depends on detailing. The brand is the starting point. The assembly is the https://t.co/2O9pWIVeiO comes from fewer surprises
Architects trust premium wood brands because they reduce uncertainty where it matters most. They help preserve clean lines, support honest material expression, and give the project team reliable information before construction begins.For signature work, that reliability is worth as much as the visual quality. A beautiful board is only successful if it arrives on time, matches the specification, accepts the finish, works with the detail, and performs in the climate where it is installed.The takeaway is simple. Specify wood as part of the building system, not as decoration. Choose brands and material partners that can support the demands of the design, the site, and the owner’s expectations. That is how premium wood becomes more than a finish. It becomes part of the project’s lasting character.

Europe’s Defence Transformation: Ukraine’s Technology – New Military Alliances and the Industrial Architecture of European Security 
Europe is entering a structural transformation of its defence architecture. The central development is not simply higher military expenditure, but the emerging integration of Ukrainian combat-tested innovation, European industrial production, NATO operational requirements and EU financial instruments into an interconnected system of military development and production.

The emerging Poland–Ukraine counter-drone arrangement illustrates a wider transition: Ukraine is becoming a defence technology provider, industrial partner and source of operational expertise, rather than solely a recipient of military equipment.

This transformation is supported by several documented developments:

NATO’s 5% GDP commitment by 2035, comprising at least 3.5% for core defence and up to 1.5% for wider defence- and security-related expenditure.
EU SAFE financing of up to €150 billion, intended to accelerate defence procurement and industrial production.
Four EU defence flagships: European Drone Defence Initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, European Air Shield and European Space Shield.
United Kingdom–Ukraine cooperation: licensed production of Ukrainian interceptor drones, integrated with British manufacturing and development capabilities.
Germany–Ukraine cooperation: arrangements concerning joint development and production of the Anubis and Seth-X drone systems.
Sweden–Ukraine cooperation: industrial co-production, technology exchange and a proposed acquisition of up to 20 Gripen E/F aircraft, potentially accompanied by donations of up to 16 Gripen C/D aircraft.
NATO Eastern Sentry: strengthened multinational air defence, surveillance and coordination following Russian incursions into Allied airspace in September 2025.
The principal strategic judgment is that Europe is moving from predominantly national defence procurement towards a network of overlapping bilateral industrial partnerships, multinational capability coalitions and common European financing mechanisms. These structures may increase production and military adaptability, but they do not yet constitute a unified European defence-industrial system.

The decisive uncertainty is whether governments can convert political agreements, technology-sharing arrangements and financial commitments into operationally interoperable systems, sustainable manufacturing volumes and resilient supply chains before the evolving threat outpaces European deployment.

Europe’s Defence Transformation: Why Military Spending Alone Will Not Deliver Industrial Sovereignty
Europe is committing hundreds of billions to defence while its military-industrial system remains divided by national procurement, foreign technology dependencies and unequal production capacity. The decisive question is whether this expenditure will create a sustainable European security architecture or finance another generation of fragmented national capabilities.

The contradiction has become sharper with Ukraine’s emergence as a supplier of combat-developed technologies rather than merely a recipient of military assistance. Poland’s proposed exchange of MiG-29 aircraft for Ukrainian counter-drone expertise illustrates a wider transformation involving Germany, France, Italy, the United Kingdom and the Nordic–Baltic countries. NATO is setting higher investment requirements, the European Union is expanding financial instruments, and bilateral agreements are multiplying. Yet political commitments, industrial contracts and operational readiness remain three different realities. Europe’s security, public finances and manufacturing competitiveness will increasingly depend on whether governments can connect them.

More Money, but Not Yet a Common Defence Economy
The scale of Europe’s financial commitment is considerable. According to the European Defence Agency, EU defence expenditure reached €418 billion in 2025, with €454 billion projected for 2026. Equipment procurement amounted to €115 billion in 2025, yet collaborative procurement represented only 24% of equipment expenditure. The figures reveal the central weakness: expenditure is expanding faster than the institutional mechanisms required to consolidate industrial demand.

NATO’s June 2025 Hague Summit established a separate commitment to invest 5% of GDP annually by 2035, comprising at least 3.5% for core defence and up to 1.5% for broader security-related expenditure. The European Union’s Security Action for Europe instrument, SAFE, provides up to €150 billion in EU-backed loans, while the European Defence Industry Programme, EDIP, establishes €1.5 billion in grants for 2025–2027, including €300 million dedicated to supporting Ukraine’s defence-industrial integration.

These instruments serve different purposes and cannot be combined into a single spending total. NATO establishes national investment commitments; SAFE offers repayable financing; EDIP provides targeted industrial support. Their economic effectiveness depends on national procurement decisions, contract execution and the ability of manufacturers to expand production. Financial authorisation is not manufacturing capacity, and manufacturing capacity is not military availability.

The immediate fiscal tension concerns how governments allocate expenditure between personnel, equipment, infrastructure, technological development and industrial expansion. Purchasing established foreign systems may address urgent capability gaps, while investment in European production can require longer contractual commitments and additional industrial expenditure. The balance determines whether higher defence budgets strengthen European manufacturing or deepen dependence on external suppliers.

Ukraine Is Changing the Economics of Technology Transfer
Ukraine’s defence-industrial relationships are increasingly structured around reciprocal technological exchange. The significance lies in the transfer of engineering knowledge, manufacturing rights, operational information and technical adaptation capabilities, rather than exclusively in the delivery of equipment.

The United Kingdom’s cooperation with Ukraine illustrates this change. A September 2025 technology-sharing announcement identified the Ukrainian-designed Octopus interceptor as an initial project, with a stated ambition to manufacture thousands of systems monthly. In January 2026, the British government reported that Octopus cost less than 10% of the drone it was intended to destroy and described design modifications occurring approximately every six weeks. The March 2026 industrial declaration subsequently incorporated licensed production and the broader Lyra programme, connecting unmanned systems, air defence and advanced weapons development.

These official claims are commercially and operationally significant, but production targets and reported cost advantages do not establish audited output or combat performance. The economic value of interception depends on the complete defensive system: sensors, communications, operators, maintenance, ammunition expenditure and the consequences of failure. A low-cost interceptor without reliable detection and command integration cannot resolve the wider problem of defending critical infrastructure against repeated attacks.

Germany’s 14 April 2026 strategic partnership with Ukraine identified joint-production arrangements involving the Anubis long-range and Seth-X mid-range unmanned systems. Norway signed its first Build with Ukraine production arrangements on 27 April 2026, while Lithuania announced cooperation involving the SkyFortress acoustic detection system and a proposed industrial venture between Pekkla UAB and December One RND Ltd, targeting production in 2027.

Poland’s proposed arrangement adds another dimension. Deputy Minister of National Defence Cezary Tomczyk announced in November 2026 that negotiations concerning two additional MiG-29 aircraft and Ukrainian counter-drone technologies were approaching completion. The industrial importance depends on whether Warsaw receives finished equipment, technical documentation, software, manufacturing rights or broader development capabilities. Final contractual provisions and completed technology transfers remain outside the established record.

Ukraine’s emerging value to European defence is therefore not confined to what it manufactures. It also concerns how rapidly its operational experience can be converted into industrial designs that European companies can reproduce, modify and sustain.

Europe’s Industrial Sovereignty Is Limited by Contracts, Components and National Interests
European defence production remains organised around national industrial capabilities and multinational programmes whose interests do not always coincide. Germany contributes substantial engineering, ground-systems, ammunition and air-defence capabilities. France maintains advanced combat aviation, missile and systems-integration industries. Italy contributes aerospace, electronics, radar, naval technologies and complex weapons through companies including Leonardo, Fincantieri and multinational industrial structures such as MBDA. The United Kingdom combines advanced military engineering with bilateral technology development and manufacturing cooperation.

These capabilities offer industrial depth, but they do not automatically constitute an integrated European production system. A multinational programme must resolve industrial workshare, intellectual-property ownership, export restrictions, technical certification, procurement schedules and responsibility for modifications. Different national requirements can produce duplicated development and incompatible equipment even when governments pursue comparable military objectives.

Air and missile defence demonstrates the problem. Patriot, SAMP/T, IRIS-T SLM and NASAMS provide different technical and operational capabilities, with distinct industrial supply chains and integration requirements. Their presence in European inventories does not establish a unified defensive architecture. Effective cooperation requires compatible surveillance, protected communications, command procedures, training and sustainable interceptor supplies.

The institutional division is equally important. NATO remains responsible for collective defence planning and operational interoperability, while the European Union finances eligible industrial development and collaborative procurement. National governments retain decisive authority over acquisitions, military commitments and many technology-transfer decisions.

The resulting system can encourage cooperation without guaranteeing it. SAFE financing may support common procurement, but it cannot eliminate disagreements over specifications, domestic industrial participation or suppliers. EDIP may strengthen industrial development, yet its €1.5 billion envelope is substantially smaller than the capital requirements implied by Europe’s aggregate defence expenditure.

The strongest measure of industrial sovereignty is consequently not the nationality of a prime contractor. It is whether participating governments possess sufficient legal rights, qualified suppliers, maintenance capacity and technical access to sustain essential military functions when individual production sites or external supply relationships are disrupted.

The Eastern Flank Is Becoming Europe’s Military-Industrial Testing Ground
NATO’s Eastern Sentry, launched on 12 September 2025 following Russian drone incursions into Polish airspace, represents an operational response to the increasingly demanding security environment along the Alliance’s eastern frontier. It connects surveillance, combat aviation, air-defence capabilities and multinational coordination, but remains distinct from EU procurement and industrial programmes.

The Nordic–Baltic countries are developing complementary arrangements. Sweden’s May 2026 announcement envisaged Ukraine acquiring up to 20 Gripen E/F aircraft, potentially accompanied by donations of up to 16 Gripen C/D aircraft. The Swedish package was valued at SEK 25.2 billion, including SEK 22.2 billion associated with aviation-related measures. These announcements remain subject to contractual and implementation conditions and should not be treated as completed aircraft deliveries.

Norway announced plans to provide more than NOK 12 billion in 2026 for Ukrainian drone and autonomous-system procurement. Latvia, which co-leads the Drone Coalition with the United Kingdom, identified 20 participating countries and planned €50 million for drone procurement during 2026. Its bilateral framework with Ukraine envisaged approximately €110 million over the first two years, subject to the required authorisations.

Lithuania’s October 2026 arrangements concerning SkyFortress and electronic-warfare production demonstrate how smaller countries can seek specialised industrial roles through Ukrainian technology partnerships. The proposed industrial localisation is significant, but planned facilities, signed memoranda and successful testing remain different stages of capability development.

The emerging pattern is a distributed network in which countries contribute procurement demand, engineering resources, manufacturing capacity, testing infrastructure and operational experience. Its vulnerability is that bilateral acceleration may produce technical fragmentation unless equipment can be integrated into common NATO-compatible architectures.

NATO, Washington and Türkiye Complicate the Meaning of European Autonomy
Europe’s industrial transformation is occurring within a security relationship in which the United States remains central to advanced military technologies, strategic deterrence and NATO interoperability. American-origin equipment can provide capabilities that European producers cannot immediately replicate, but its acquisition may create contractual dependencies involving proprietary components, software, maintenance and export permissions.

This is not an argument for eliminating transatlantic procurement. The Hague Summit declaration explicitly supported stronger transatlantic defence-industrial cooperation and measures to reduce barriers to defence trade. The underlying challenge is to distinguish productive interdependence from vulnerabilities that could restrict European operational decisions.

Türkiye occupies a different position. As a NATO Ally with an independent defence-industrial sector outside EU membership, its potential participation in European programmes depends on the applicable procurement, industrial-origin and authorisation requirements. Cooperation cannot be inferred from NATO membership alone.

Russia and Belarus add a geographic and operational constraint. NATO identifies Russia as its principal direct security threat, while Belarus’s military relationship with Moscow affects northeastern European defence planning. Russian military regeneration, electronic warfare and hybrid activity create continuing requirements for European surveillance, infrastructure protection and industrial resilience. Yet a sustained threat assessment must not be confused with a prediction of imminent conflict.

The resulting geopolitical structure contains a persistent contradiction: Europe seeks greater freedom of industrial and military action while continuing to depend on multinational supply chains, American technologies, national procurement sovereignty and different regional security priorities. Autonomy cannot be established by expenditure alone; it requires enforceable technology rights and the practical capacity to maintain and replenish equipment.

The Cost of Inaction Will Fall on Procurement Budgets, Industry and Military Readiness
Between 2027 and 2028, the decisive issue will be whether national governments convert higher defence allocations and bilateral technology agreements into repeat procurement, operationally compatible equipment and demonstrable manufacturing output. The EU’s Readiness Roadmap 2030 identifies the European Drone Defence Initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, European Air Shield and European Space Shield as capability priorities, but their implementation depends on national decisions, technical integration and industrial investment.

Three outcomes remain possible through 2031. Industrial convergence would strengthen common standards, multinational manufacturing and supply-chain resilience. Bilateral acceleration could deliver rapid technological gains while leaving continental integration incomplete. Persistent fragmentation would increase procurement costs through duplicated programmes, incompatible systems and limited production consolidation. These pathways may overlap rather than emerge as mutually exclusive outcomes.

The cost of insufficient coordination will be distributed unevenly. National treasuries could finance overlapping procurement and sustainment systems. Defence manufacturers could face uncertain order volumes that discourage investment in capacity. Smaller suppliers could bear the expense of incompatible certification and production requirements. Armed forces could receive equipment whose maintenance, ammunition supply or communications interfaces prevent efficient multinational employment. Ukraine could remain dependent on fragmented support despite providing technologies that European partners seek to industrialise.

The relevant test is already visible in the contrast between €454 billion in projected EU defence expenditure for 2026 and the 24% collaborative share of equipment procurement recorded for 2025. Additional spending will not necessarily correct that structure.

Over the next 12–24 months, the meaningful measure of progress will be the proportion of financial commitments translated into funded orders, completed technology licences, verified production, qualified suppliers and operational interoperability. If governments fail to connect those functions, European taxpayers will finance a larger defence-industrial system without obtaining a proportionate increase in usable military capability.

text:
This is exactly what I mean when I say the tax law is a series of incentives. The government wants to attract investment to particular communities, so it offers tax benefits to investors who meet the requirements.

Senator Tim Scott highlighted 112 Opportunity Zone designations in South Carolina. They’re part of the 6,576 designations the Treasury and the IRS announced nationwide, effective January 1, 2027.

Let’s say you’re looking at two buildings a few blocks apart. Both are in the same ZIP code. Both need work. You can see a business case for renovating either one. But only one might be in a designated Opportunity Zone, because the boundaries follow census tracts. I’d check the exact address on the official map before putting any tax benefit into my numbers.

Then I’d look at the deal itself. What will the renovation cost? Who’s going to rent the space? How much cash will you need if it takes six months longer than expected to find a tenant?

Once those numbers make sense, bring the deal to your tax advisor. Ask whether your gain is eligible, whether the fund and project qualify, and when you’ll owe tax on the gain you reinvest. If the tax comes due while your money is still tied up, you’ll need a plan to pay it.

That’s the conversation I’d have before committing any money. Bring your advisor the property address, the fund documents, and the numbers you’re using to decide whether to invest.

TEXAS BABYSITTER ARRESTED AFTER MOTHER REPORTS DISTURBING ABUSE OF 3-YEAR-OLD SON

A 23-year-old Texas babysitter has been arrested on a charge of aggravated SA of a child, and a mother who says her 3-year-old son was victimized is now sharing disturbing allegations about the woman she once trusted to care for her children.

Maria Rosemary Gardiner, 23, was booked into the Tarrant County Jail on November 4–5, 2026. Public booking information lists a charge of aggravated SA of a child and a $75,000 bond.

The mother of a 3-year-old boy spoke directly with me about her experience with Gardiner, whom she says was active in Dallas-Fort Worth area babysitting groups and offered childcare services for as little as $40 per week.

According to the mother, Gardiner babysat her children between May and July 2026. During that time, the two women developed a close friendship, and the mother says she came to consider Gardiner her best friend.

However, she eventually began noticing concerning changes in her young son. She says he started referring to Gardiner as “mommy” and would sometimes return home with unexplained bruises and marks on his body. When questioned about the injuries, the mother says her son indicated Gardiner was responsible. She subsequently stopped allowing Gardiner to babysit her children.

Months later, the mother says she received a disturbing recording allegedly showing Gardiner SA’ing her 3-year-old son. She claims Gardiner had recorded the abuse and distributed the footage to other individuals.

The mother says she immediately reported the recording to Arlington Police, and Gardiner was arrested less than a week later.

According to the mother, other children were present at Gardiner’s residence when officers arrived. She also claims investigators obtained search warrants for Gardiner’s home and electronic devices, although those details have not been independently confirmed.
The allegations do not end there.

The mother claims Gardiner had a pattern of presenting children she babysat as her own. She alleges Gardiner even created a fraudulent birth certificate identifying her 3-year-old son as Gardiner’s child.

She also alleges Gardiner previously lost custody of her biological child following concerns that she had deliberately made him ill. That allegation has not been independently verified.

Since Gardiner’s arrest, the mother says at least 3 additional families have come forward with concerns that their children may have experienced abuse while in Gardiner’s care. Authorities have not publicly confirmed additional victims or charges related to those claims.

The mother says her son continues to struggle emotionally with what allegedly happened. She describes him waking during the night frightened that the woman he calls “scary mommy” is coming for him.
For this family, the betrayal is particularly devastating. The mother says Gardiner was not simply someone she hired to watch her children. She was someone she trusted, welcomed into her family’s life, and considered a close friend.

Gardiner’s arrest and listed charge are documented in public booking information. The additional allegations shared by the mother have not all been independently verified, and Gardiner is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

Sources: Public Tarrant County booking information; firsthand statements provided directly to True Crime Mama by the alleged victim’s mother.

text:
Latest #WatsonWire: It’s time to start the process to get rail to the airport.

For years, our Austin Bergstrom International Airport (ABIA or AUS) operated beyond the capacity it was originally designed to accommodate. That’s a sign of success, and a reminder that we can’t build Austin’s future relying on infrastructure designed for its past.

We need to envision a successful future and prepare for it.

The “Journey With AUS” expansion project is delivering significant improvements in building the kind of airport a growing, globally connected city like Austin needs for decades to come.

As we build a better airport, we also need to think about how we’re going to get people there to catch their flights and how to get them out of there to participate in our city.

A world-class airport needs a multimodal, world-class transportation system to connect to it. Sure, we need to improve roadway access. And we also should give people more choices about how they travel.

We need to have the same long-term vision for Austin light rail that we’ve had for ABIA.

An airport rail connection has been part of Austin’s long-term transportation vision for years. With Journey with AUS, we have a chance to plan these projects strategically rather than trying to connect them after the fact.

Until now, Austin Transit Partnership (ATP) has appropriately prioritized navigating the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) process for phase 1 of our system. This year, ATP received the important Record of Decision (ROD) from FTA and completed, in record time, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) process for phase 1.

In addition to getting the ROD and completing the NEPA process, I’ve wanted all major design and construction contracts in place and assurance that all of our financial decision-making is guided by a financial stewardship protocol before ATP takes any other big next steps.

We have the ROD, the NEPA process is complete, the major contracts are in place, and the financial stewardship protocol is being followed.

With these important milestones met, we can now take a major step: ATP will start the planning activities for a potential extension to take Austin light rail all the way to the airport.

Chair: “virginia reserves, the gentleman from massachusetts is recognized.”

McGovern: “and i want to thank the gentleman for making my point. this is about retirement plans. it's not about lowering costs today. it's not about repealing the tariffs. it's not about ending this stupid, illegal, costly war in iran. yeah, so the gentleman's made my point, and i'm grateful for that. and, mr. speaker, i'm going to urge that we defeat the previous question. if we do, i will offer an amendment to the rule to provide for consideration of h.r. 1589, the american dream and promise act, which would provide a pathway to citizenship to dreamers who are undocumented immigrants who were brought to the united states as children. they were brought here as children. mr. speaker, last week, the american people voted to reject this administration's cruel and inhumane immigration policies, policies that resulted in tearing families apart, destroying communities, harassing citizens, even killing american citizens in our streets. president trump promised he'd only go after violent criminals. instead, ice agents arrested people with no criminal records at their jobs, at schools, at churches, and in their homes. the administration even deported individuals after the courts told them not to. so, enough is enough. the american people want solutions. this bipartisan bill is an important first step to correcting this madness. dreamers are american in every way but on paper. and for decades, they have contributed to and they have shaped the fabric of america. and yet, they are currently denied their place in the american story. the american dream and promise act writes them into that american story. and, mr. speaker, i ask unanimous consent to insert the text of my amendment into the record, along with any extraneous material immediately prior to the vote on the previous question.”

Chair: “without objection.”

Griffith: “mr. speaker. there's objection. the amendment, as i heard it being discussed, has no relevancy and therefore is not germane to the underlying bill.”

Chair: “there is no amendment pending. the gentleman has objected to the unanimous consent request. the objection is heard.”

McGovern: “the gentleman referred to it as an amendment and asked that the text be placed into the record and that if the previous question is defeated, then it would be brought forward, as i understood it. and maybe i misunderstood. i would suggest that the gentleman raise the point of order after amendment passes, and that's the appropriate time to do it. i mean, those are the procedural rules. is the gentleman correct that the appropriate time to raise the objection would be if the amendment passes?”

Chair: “state your point. no, after we defeat the previous question, it will be appropriate. gentlemen will suspend. the chair will not offer advisory opinions, but there is no amendment pending at this time.”

Griffith: “all right. in that case, i would withdraw my objection.”

Chair: “gentlemen, we've withdrawn. the gentleman from massachusetts has recognized.”

McGovern: “i mean, this is so typical, mr. speaker, of the way republicans have run this house. i mean, you know, it's not enough that they have presided over the most closed congress in history. i just want to point out for the record, so far, mr. speaker and this congress, republicans have issued 173 closed rules. that means 84% of the bills that have come to the floor, there are no amendments, have been allowed. and republicans have blocked 81% of all amendments submitted in this congress. that's over 5,400 amendments have been blocked. democratic amendments and republican amendments have been blocked. i mean, we're in the house of representatives chamber. this is supposed to be like the greatest democracy in the world. and we haven't seen an amendment, a single amendment made in order in four months. i mean, what the heck is going on around here? operating the house in such a closed manner has a chilling effect on the deliberative process. it signals to members that their ideas are not even worth submitting as amendments. and i would also just say, mr. speaker, that, you know, kind of the objection that the gentleman just raised, again, trying to squelch debate, i mean, really? i mean, i don't get it. on an important topic that we've raised here today, but to discuss our proposal, i want to yield two minutes to the gentleman from texas, the sponsor of this great piece of legislation, ms. garcia.”

Garcia: “thank you, mr. speaker, and thank you to my colleague and friend, mr. mcgovern. i rise today to urge my colleagues to vote no on their previous questions so that we can offer an amendment to bring my bipartisan american dream and promise act to the house floor. dreamers were brought to this country as children. most daca recipients arrived here at the age of 7 years old. they have grown up here, went to our schools, built careers, raised families, and contributed to our economy. when they take the pledge of allegiance, they take it because in their heart and their soul and their mind, they are american, as mr. mcgovern said, except on paper. temporary protective status and deferred enforcement departure holders have also spent years, even decades, building their lives here. these folks left our countries because of violence, human trafficking, horrific political conditions to find a place here in our country. these people who have followed, they are all people who have followed the rules. they have done everything we have asked of them, and now their lives have been turned upside down by trump's mass-deportation machine. families are being torn apart, and the urgency, the urgency could not be greater than now. even trump has said he's willing to work with democrats on immigration reform. he said that this very weekend. he told homeland security secretary mcwane mullen to work with democrats on immigration reform. and mullen himself suggested congress could consider a pathway to permanent legal status for daca recipients. well, mr. president, here's your chance, because the dream and promise act does exactly that. we have a bipartisan bill before us. we don't have to wait until the next congress to act. we can do it now.”

McGovern: “i yield the general additional one minute.”

Chair: “additional one minute.”

Garcia: “we have a bipartisan bill before us. we don't have to wait till next congress. we can do it now and send it quickly to the senate, and i'm assured that they're prepared to take it up over there immediately. i urge my colleagues to vote no on their previous questions so that we can move together on this piece of legislation, which could be the foundation of the immigration reform that we need in this country. thank you, and i yield back.”

Chair: “the gentleman from texas yields back. the gentleman from massachusetts reserve, the gentleman from virginia is recognized.”

Griffith: “thank you, mr. speaker. i find it interesting. i enjoy playing with the rules. i love the rules. and as jefferson's manual states, i'm gonna have to paraphrase, 'cause i couldn't pull it up fast enough, but there's nothing that tends to throw more power into the hands of the administration of a legislative body than a failure to follow the rules. and so while my esteemed colleague would have you believe that i'm attempting to squelch debate, i'm actually just trying to make sure that we're following the rules. and with that, i reserve.”

Chair: “gentlemen from virginia reserves, the gentleman from massachusetts is recognized.”

McGovern: “i know the gentleman heard the word amendment and got nervous, so i know where he's coming from. but may i ask how many more speakers that you may have on your side?”

Griffith: “mr. speaker, i would advise the gentleman that i don't have any additional speakers and that i am prepared to close if he is.”

Chair: “the gentleman from massachusetts is recognized.”

McGovern: “i yield myself the remaining time, mr. speaker.”

Chair: “the gentleman is recognized.”

McGovern: “mr. speaker, i started this debate by talking about the message the american people sent last tuesday. and i want to end by making something very clear. they didn't just vote to throw republicans out. they voted for a government that actually gives a damn about them. democrats have an obligation to deliver. and i will fight like hell to make sure that we do deliver, that we do use our power to make a real difference in people's wallets and pocketbooks. we live in the richest country in the history of the world. we live in the richest country in history. yet we have children who show up to school hungry. we have nearly 50 million, that's five zero, 50 million hungry people in america today. that is a disgrace. it is immoral. i am ashamed of that. everybody should be ashamed of that. and that is why this election matters. it is time for a government that cares more about hungry kids than favors for big oil lobbyists. and i don't think that that's a radical idea. i just think it's common sense. and i don't expect people to take our word for it. you know, we've got to earn people's trust by showing that we are different, by showing people that washington can actually work for them again, by showing them that we are going to fight for an affordable america. but first, we have two months left in this congress where republicans control everything, the house, the senate, and the white house. and i have a simple request for my republican colleagues. don't use these final weeks to ram through a bunch of extreme partisan nonsense that the american people rejected. keep the government open. finish the work that we're supposed to do. and show the american people a little respect. come january, things are going to change around here. the american people did their part last tuesday. now we in congress have got to do ours. and with that, i yield back my time.”

Chair: “the gentleman from massachusetts yields back. the gentleman from virginia is recognized.”

Griffith: “thank you, mr. speaker. i urge passage of this rule and adoption of hr 1013, the retirement fairness for charities and educational institutions act of 2025. congress should not continue to delay firefighters, public school teachers, charity workers the cost of effective investments enjoyed by private-sector employees. all this bill does is put those non-profit workers and school teachers on a level playing field with the private-sector employees. again, this measure passed the financial services committee, 43-8, 15 democrats supporting the measuring committee. was also incorporated into the strongly bipartisan invest act, which passed the house 302-123 with 87 democrats in support. this should be an easy vote to help make retirement more affordable, more secure for millions of people that work at non-profit organizations. accordingly, mr. speaker, i ask that everybody vote for this rule and for the underlying bill. and with that, i yield back the balance of my time and move the previous question on the resolution.”

Chair: “gentlemen, for virginia, it yields back. the question is on ordering the previous question on the resolution. those in favor say aye.”

Members: “aye.”

Chair: “those opposed, no.”

Members: “no.”

Chair: “in the opinion of the chair, the ayes have it. for what purpose, gentlemen from massachusetts?”

McGovern: “i ask for the yeas and nays, please.”

Chair: “the yeas and nays are requested. those favoring a vote by the yeas and nays will rise. a sufficient number having risen, the yeas and nays are ordered pursuant to clause 8 of rule 20. further proceedings on this question will be postponed. pursuant to clause 12a of rule 1, the chair declares the house in recess, subject to the call of the chair.” 2/2

Chair: “the chair will entertain up to 15 requests for one minute speeches on each side of the aisle. for what purpose do gentlemen from california seek recognition? without objection, the gentleman is recognized.”

Gentleman from California: “yaacob disease, or cjd, awareness day. so i'd like to take a moment to raise awareness about this rare brain disease. cjd causes a rapid decline in a person's cognitive health and often leads to death within a few months or one year following the onset of symptoms. while there are approximately 600 new cases in the united states each year, this condition sadly does not have a cure. in 2018, i was personally impacted by the loss of a dear friend and mentor, the former mayor of bakersfield and founder of hall ambulance, harvey l hall. harvey hall was a compassionate man with a great love for life, his family, the central valley, and the nation. he was also a beloved member of our community and the longest serving mayor in bakersfield history. sadly, mayor hall lost his life just two weeks after his cjd diagnosis. while we don't have a cure for this disease, raising awareness for cjd brings us closer to breakthroughs in treatments, faster diagnostics, and vital support caregivers need. together, we can bring hope to those living with this devastating disease and the families who have lost loved ones to cjd. thank you and i yield back.”

Chair: “gentlemen yields back. for what purpose, gentlemen, california, seek recognition? without objection, the gentleman is recognized.”

Gentleman from California: “mr. speaker, i rise today to recognize veterans day and honor the veterans who have served our country and the sacrifices they and their families have made. our responsibility to those who serve does not end when they take off the uniform. we must make sure that they have the healthcare, the housing, and the support they need when they come home. i see that commitment first hand across my district from the new va clinic in lancaster to groups like blue star mothers, our vfw and american legion posts, coffee for vets, vets for veterans, and the many veteran service organizations that support those who have served. and in congress, i will keep fighting to deliver on our promise by demanding house leadership pass the major richard starr act and get it signed into law, ensuring combat injured veterans receive the full retirement benefits that they have earned. to all those who have served, thank you. you deserve more than our gratitude. you deserve our continued commitment. i yield back.”

Chair: “gentlemen yields back. for what purpose, gentlemen, new york, seek recognition?”

Gentleman from New York: “mr. speaker, i ask that you advance the center of just the house in one minute. and to advise and extend my responsibility.”

Chair: “without objection, the gentleman is recognized.”

Gentleman from New York: “thank you, mr. speaker. mr. speaker, i rise today to honor the mount vernon boys and girls club. serving more than 1,400 young people every day, this exceptional organization remains a cornerstone in the mount vernon community. by offering engaging academic programs, creative electives, and workforce development training, the boys and girls club provides young people with the tools they need to succeed in and outside of the classroom. beyond these programs, the club offers a safe, welcoming gathering place where members can discover new talents, evolve as students, and pursue their goals. i commend the leadership, staff, and mentors at the boys and girls club of mount vernon for their dedication. and i look forward to seeing the impact its members will make in the years to come. thank you, mr. speaker, and i yield back.”

Chair: “gentlemen yields back. for what purpose, gentlemen, for massachusetts, take recognition?”

Gentleman from Massachusetts: “i ask that you advance the house in one minute, to advise and extend my remarks.”

Chair: “without objection, the gentleman is recognized for one minute.”

Gentleman from Massachusetts: “mr. speaker, recently i hosted an affordability round table in my hometown of worcester to hear directly from constituents who are doing everything right, but are still getting squeezed by the trump administration's reckless economic policies that favor the well-off and the well-connected overworking people. just yesterday, the trump administration doubled down on its heartlessness with the announcement of an intentional policy change to kick another 6.3 million americans off nutrition assistance. let's remember, that's on top of the more than 5.5 million people who have already been kicked off a snap by republicans big ugly bill, and the worst of the cuts haven't even hit yet. and the cruelest part of all of this, it's children who will be hurt the most. tens of thousands of children will lose free and reduced price meals, summer meal benefits, and even wick due to nothing more than onerous paperwork burdens. last week, the american people made their verdict on trump very clear. i look forward to fighting back against this unconscionable policy. let us all come together and end hunger now. i yield back.”

Chair: “gentlemen yields back. for what purpose, gentlewoman from california seek recognition?”

Gentlewoman from California: “i have the right to consent to speak for one minute and revise and extend my remarks.”

Chair: “without objection, the gentlewoman is recognized for one minute.”

Gentlewoman from California: “i'm so proud to represent san diego, the biggest military community in the country. it's my community, my neighbors and friends who've been shipped off to fight secretary hegseth's reckless war in iran. so i take it personally when our leaders are cavalier with our service members lives, i take it personally when our leaders ask our service members to take illegal action in iran and venezuela and yemen. and i take it personally when my constituents aboard the uss abraham lincoln spend ten months at sea, sometimes without enough food to eat, hot water to take a shower, and sufficient access to healthcare. it's my constituents who are still there fighting this war. and what has it all been for? we're not any safer or more secure. and look what's been done in our name. a girl's elementary school bombed in manob. hundreds of people murdered in boats in the caribbean and the eastern pacific. this isn't strength, it's recklessness. it's illegal and someone should be held accountable and we should start with secretary pete hegseth. so my vote today to impeach him isn't political, it's personal and it's for the service members that i represent.”

Chair: “for what purpose does a woman from maryland take their recognition?”

Gentlewoman from Maryland: “to address the house for women and to revise and extend my remarks.”

Chair: “without objection, the gentlewoman is recognized.”

Gentlewoman from Maryland: “mr. speaker, i rise today on behalf of an award winning environmentalist and chesapeake bay champion, dr. walter boynton. for over 50 years, dr. boynton's research has been foundational to our scientific knowledge of the bay and the policies that will preserve its watershed. in 1983, dr. boynton helped design, implement, and institutionalize the chesapeake bay monitoring program. widely considered one of the best in the world, which still tracks key statistics for the bay today. his research team was also the first to identify excess nutrients as the cause of death for underwater grasses and their impact on keystone species in the greater bay. dr. boynton's work has immensely impacted our beloved watershed and watersheds worldwide, and the chesapeake bay being so large and complex. it is thanks to his work and researchers like him that we'll be able to protect this national treasure and unique ecosystem for generations to come. i yield back.”

Chair: “the gentlewoman yields back. what purpose does a gentlewoman from texas seek recognition?”

Garcia: “mr. speaker, i have three minutes to say that there's the house for women and it is your right to say my remarks.”

Chair: “without objection, the gentlewoman is recognized for one minute.”

Garcia: “mr. speaker, we need just one republican to sign my discharge petition to force a vote on the american dream and promise act. just one more. we have 217 signatures, we need one more. dreamers, temporary protected status holders, and deferred enforced departure holders are having their lives turned upside down by trump's mass deportation machine. it is cruel, it is unjust, and congress can do something about it and they can do it now. three of my republican colleagues have already signed. they recognize this is a common sense legislation that the american people support, the majority of americans support the dream act. even donald trump himself admitted his deportation policies have been too tough. now he says he's willing to work with democrats on immigration reform. mr. president, here's your chance. tell one house republican to sign our discharge petition. let's bring this bill to a vote and work together to get started on immigration reform. thank you and i yield back.”

Chair: “gentlewoman yields back. for what purpose does a gentleman from virginia seek recognition?”

Griffith: “mr. speaker, by the direction of the committee on rules, i call up house resolution 1650 and ask for its immediate consideration.”

Chair: “clerk will report the resolution.”

Clerk: “house calendar number 92, house resolution 1650. resolve that upon adoption of this resolution it shall be in order to consider in the house the bill hr 1013 to amend the federal securities laws to enhance 403(b) plans and for other purposes. all points of order against consideration of the bill are waived. the amendment in the nature of a substitute recommended by the committee on financial services, now printed in the bill, shall be considered as adopted. the bill as amended shall be considered as read. all points of order against provisions in the bill as amended are waived. the previous question shall be considered as ordered on the bill as amended. and on any further amendment thereto to final passage without intervening motion except one. one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the chair and ranking majority member of the committee on financial services or their respective designees, and two, one motion to recommit.”

Chair: “the gentleman from virginia is recognized for one hour.”

Griffith: “mr. speaker, for the purpose of debate only, i yield the customary 30 minutes to the gentleman from massachusetts pending which i yield myself such time as i may consume. during consideration of this resolution, all time yielded is for the purpose of debate only. mr. speaker, i ask unanimous consent that all members have five legislative days in which to revise and extend their remarks.”

Chair: “without objection.”

Griffith: “the rules committee met last night and favorably reported a rule providing for consideration of one measure, the retirement and fairness for charities and education institutions act of 2025. house resolution 1650 provides for consideration of hr 1013, the retirement fairness for charities and education institutions act of 2025 under a closed rule. the rule provides for one hour of general debate equally divided and controlled by the chair and the ranking minority member of the committee on financial services or their respective designees, and provides for one motion to recommit. hr 1013 is a bill trying to make retirement more secure for a huge swath of population that works at non-profit organizations, including at hospitals and public schools. millions of public school teachers, nurses, some first responders, and charity employees depend on section 403(b) tax sheltered annuity plans for their retirement. these 403(b) plans were set up to provide a way for non-profits to offer retirement benefits and compete with 401(k) plans and private pensions. however, 403(b) plans have been left behind and have had more restrictive rules around which investments those institutionally sponsored plan managers are allowed to make. the bill allows these plans the option of investing in collective investment trusts if they so choose. collective investment trusts are similar to mutual funds, but have a lower cost to its investors. to clarify, these products are sold to retirement plans and not to individual retail investors. these types of investment decisions are routinely made under the 401(k) plans. and there is no reason for non-profit workers to be hindered in their retirement returns only because these plans aren't available to them. these types of investments that we're talking about under this bill are already an option for 401(k) beneficiaries and for federal employee retirement accounts. i have heard some members on the other side of the aisle act like each retirement plan is forced to invest in collective investment trusts. not so. i would also remind them that each plan manager still has to apply fiduciary rules to whatever investment decisions they make for planned beneficiaries. i get the concern. my mother was a public school teacher, a single parent, who slept on a couch in our front room so that my sister and i could each have our own bedroom. so i understand the importance of making sure that her retirement, and she has passed away, but understand the importance of protecting her retirement when she was still alive. and every other teacher's retirement and non-profit employment retirements should be protected. this bill does that. what this bill does is it looks to do, what it looks to do is to allow for more competition in the retirement investment market, which will hopefully lead to more plans investing in lower fees, higher return pools that ultimately make it more likely for retirees to get bigger payouts. i understand the skepticism when we're looking at a distinct class of retirees, but i would emphasize again there are rules around how retirement plan managers are required to evaluate investments for each plan. really what republicans are aiming to do with this bill is to increase retirement parity and expand access to retirement benefits to people who work for non-profits or who are school teachers. i hope all members of this house support the passage of this rule and the underlying bill, and i urge a yes vote. with that, mr. speaker, i reserve the remainder of my time.”

Chair: “the gentleman from virginia reserves, the gentleman from massachusetts, it's recognized. the gentleman is recognized.”

McGovern: “well, thank you, mr. speaker, and i want to thank the gentleman from virginia for yielding me the customary time, and i yield myself such time as it may consume. mr. speaker, the sun is coming up, and soon it will be a new day in america, and the american people are the ones who are bringing the light. they voted against the chaos, the corruption, and the cruelty, and they voted overwhelmingly in red states and blue states, in small towns and in big cities, from sea to shining sea, to reject this president and this failed administration. they voted to repudiate maga, to rebuke stephen miller and elon musk and kristi noem and cash patel and all the rest of the incompetent clowns empowered by donald j. trump, and the american people delivered their verdict on the work of this failed republican majority here in this congress. come january, republicans will no longer be in charge around here. their incompetence and their foolishness and their obsession with culture wars and billionaire giveaways have cost them the majority. and what is stunning to me, mr. speaker, is that instead of taking the hint or listening to the overwhelming majority of americans who told them to change course, republicans are doubling down on the same tactics and messaging they've been jamming down our throats these last two years. and it's a perfect example of why they lost in the first place. they do not listen. speaker johnson said yesterday that the voters made the wrong choice. the voters made the wrong choice? i mean, are you kidding me? now you might disagree with their choice, mr. speaker, but it's not wrong. you just ain't listening. and then to double down even further, the failed lame duck president appointed stephen miller, the architect of all the cruel policies that most people hate, as his new white house chief of staff. mr. speaker, what planet are these people living on? republicans need to take a long, hard look in the mirror because if they don't break with this delusional thinking and actually start listening, start rejecting extremism, it's going to be a long, long, long, long time before they are ever in the majority again. but let me be clear. it is not enough for democrats simply to win power. now we need to use that power to make a real difference in people's everyday lives, to put economic power back in the hands of everyday people instead of the rich and the powerful. for too long, for too long, the greedy crooks and out of touch mar-a-lago billionaires have gotten away with screwing over the american people. it is time to hold them accountable for ripping us off with their corruption. groceries, gas, housing, healthcare, everything costs too damn much. and people are wondering why, why in the richest country in the history of the world it's gotten so hard just to make ends meet. republicans chose to cut healthcare and food assistance to pay for tax breaks for billionaires. they've let corporate greed run wild. they've spent the last two years looking the other way while the rich and the powerful enrich themselves while the rest of america falls behind. they have let this war in iran go on and on and on while the value of the president's own oil and gas investments goes up and up and up by tens of millions of dollars. are you kidding me? and republicans wonder why people are fed up. this whole damn system is upside down. and today, instead of doing something to address any of that, republicans schedule a debate about a bill on investment plans that won't do a damn thing to bring down costs for ordinary americans. and here's the thing. and here's the thing, mr. speaker. i don't think the american people voted last tuesday just to trade one political party for another and go back to business as usual. they want things to change. they don't want us to nibble around the edges or just undo what republicans did and call it a day. they want us to reject the broken status quo in washington that for too long has stolen from those with the least to give more to those with the most. it is time for economic power in this country to return back to main street, to working people, to small business owners who have been screwed over and screwed over for far too long by the rich and the powerful. democrats understand that. we know that through the results of tuesday's elections, we have been entrusted with an enormous responsibility. my republican colleagues apparently heard something else entirely. they can keep blaming the voters, but come january, things are gonna change around here. and we're gonna make damn sure that that change we fight for means something, that it means something to the people who sent us here. and i reserve my time.”

Chair: “general from massachusetts reserves. gentlemen, virginia is recognized.”

Griffith: “thank you, mr. speaker. well, when we finally got to the bill at the order of the day, there was something that jumped out at me. i was actually planning on just reserving. but my colleague, and i suspect he may have gotten excited and misspoke, but he said, this bill does not do anything for ordinary americans. mr. speaker, i ask you, since when does the average schoolteacher not count as an ordinary american? since when does the nonprofit worker, working for some charity or a hospital, not qualify as an ordinary american? this bill, and i understand all the other objections that the gentleman made about what's been happening and all of his concerns, but this bill lowers the price of buying a retirement product for ordinary teachers, for ordinary nurses, for ordinary people working for nonprofits. that's what this bill does. and it is a common-sense bill, and you know how we know? because some people could say, well, this is just more republican rattling going on by mr. griffith. but this bill came out of committee 43 to 8. it was a bipartisan bill. in fact, a majority of the democrats on the committee that heard this bill, 15 of them, voted in favor of this measure. only 8 chose to take the countering course because those 15 understand that this actually helps ordinary americans. so when you boil it down to what this bill is about, it's a good bill for ordinary americans. it helps to save money long-term for the retirement plans of ordinary americans and puts them in the same place as people who work for for-profit businesses in many cases. and with that, i reserve the remainder of my time.”

Chair: “gentlemen from virginia, reserves of gentlemen from massachusetts is recognized.”

McGovern: “so, mr. speaker, let me read the quote back to the gentleman of what i said, which was that, they scheduled a bill on investment plans that won't do a damn thing to bring down the cost for ordinary americans. costs, costs is the key word here. now, maybe in 30 years, you can make that argument, but the bottom line is, what people are worried about right now is the cost of groceries, the cost of gas, the cost of housing, the cost of everything. they're worried about that today, today. and, you know, i would say to the gentleman, you know, read the room. you know, with all due respect, the american people have heard your argument. they've heard the argument of the republicans over and over and over again. and that argument never seems to address costs that people are dealing with right now. but the american people heard the argument, and they rejected it, and they rejected it. one of the things that we must do come january 3rd is focus in on how do we lower costs that people are facing today. life is just too damn expensive for working families in this country. people are paying more at the grocery store. they're paying more at the gas station. they can't afford rent. they can't afford to buy a house. they can't afford to do anything because everything is up through the roof. and part of it is because of this illegal war in iran. part of it is because of these stupid tariffs that the president insists on putting in place, which, by the way, i don't even think are legal. and when democrats take over, we're gonna debate these tariffs, and we're gonna have votes on these tariffs on this house floor. we're gonna do everything we can to overturn them so that the american people can see their costs go down. and with that, i reserve my time.”

Chair: “massachusetts reserves, the gentleman from virginia is recognized.”

Griffith: “well, mr. speaker, let me make it clear. this is a bill about retirement investment plans. it has nothing to do with tariffs. just so everybody understands, this is not about tariffs. and it lowers costs today. now, it's true that the money may not be reaped until the future, but it lowers costs today because it is anticipated that this bill will lower the fees on the retirement plans that many of our nonprofit workers and our schoolteachers use for their retirements. and with that, i reserve.” 1/2

Through the TGA Adaptive Golf Program, individuals with physical and mental impairments have opportunities to learn, play, and compete. From clinics for beginners picking up a club for the first time to experienced golfers pursuing their competitive goals, the program helps create a place for everyone to grow, build confidence, and experience the joy of golf.

Your support makes these opportunities possible.
