text:
WEEK 10 FIRST LOOK 🏈

The early week breakdown of the Week 10 slate through the lens of StatATL

CHIEFS 🏹@ FALCONS 🪶

The Chiefs have generally been a spot I've avoided QBs against. We're more than halfway through the season and no QB has accounted for more than two TDs against Kansas City, while only Kirk Cousins has surpassed 257 passing yards.

Cousins did post by far the best game against KC, with 365 total yards and two TDs, but he did it on 52 pass attempts. 

For reference, Michael Penix's season high for pass attempts is 34. With all that in mind, I'll likely avoid Penix in this spot.

On the other side of the ball, Atlanta presents a middling matchup for Patrick Mahomes, but not one I'm initially interested in.

Kenneth Walker is going to stand out here with four games over 30 DK points already this season. 

However, the matchup is more difficult than it appears, as Atlanta has two outlier games hurting its stats, including facing 52 rushes in its Week 8 matchup against Tampa Bay.

Bijan Robinson will likely draw lower ownership and has seen 20+ touches in every game but one this season. I expect him to be a contrarian pay-up option this week, but Bijan has topped 29 DK points four times himself, so the ceiling is definitely there.

The matchup for the Falcons pass catchers is atrocious. Only Brock Bowers (6-86-1) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-150-1) have topped 16 fantasy points all season against KC.

On the other side of the ball, this is an intriguing spot to consider Rashee Rice or Xavier Worthy. Atlanta has allowed 6 receivers to surpass 95 receiving yards against them this season.

TEXANS 🐂@ BROWNS 🟫

Coming off the best game of his career, C.J. Stroud doesn't stand out here. 

An opposing QB has yet to hit the 300-yard passing bonus against the Browns this season, while only Trevor Lawrence and Aaron Rodgers have cracked 20 DK points.

On the other side of the ball, Shedeur Sanders would be appealing if he drew the start in a plus matchup at just $4,600.

On the ground, the matchup is above average for both Woody Marks and Quinshon Judkins. However, both have continually shown the inability to produce a score that would hurt you for not rostering them. My early lean is to do just that and ignore both run games.

Through the air, the matchup doesn't stand out for Nico Collins, as Garrett Wilson (7-104-1) is the only pass catcher to top 20 DK points against the Browns all season. Collins has also seen eight or fewer targets every game since Week 1.

The other side of the ball stands out, as opposing pass catchers have smashed against Houston. Denzel Boston ($5,200) and KC Concepcion ($4,800) present strong midrange options.

VIKINGS 🟪@ PACKERS 🧀

Both defenses have really been impressive this season and present bottom-10 matchups for opposing QBs.

Jared Goff (22.0 DK points) and Drake Maye (21.3) have been the only QBs to crack 16 points against the Packers, while only Jordan Love (24.5) has topped 14 DK points against the Vikings. That includes the likes of Josh Allen and Caleb Williams.

Love has been impressive and can be considered despite the matchup, while the Vikings QB situation is in shambles.

On the ground, it looks like Josh Jacobs is going to miss time after injuring his thumb against New England. However, the Packers' inability to run the ball all season has me completely ignoring the Green Bay backfield this week.

The matchup is better for Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason, but it's hard to get excited about either with the split nature of the Vikings backfield.

Through the air, the Packers have been one of the most predictable offenses in the league. Both Matthew Golden and Christian Watson have each topped 20.9 DK points five times, and notably, in four of those weeks, they've done it together.

In nine games, the trio of Love, Watson and Golden has topped 65 DK points five times, with three games over 82 DK points. 

It's unlikely this week is one of those explosions, but it's a good tidbit to keep in mind in future weeks.

Outside of Watson and Golden in Week 1, no WR has topped 70 yards or 17 DK points against Minnesota, which has my interest tempered in both this week.

The other side of the ball is interesting, as several WRs, including Justin Jefferson, have torched the Packers this season. Jefferson posted his lone 30-point outing of the season against Green Bay, while Drake London (9-194-0), Amon-Ra St. Brown (9-153-0) and Jameson Williams (5-91-2) also posted 25+ point outings.

While it's a solid on-paper matchup, the Vikings QB situation may keep me away from any Minnesota players this week.

DOLPHINS 🐬@ COLTS 🐎

I must also be a glutton for punishment, because I'm initially drawn to Malik Willis again, in another great on-paper matchup.

The Colts have allowed five of nine starting QBs they've faced this season to top 20 fantasy points, despite only Patrick Mahomes attempting more than 34 passes against them.

The ground matchup also stands out for Ollie Gordon, as the Colts have allowed Derrick Henry, Kenneth Walker, Jaylen Warren and Bhayshul Tuten all to surpass 150 total yards against them this season, while Javonte Williams went for 124 total yards and a TD last week.

On the other side of the ball, the matchup is above average for Indianapolis, and it will be interesting to see if Jonathan Taylor gets traded today.

No WR on either team stands out here, but Caleb Douglas would be my favorite stacking partner with Willis, with Tyler Warren my favorite bring-back on the Colts, prior to the trade deadline.

Check back Saturday to see how my thoughts develop on this game throughout the week.

PANTHERS 🐈‍⬛@ SAINTS ⚜️

Chuba Hubbard stands out here, despite his price rising to $7,200.

Since Week 2, Hubbard has seen 20 or more touches in every game except one, while Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson, Aaron Jones and Jaylen Warren all accounted for 117 or more total yards against New Orleans, with only Warren not adding at least one TD.

On the other side of the ball, Audric Estime is an intriguing punt at just $4,500, a week after seeing 16 touches.

Through the air, the matchup is interesting for both Bryce Young and Tyler Shough, as both QBs have topped 19.7 points in five of eight games this season and have middling matchups here.

Initially, Shough is my preferred option and stacks easily with Chris Olave, who has double-digit targets in 75% of Saints games this season.

Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble are both initially interesting punt options, as the Saints have been generous to opposing TEs.

BILLS 🦬@ JETS ✈️

An intriguing spot for Josh Allen, as Brock Purdy may draw more ownership than Allen for those spending up at QB.

The Jets have been a middle-of-the-road matchup for opposing QBs. However, they have yet to see an opponent top 34 pass attempts in a game.

Malik Willis, Drake Maye and Kirk Cousins all posted 24+ fantasy point outings despite this limited passing volume, while Allen has posted three games of 34.5 or more DK points while attempting 31 or fewer passes.

The other side of the ball is equally as intriguing for Geno Smith.

While many watched the Bills shut down Carson Wentz on Monday Night Football, other opposing QBs have found great success against Buffalo.

They have allowed games of 383 yards and three TDs (Matthew Stafford), 323 total yards and three TDs (Drake Maye), 334 total yards and four TDs (Jared Goff) and 313 yards and two TDs (Kirk Cousins).

At $4,800, Geno could provide a strong point-per-dollar score on this 10-game slate.

On the ground, the Bills have kept every opposing RB to 60 rushing yards or less, which includes the likes of Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry and Kyren Williams. Not a spot to consider Breece Hall or Braelon Allen.

On the other side of the ball, the matchup stands out for James Cook, who has seen 22 or more touches in 75% of Bills games. Jahmyr Gibbs, Kyle Monangai, Ollie Gordon and Kenneth Walker all exceeded 100 total yards, with at least one TD, against the Jets.

Through the air, opposing top pass catchers have thrived against Buffalo, with Nico Collins, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Tre Tucker and Puka Nacua all surpassing 20 fantasy points. Nacua and St. Brown both exceeded 38 DK points.

Sam LaPorta (6-52-1), Michael Mayer (7-95-0), Tyler Higbee (5-83-0), Tre Harris (6-76-0) and Davante Adams (5-51-2) also produced strong scores in supplementary roles.

Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper and Adonai Mitchell are all intriguing if building around this game, while DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid initially are my favorite stacking partners with Josh Allen.

JAGUARS🐈 @ TITANS ⚔️

After allowing Deshaun Watson and Joe Burrow to combine for 800 yards and seven TDs the past two weeks, the Titans host the 6-2 Jaguars led by Trevor Lawrence.

The matchup is obviously very strong on paper. However, Lawrence has only attempted 40 total passes the last two weeks combined, both 21+ point blowout wins over the Ravens and Colts.

With how strong the Jaguars defense is, it feels unlikely Lawrence is asked to throw more than 30 times, and as such, that tempers my interest in him.

On the ground, the Titans haven't given up any massive games to opposing RBs, but Quinshon Judkins, Chase Brown and Jonathan Taylor all topped 18 DK points against Tennessee the past three games.

At $6,600, Bhayshul Tuten is intriguing in a spot I'd expect Jacksonville to win going away.

Through the air, the Titans have faced six WRs all season that saw eight or more targets. Five of the six scored 24 or more DK points, with Keenan Allen (8-82 on 11 targets) the lone outlier.

As such, Parker Washington ($6,200) stands out here.

On the other side of the ball, Carnell Tate ($5,200) is interesting.

RAMS 🐏 @ CARDINALS 🐦

The big early news surrounding both of these teams is around injuries.

Puka Nacua was placed on IR, leaving a huge void in the Rams passing attack, as Davante Adams is also expected to miss several more weeks.

On the other side of the ball, Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury and is out for the season. Outside of TE Trey McBride, this leaves the Cardinals with receiving options of Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay and Simi Fehoko.

That trio has combined for 93 receiving yards this season. Yikes.

The outlook isn't much more exciting for the Rams, who are left with Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington.

Mumpfield has one serviceable game this season, a 4-93-1 performance against the Rams when Puka missed time earlier this season, while Atwell posted 52 yards in Week 8.

I expect the field to have interest in several of these options as salary savers at the position, but my early lean is likely to completely avoid all the WRs in this game, with some potential interest in both teams' TEs.

Carson Beck is set to make his NFL debut, but even at just $4,200, he doesn't initially interest me with such limited weapons.

On the ground, Jeremiyah Love is still on IR, which should lead to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight splitting the backfield work for Arizona. Nothing to get excited about here.

Along with the Cardinals run game, another spot I'll likely avoid is the Rams backfield, which continues to operate as a timeshare between Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

The price is attractive for Corum at $5,100, but he's only seen more than 13 touches once all season and only has 10 receptions on the season.

Circling back to the TEs, Trey McBride ($7,100) should see double-digit targets again and is intriguing.

On the other side of the ball, Matthew Stafford is still likely to attempt at least 25 passes even without Nacua and Adams. 

I expect the Rams to run double- and triple-TE sets at a high frequency, which creates some early interest in Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee.

SEAHAWKS 🟢@ RAIDERS ☠️

Drew Lock has some initial appeal, as the Raiders have already allowed Drake Maye and Tyler Shough to each account for 290+ yards with four or more TDs earlier this season, while Geno Smith and Brock Purdy both accounted for 270+ yards and multiple TDs the last two weeks.

Through the air, Las Vegas presents an above-average matchup for Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and he's interesting once again this week.

The Raiders have also been particularly friendly to opposing TEs and have allowed Juwan Johnson, Davis Allen and Noah Fant to all have multi-TD performances against them, while Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon, Oronde Gadsden and Dalton Kincaid also posted double-digit DK scores.

At $3,900, AJ Barner is also intriguing as a pay-down option.

The ground game also stands out for Seattle, as opposing RBs have smashed the Raiders. Braelon Allen, Kyren Williams, James Cook, Kenneth Walker, Omarion Hampton and Blake Corum all accounted for over 100 total yards, with all six adding at least one TD, while Christian McCaffrey had 87 yards and two TDs last week against this Las Vegas defense.

Zach Charbonnet saw 17 touches last week and has seen five of the seven red-zone rushes since returning from injury. He is my preferred Seattle RB and is priced at $5,600.

On the other side of the ball, tough matchups across the board for the Raiders.

Caleb Williams has been the only QB to top 190 passing yards against Seattle, while no opposing RB has rushed for 70 yards or accounted for more than 95 total yards.

Not a week I'll be considering Kirk Cousins or Ashton Jeanty.

The Seahawks also present bottom-eight matchups for both Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker.

Despite facing Trey McBride twice, Colston Loveland, Travis Kelce, George Kittle and Hunter Henry, no opposing TE has exceeded 65 receiving yards. 

The Seahawks have only surrendered two TDs to the position all year, and both came in the first two weeks of the season.

49ERS ⛏️@ COWBOYS 🤠

On paper, the final game of the slate should offer us more fantasy goodness than the other two afternoon games.

A solid spot for Brock Purdy here. However, C.J. Stroud has been the only QB to top 300 yards in this matchup.

Jaxson Dart, Jayden Daniels and Lamar Jackson all added 50+ yards on the ground in this matchup, which adds some appeal to Purdy, who has over 200 rushing yards on the season.

The 49ers have been a below-average opponent for opposing QBs.

At $6,400, Dak Prescott doesn't stand out here, as he's only topped 23.5 DK points once all season, while no opposing QB has posted a fantasy score above 25 points against San Francisco all year.

On the ground, this is an intriguing spot for Christian McCaffrey, as the Cowboys have given up some massive games to opposing RBs, specifically Bucky Irving (175 total yards and two TDs) and Tyler Allgeier (191 total yards and two TDs).

He's expensive at $8,500 but should remain heavily involved if Dallas is pushing or keeping up with San Francisco.

Through the air, Mike Evans is likely to miss another week, however Deebo Samuel is slated to practice this week and could return Sunday. 

Keenan Allen was traded to SF this week, and while we have no idea how much he'll play, he's intriguing at $5,100, especially if Evans and Deebo both are inactive

The matchup is tough for CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, if active, as San Francisco has only allowed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (5-102-1) and Brock Bowers (7-111-1) to top 100 yards this season.

If Pickens were to miss again, Lamb would have potential to see his fourth game with 16+ targets in the past seven weeks. Even at $8,800 in a tough matchup, that potential opportunity is hard to ignore.

My favorite Cowboy in this game might end up being Brevyn Spann-Ford ($3,200), as Jake Ferguson is likely to miss multiple weeks with a knee injury suffered against Indianapolis.

These are the initial reads, not final decisions. We'll keep evaluating the matchups, roles and ownership as the week develops and some more trades are finalized. 🔥

text:
Training Your Service Dog, Part 34: Rideshare Car Entry and Exit
Tuesday, Nov 10, 2026

Part 33 covered the city bus. Next up: the rideshare car, where your dog loads, settles in the footwell and exits calmly.
Know your rights first. Guiding Eyes for the Blind notes that the ADA requires rideshare drivers to transport service animals, with no pet fee and no need for a vest or papers. Drivers may only ask the two ADA questions.
Message your driver your exact pickup spot, and mention your dog is with you if you choose. Lyft lets riders disclose a service animal in the app and no Pet ride is needed.
Practice at home with a parked car. Cue a wait at the open door, then invite your dog in, into a down in the footwell. Pay with food while relaxed. Food stays the daily training paycheck. Then cue a wait again before stepping out.
A small towel for the floor is optional and a polite offer if a driver asks. Never yell the dog's name. No loud NO. Keep dogs on our schedule.
How to measure progress: aim for 8 of 10 calm entries and exits across 2 cars this week, with a wait at the door, a down within 30 seconds and no jumping out. Here in Tampa Bay, Odin is an 8 1/2 year old golden who started functional tasks at 6 months with Ski.
Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

Sources: Guiding Eyes for the Blind, Lyft accessibility guidance, photos of Odin by DigitalAssetsUS.

Mark your calendars! The Professional Outdoor Media Association (POMA) is bringing its annual Summit to Branson, Missouri, May 24–26, 2027, and attendees can expect three days packed with outdoor experiences, meaningful connections, hands-on opportunities and industry inspiration.

With its unique blend of outdoor adventure, professional development and relationship-building, the POMA Summit is where outdoor storytellers, brands and industry leaders come together. Whether you're a writer, photographer, videographer, broadcaster, podcaster, content creator or outdoor industry professional, the Summit offers an opportunity to build relationships, discover new products, develop story ideas and strengthen connections that can make a lasting impact on your business.

The POMA Summit isn't your typical industry conference. It's an opportunity to get out in the field, experience products firsthand, connect face-to-face with the people behind the brands and build relationships with fellow outdoor communicators. From educational sessions and networking opportunities to hands-on outdoor experiences and evening gatherings, there's something for everyone.

"There's nothing quite like bringing the outdoor media community and industry together in one place," said Stephanie Spika Hickey, POMA Executive Director. "The Summit is about more than exchanging business cards. It's about building relationships, creating opportunities, sharing ideas and having experiences together. Whether you're a longtime POMA member or someone attending for the first time, you'll leave with new connections, fresh inspiration and memories that last long after the event."

REGISTRATION OPENS JANUARY 2027

You do not have to be a POMA member to attend the Summit! Outdoor media professionals and industry representatives are welcome. However, registration rates will be higher for non-POMA members, making membership an added value for those planning to attend.

Registration will officially open in January 2027. Additional details, including the event schedule, outdoor experiences and registration rates, will be announced in the coming months.

A GREAT TIME TO GET INVOLVED WITH POMA

The Summit is also a great opportunity to become part of a growing community dedicated to strengthening outdoor communications and supporting the hunting, fishing and outdoor industries.

Outdoor media professionals are encouraged to explore POMA membership and take advantage of year-round benefits, including professional development, networking, exclusive member opportunities, industry connections and access to special events.

Interested in joining? Learn more about POMA Media Membership.

Businesses, manufacturers, conservation organizations, tourism agencies and other industry partners are also encouraged to explore POMA Corporate Partnership opportunities. Corporate Partners gain valuable exposure to a network of professional outdoor communicators and opportunities to connect with the people telling the stories that shape the outdoor industry.

Learn more about POMA Corporate Partnerships.

text:
R.O.A.R. 
A few ways to take care of ourselves and each other while we show up for Oregon:
*Take breaks when you need them. 

*Mute the thread, turn off the news, eat something, or call a friend. 

*Give yourself permission to be done for the day.

*Make room for people to help in different ways. 

*Some folks can attend a meeting. Others can read the agenda, write a public comment, offer a ride, or check in on someone afterward.

*Look out for your people. If you’re going to an event together, agree on where to meet and how everyone’s getting home. A simple “Made it home” text goes a long way.

*Give each other an easy way to step away. “Want me to walk out with you?” can be all someone needs to hear when things get overwhelming.

*Offer something specific. “I can give you a ride,” “I’ll send you the meeting notes,” or “Want me to call tomorrow?” is easier to say yes to when someone’s worn out.

*Check in after the noise dies down. Ask how someone’s doing the next day, and make time to talk about the rest of life, too.

We must stick together and help each other because we are all we have, but we also have God.

P Diddy was j*rking off in front of a hundred guests sitting next to the prince . On a couch. In full view of everyone. A girl would walk up, stay a minute, walk away. Then another. He'd go inside, come back, start again. A hundred women at his party and he was still doing it alone.

She was twenty feet away when he leaned over to the man next to him and whispered four words: "I want her."

Her name is Tanea. A singer from South Central who was never famous. A man she calls the Prince flew her to Miami after three weeks of promising her a music career. The career meeting turned out to be a party on Star Island. The party turned out to be a freak off.

In the video she walks through what she saw like a paramedic describing a scene they arrived at too late. No emotion. Just the sequence.

Phones went into sealed bubble cases at the door. His son Christian hand-picked who got in. White robe, slippers - that was the pass. Inside, people passed out on furniture, strangers having s*x in every room, house music shaking the walls at sunrise.

He called her over. Offered the photo booth. Ice cream. "Everything is free," he said. Then he turned to the Prince and started whispering about her like she wasn't standing right there.

"I want her. Like, I want her."

Before she could even ask what that meant, three people hit her with the same question. The Prince. A girl too gone to stand straight. Then Diddy himself: "You're going to Cuba with us, right?"

She said yes - and walked straight to the front door.

She called the police on the Prince, got handed a printed plane ticket on her way out, and flew back to LA that same night. She later learned why that mattered: Cuba is one of the few places they don't always stamp your passport. And where people disappear.

She told this story on camera in 2022. The internet called her a liar. Two years later, the FBI kicked down that same front door.

So did Diddy let her walk out because he had a hundred other girls that night, or because he already knew she'd never be able to prove a single thing she saw?

The Royal Eswatini Police Service (REPS) has joined forces with the Eswatini Bankers Association, financial institutions, mobile network operators and other key stakeholders to strengthen the national fight against fraud through the launch of the 2026 International Fraud Awareness Month.

The campaign, launched at the Police Headquarters Conference Room, is held under the theme “TIVIKELE – Stay Safe Online. Think Before You Click. Verify Before You Trust.” It seeks to educate the public, strengthen fraud detection and encourage the proactive reporting of fraudulent activities.

The launch comes against the backdrop of concerning statistics revealed by the Eswatini Bankers Association, which disclosed that financial institutions recorded losses exceeding E31 million between November 2025 and 31 October 2026. According to the association, this represents the highest annual fraud-related losses recorded by the banking sector in the past decade.

The association described the figures as a wake-up call for the country, emphasising the need for increased public awareness, stronger institutional controls and closer cooperation among stakeholders in the financial sector.

National Commissioner of Police, Mr Vusi Manoma Masango, echoed these concerns, assuring EmaSwati that the police and their partners would not relent in their efforts to combat financial crimes.

Using the expression “Itawulala ibonene,” Masango emphasised the determination of law enforcement and its partners to confront fraudulent activities targeting banks, financial institutions and unsuspecting members of the public.

The National Commissioner revealed that between 1 October 2025 and September 2026, the Royal Eswatini Police Service recorded 1,404 financial crime cases. The reported cases involved an actual financial value of E110,248,879.90, while the potential financial value was approximately E1,122,528.61, according to the statistics presented.

He further noted that reported cases had decreased by 428. However, he cautioned that the decline should not be interpreted as an indication that fraud had been eliminated, particularly given the substantial financial losses still being experienced.

“We remain concerned about the substantial financial losses reflected in these statistics. Even one victim losing their hard-earned money to fraud is one victim too many,” Masango said.

The National Commissioner also highlighted the growing risks associated with digital transformation, urging EmaSwati to remain vigilant as they increasingly embrace online banking, mobile money and other digital financial services.

He warned citizens against falling for suspicious investment opportunities, fraudulent offers and messages designed to create panic or pressure individuals into making hurried financial decisions.

Masango encouraged the public to verify information before sharing personal or financial details, avoid clicking suspicious links and seek assistance whenever they are uncertain about the legitimacy of a transaction or communication.

Importantly, he urged victims of fraud not to remain silent or blame themselves, noting that criminals often use sophisticated manipulation tactics to deceive unsuspecting people.

Abdul El-Sayed: “It’s also better early than late, and that is why I apologize for it.”

Abdul El-Sayed: “When Christian Nationals, for example, does something heinous, we give them their humanity and their individuality. But when somebody of a different faith or of a different community does something, we couple them in as speaking for the group.”

text:
Pablo Picasso and his Dalmatian, Perro, photographed at his villa in Cannes, France, in 1961.

Known for revolutionizing modern art, Picasso also had a lifelong interest in animals, many of which found their way into his paintings and personal life.

Among his canine companions was Perro, a Dalmatian who lived with the artist at his villa, La Californie, on the French Riviera.

This intimate moment was captured by Irish photographer Edward Quinn, who spent more than two decades documenting Picasso's life, family, and creative surroundings. Through his photographs, Quinn offered a rare look at the artist beyond his paintings and public reputation.

Away from the studios, exhibitions, and international recognition, photographs like this reveal a more familiar side of Picasso: a man enjoying a quiet moment with his dog.

It is a reminder that even some of history's most influential figures shared the simple companionship that animals have offered humans for centuries.

🏠 Indianapolis, Indiana: 220 people housed directly from the streets since June 2025.
🏠 Denver, Colorado : Street homelessness fell from 1,423 people in 2023 to 518 in 2026.

The common thread? Communities working together, using reliable data, expanding access to housing and connecting people with the support they need.

This progress isn't about one political party or one program. It's about local partners coming together around measurable results.

Read Adam's op-ed in Next City: https://t.co/b7LGj81dyG

‼️ OLE MISS STUDENT APOLOGIZES AFTER VIRAL VIDEO SHOWS WOMEN MAKING MONKEY NOISES OUTSIDE BLACK STUDENTS’ APARTMENT

OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI — One of the University of Mississippi students accused of making racist gestures outside an apartment occupied by three Black students has broken her silence, issuing a public apology while claiming she had no idea who lived inside the apartment.

Alaina Kunes, an 18-year-old freshman at Ole Miss, released a statement on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, following widespread outrage over a viral Ring doorbell video recorded on Friday, November 6.

The footage shows three white female students- Identified as Alaina Kunes and Lauren Mayfield- walking past an apartment when two of them approach the doorbell camera, make monkey noises, and beat their chests. A third student- identified as Sarah Whitehead- walks past without appearing to participate in the gestures.

The video was shared on TikTok by Ole Miss student Jakiyra Metcalf, who lives in the apartment with two other black students. It quickly went viral, accumulating millions of views and sparking widespread condemnation.

Metcalf later revealed that the women captured on camera were allegedly their upstairs neighbors.

Now, Kunes is apologizing for her behavior, insisting that she was unaware of the residents’ race when the incident occurred.

“Before the incident on November 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however, I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful.”

Kunes maintained that she would never intentionally direct such gestures or noises toward a person of color and claimed she has personally apologized to the women affected.

She also acknowledged that she could never fully understand the pain her actions caused, saying the women “deserve to feel seen and understood.”

According to Kunes, the behavior captured in the video does not reflect the person she is trying to become.

She further revealed that she and her family have received death threats and harassment since the footage began circulating online. She thanked authorities for helping ensure their safety and requested privacy as the investigation continues.

Sources who spoke with TMZ claimed the students were making animal noises at multiple apartment doors as they walked through the building and that the behavior was intended as harmless fun rather than a racially motivated act.

However, the explanation has done little to quiet the controversy surrounding the incident.

The University of Mississippi has confirmed that the women involved are students and that the matter is being investigated by the appropriate university offices.

Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs Shawnboda Mead condemned the behavior, describing it as deeply troubling and inconsistent with the university’s values.

University officials have also contacted the students living in the apartment to offer support and resources.

Meanwhile, the American Civil Liberties Union of Mississippi has confirmed that it received complaints regarding the incident and is reviewing them.

The organization has emphasized that universities have obligations under federal civil rights laws to address racial harassment that creates a hostile educational environment.

As of Tuesday, November 10, university officials had not publicly announced whether any disciplinary action would be taken against the students involved.

Kunes says she intends to cooperate fully with the university’s investigation.

text:
Oh, this is nice and simplistic.  Just like so many political talking points.

Just enough to wedge an idea into your brain during the half-second you spend doomscrolling, without requiring you to actually think about it.

Unfortunately, as with most things in real life, the actual issue is considerably more complicated than this cheap little meme would have you believe.

First, let me make something absolutely clear: I have no problem whatsoever with Democrats, or anyone else, wearing pins to remember murdered children. I think that's a perfectly decent thing to do.  It's the rest of the framing I find absolutely disgusting.

Now, I'm going to moderate myself here, because this is one of those subjects that ordinarily makes me spitting mad. I'm going to make a conscious effort to remain civil and stick to the facts.

Let's start with the basic premise:

"If we banned guns, children wouldn't die in school shootings."

It's one of those ideas that sounds perfectly reasonable if you devote three brain-thought tokens to it.

Unfortunately, the more tokens you spend examining it, the murkier things become.  

Let's talk about prohibition.

Restricting access to something dangerous can certainly reduce access to it. I'm not disputing that.  What I'm disputing is the assumption that restricting the object necessarily solves the underlying problem.

Consider illegal drugs.  We've been restricting and prohibiting various drugs for more than a century. We got particularly serious about enforcement under Nixon, when the modern War on Drugs began.

Has it eliminated illegal drug use?  Of course not.  
Drug-use trends have risen and fallen over the decades.  Certain substances have declined in popularity, while others have become more prevalent. But after more than fifty years of aggressive enforcement, we still have an enormous illegal drug market.

We've created some rather spectacular unintended consequences along the way.  The illegal drug trade is enormously profitable precisely because it's illegal. That profitability helps sustain international cartels, organized crime, and violent street gangs.

People suffering from addiction face stigma and the possibility of criminal prosecution, which can discourage them from seeking help.  Criminal records can make employment and rebuilding a life considerably harder.

Drugs themselves become more dangerous when they're manufactured and distributed outside any legitimate system of quality control.

Now, I'm a recovering drug addict.  I know firsthand how destructive addiction can be.  I also know firsthand that someone determined to obtain an illegal substance can be quite difficult to stop.

Look at marijuana.  Even in states like Texas, where recreational marijuana remains illegal, it's hardly some mysterious substance nobody can find.  I could go outside when school lets out and score some weed in less than fifteen minutes.

Prohibition has costs.  Those costs don't magically disappear because the intentions behind it are good.

Which brings us back to firearms.  Unlike illegal recreational drugs, firearms have legitimate and important uses, including hunting, sporting activities, and, most importantly for this discussion, self-defense.

"But Europe has almost no gun deaths, while America leads the world!"

Well, no.  First, Europe isn't a country, and European nations have different laws, cultures, crime rates, and histories. 

Second, the United States does not lead the entire world in firearm homicide rates. Several countries have substantially higher rates.

America absolutely has a serious firearm violence problem, particularly compared with other wealthy, developed countries. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.  But there's another important distinction that gets lost in these conversations:

Gun deaths are not all the same thing.

Suicides, domestic murders, gang-related homicides, accidental shootings, and school massacres are different problems with different causes.  They may involve the same instrument, but that doesn't mean the same policy will solve all of them.  A substantial portion of American firearm homicide is associated with broader problems of violent crime, concentrated poverty, and criminal activity.

Remember when I was talking about illegal drugs?  Well, here we are again.

Drug trafficking and illegal markets contribute enormously to gang violence.  The same prohibition policies that are supposed to protect society can help create enormously profitable criminal enterprises willing to use violence to protect their business.

Funny how these things intersect, isn't it?

Now let's talk about something this meme conveniently ignores: defensive gun use.  Every year, Americans use firearms to defend themselves against criminal threats.  
Exactly how often is a matter of considerable dispute.

Some estimates put defensive gun use around 25k s annually. Other surveys have produced estimates exceeding a million.  Personally, I'm skeptical of the highest estimates. I suspect the real number is much closer to 40,000/year.

Even the conservative estimates represent a substantial number of people protecting themselves from violent crime.  That's important.

When you propose restricting access to firearms, you aren't merely affecting people who might commit crimes.  You're also affecting people who might need a firearm to stop one.

That's the part gun control advocates so frequently seem unwilling to acknowledge.  A firearm is not inherently an act of violence.  It is an instrument that can be used for violence, for defense against violence, or for entirely peaceful purposes.

The overwhelming majority of American gun owners never use their firearms to commit violent crimes.. which is why the accusation in this meme is so thoroughly dishonest.

It takes an object that millions of Americans own and use lawfully, including for the defense of innocent life, and declares that displaying support for the right to own it amounts to celebrating murdered children.

That's emotional manipulation.

It's particularly nasty emotional manipulation.

Now, before someone says I'm arguing that gun laws accomplish absolutely nothing, I'm not.

Certain restrictions may prevent certain crimes.  Others may have unintended consequences.  The effectiveness of any particular law deserves to be examined on its merits.

What I reject is the simplistic notion that making something illegal necessarily makes society safer.

Here's another example:  Prescription painkillers.

Ask people suffering from severe chronic pain what it's like trying to obtain adequate pain management these days.  In response to a very real opioid crisis, we've imposed restrictions that have sometimes made legitimate treatment extraordinarily difficult.  People who genuinely need these medications can find themselves treated like prospective criminals.

Meanwhile, illicit opioids, including fentanyl, remain a devastating problem.

We have managed to make life harder for legitimate patients without eliminating the illegal market.

Does that sound familiar?  Because it's precisely the kind of unintended consequence that worries me about firearm restrictions.

The people most willing to obey the law are the easiest people to restrict.  The people already willing to commit murder are, by definition, considerably less concerned about obeying it.  

And now, finally, let's talk about school shootings, because that's what this meme is really trying to exploit.  

School shootings are horrific.  They're also relatively rare events, statistically speaking. The number of children murdered in school shootings each year is considerably smaller than many people imagine when they hear broad statistics about gun violence involving children.  (most of those "children" are 17-19 years old and gang members)

That doesn't make a single one of those deaths acceptable.  It means we should understand the actual scale and nature of the problem if we're serious about solving it.

Second Amendment advocates have proposed solutions!

We've suggested allowing appropriately trained, willing school employees to carry firearms, subject to serious standards and safeguards.

Now, ask your average conservative what they think of the public education establishment.  You'll probably get an answer that would make a sailor blush.  Yet, many of us would still rather see a properly trained teacher capable of defending students than leave an entire classroom helpless while waiting for police to arrive.  Gun control advocates frequently oppose this.

We've suggested placing more trained law enforcement officers in schools, with clear responsibilities for responding to violent threats.  Many gun control advocates oppose that, too, arguing that police don't belong in schools.

There are legitimate questions about training, implementation, effectiveness, and unintended consequences.  I'm perfectly willing to have those conversations.

Here's what I find infuriating:  You cannot demand that we take school security seriously, then dismiss every security proposal we offer as proof that we don't care about children.

You can disagree with our solutions.  You can argue that armed teachers are a bad idea.  You can argue that school resource officers aren't effective.  You can present evidence, challenge assumptions, and propose alternatives.

That's how serious adults discuss public policy.

But you don't get to declare that anyone who disagrees with your preferred solution is celebrating the slaughter of children.

That's morally repugnant.

I happen to believe children are among the most precious people in our society.  I think they deserve serious protection.

We protect presidents, members of Congress, judges, and other public officials with armed security.  We protect banks, courthouses, and other important institutions with armed security.  Apparently, the notion that schools might also benefit from appropriately trained armed protection is, to some people, beyond the pale.

I don't understand that.  I genuinely don't.

I especially don't understand the insistence that anyone proposing such measures must secretly be indifferent to dead children.

Here's the fundamental disagreement:

You believe restricting civilian access to firearms will make children safer.  I believe that preserving the ability of law-abiding citizens to defend themselves, while addressing violent criminals and improving school security is a better approach.

We can debate which policies actually work.  We SHOULD debate which policies actually work.

We should be willing to change our minds when the evidence warrants it.

But this meme doesn't do any of that.

It doesn't present evidence.
It doesn't examine competing solutions.
It doesn't even attempt to understand why someone might support the Second Amendment.

It simply points at one group mourning murdered children and another group displaying support for gun rights, then declares that the latter must be celebrating the murders.

That is a grotesque accusation to make against millions of decent, law-abiding Americans.

You don't have a monopoly on compassion because you wear a particular pin.  

You don't have a monopoly on caring about children because you support a particular law.

You certainly don't get to claim the moral high ground by deliberately misrepresenting the beliefs and motives of people who disagree with you.

We both want children to come home from school alive.

We disagree about how best to accomplish that.

If you cannot recognize the difference between those two statements, then perhaps you should spend a few more brain-thought tokens on the subject before posting another meme.

text:
Massie forces Hegseth impeachment vote after primary loss

By E.D. Bivens 
WASHINGTON — Outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, triggering a procedural clock that requires House leaders to schedule a vote within days.
Massie, who lost his Republican primary in May to a Trump-endorsed challenger, accused Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution by sustaining hostilities against Iran without congressional authorization, along with related claims involving boat strikes, the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, and other actions. He has described the effort as an attempt to force accountability before Democrats assume control of the House in January. Hegseth has called the resolution a “farce” and a “stunt.” President Donald Trump has publicly supported Hegseth.
Massie’s primary defeat occurred in the most expensive House primary on record. Outside groups, including those associated with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee and other pro-Israel organizations, spent millions opposing him and supporting his opponent. Those groups are funded primarily by American citizens and donors; their spending is legal independent expenditure activity under U.S. campaign finance rules. Massie himself has received no money from tracked pro-Israel PACs, according to public FEC data.
Massie has also received itemized contributions from U.S. citizens of Middle Eastern background, including the maximum $7,000 per-cycle gifts from Texas businessman Sam Mahrouq and several family members. Mahrouq has said he was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Jordan and immigrated to the United States as a teenager. The family has donated to a range of candidates and groups across the political spectrum. No public records show contributions to Massie from foreign governments.
Separate allegations involving Massie have circulated without independent corroboration. A woman who said she dated him after his wife’s death claimed he offered her money tied to a workplace dispute and spoke of a personal relationship with Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo. Both Massie and Boebert have denied the claims. Massie has stated that no ethics complaints have been filed against him. He also accepted a 2025 award from the Quincy Institute, a U.S. think tank, alongside a Democratic colleague; critics have pointed to the institute’s leadership as evidence of concerning associations, while supporters describe it as recognition for war-powers work.
Massie has long opposed broad foreign aid and unauthorized military action, positions that have put him at odds with both Trump and pro-Israel advocacy organizations. His impeachment resolution arrives in the final weeks of his term and highlights ongoing divisions within the Republican conference over the scope of executive war powers and U.S. involvement in the Iran conflict. #Massie @PressSec

(Photo by Milo Mitchell) November 9, 2026 By Denise Heady, MA 7 min read When Jamil Newirth was just 32 years old, doctors told him he had terminal brain cancer and had about 17 months to live.  That was 14 years ago.  Today, at 46, the Hawaii native is a practicing attorney in Maui, a future he once feared he would never have. He credits his remarkable survival in part to a novel cancer vaccine developed at UCLA that uses the body's own immune system to recognize and attack brain tumors.  Newirth is among a group of patients who have experienced long-term survival after receiving the personalized vaccine through clinical trials led by UCLA neurosurgeon Linda Liau, MD, PhD and tumor immunologist Robert Prins, PhD.  For more than two decades, Dr. Liau and her team at the UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center have been working to develop new treatments for glioblastoma, the most aggressive and deadly form of brain cancer. Their work is now helping shape the next generation of cancer vaccines and combination immunotherapies that could offer new hope for patients facing this devastating disease.  "Patients like Jamil are such an inspiration to me and my team," said Dr. Liau, chair of neurosurgery at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA. "He and other patients like him are what inspires me to go to work each day and to maintain hope that immunotherapy could potentially lead to a cure for brain cancer someday."  A devastating diagnosis In 2012, Newirth had just graduated from the University of Hawaii William S. Richardson School of Law and was preparing for the bar exam when he began experiencing severe headaches.  After multiple emergency room visits, where his symptoms were initially attributed to stress, he developed nausea, vomiting and numbness on the left side of his body. An MRI eventually revealed a large brain tumor. He was diagnosed with glioblastoma.  Glioblastoma grows and spreads quickly.  Even after standard treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiation, the disease almost always returns.  "I wasn't really given any hope when I was diagnosed," Newirth recalled.  📷 Jamil Newirth found Dr. Linda Liau when he was searching for neurosurgeons investigating new treatments for glioblastoma. (Photo by Milo Mitchell) Determined to find another option, he began searching for a neurosurgeon who could offer something beyond standard treatment. That search led him to Dr. Liau, who was enrolling patients in a clinical trial testing the first personalized brain cancer vaccine.  "Dr. Liau is confident, caring and does everything with a personal touch," Newirth said. "She even flew back early from her vacation to do my surgery and start my treatment. You can tell she just really cares."  Teaching the immune system to fight brain cancer One of the biggest challenges in treating glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors is that the tumors are particularly effective at evading the immune system. Unlike some other cancers, these tumors often contain relatively few of the immune cells (also known as killer T cells) needed to recognize and attack cancer.  Dr. Liau and Dr. Prins have spent years investigating whether a personalized vaccine could help overcome that barrier.  The vaccine, an autologous tumor lysate-pulsed dendritic cell vaccination (ATL-DC) known as DCVax-L, was developed to help overcome this challenge by teaching the body to recognize proteins found in a patient's tumor.  To create the vaccine, initially developed at UCLA, researchers collect tumor tissue removed during surgery and isolate immune cells called dendritic cells generated from the patient's own blood. These cells act as messengers for the immune system, helping it identify threats.  In the laboratory, the dendritic cells are exposed to proteins from the patient's tumor, essentially training them to recognize and attack the cancer. When the cells are injected back into the patient, they help activate an immune response directed against the tumor.  Unlike traditional vaccines, which are typically given to prevent disease, this therapeutic vaccine is designed to help the immune system fight an existing cancer.  The approach is especially promising because each vaccine is tailored to the individual patient's tumor.  “This is a personalized vaccine that we developed and have spearheaded all the way from the initial preclinical studies to the original first-in-human clinical trial, to newer work testing novel formulations of the vaccine combined with adjuvants and immune checkpoint blockade,” said Dr. Prins.  For Newirth, the experimental treatment offered a possibility that conventional therapies alone could not guarantee.  While undergoing treatment, Newirth continued studying for the bar exam and ultimately passed. He credits the innovative research from Dr. Liau and her team for saving his life.  And he is not alone.  So far, approximately two dozen patients who received the vaccine through clinical trials have become long-term survivors. Their experiences are particularly meaningful for a disease where survival beyond five years remains uncommon.  However, the vaccine does not benefit everyone, and researchers are still working to understand why some patients respond more favorably than others.  “There is a significant subgroup of patients who have lived more than five years,” Dr. Liau says. “But the challenge is trying to determine which patients it may work for and for which patients it doesn’t. Each new discovery gets us closer to improving survival and quality of life for patients facing this devastating disease.”  Building on the promise of cancer vaccines The encouraging responses seen in some patients have helped shape the next phase of Dr. Liau's research.  Rather than relying on the vaccine alone, her team is now investigating whether combining it with other immunotherapies could produce stronger and more lasting responses.  One approach involves pairing the vaccine with immune checkpoint inhibitors, a class of drugs that helps immune cells overcome signals that prevent them from attacking cancer.  Although checkpoint inhibitors have transformed treatment for several cancers, they have shown limited success against glioblastoma when used alone. One reason may be that brain tumors often lack sufficient numbers of cancer-fighting T cells for these drugs to activate.  The vaccine could help address that problem by first teaching the immune system to recognize the tumor and drawing cancer-fighting T cells into it. Checkpoint inhibitors could then enhance the function of those T cells within the tumor and help them remain active.  Dr. Liau’s team is also investigating which treatments work best together, and the order in which they should be given. Researchers hope that understanding how to sequence these treatments could make them more effective against tumors that have historically resisted immunotherapy.  “Because of the heterogeneity of glioblastoma, I don’t think there is going to be one drug or one treatment that is going to be effective for all patients. The future of glioblastoma treatments is going to be these combination approaches,” said Dr. Liau.  Scientists are also exploring other types of cancer vaccines, including vaccines designed to target specific genetic mutations found in brain tumors.  Some newer vaccines are designed to target molecular features shared by patients with the same type of cancer. This approach could help researchers develop treatments for specific groups of patients without needing to identify unique targets from each person's tumor.  Building on this research, UCLA neurosurgeon Anthony Wang, MD, director of the Pediatric Brain Tumor Program at UCLA Health, is leading a clinical trial testing a new vaccine for a rare and aggressive type of brain cancer called H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma, which primarily affects adolescents and young adults. The vaccine targets abnormal proteins produced by changes in how tumor cells process genetic information, with the goal of helping the immune system recognize and attack the cancer.  Developed in collaboration with Dr. Liau and Dr. Prins, the vaccine uses patients' own dendritic cells to activate an immune response against these tumor-specific targets. The first-in-human trial is designed to evaluate the vaccine's safety and explore whether it can generate a lasting immune response against the cancer.  More time, more possibilities For Dr. Liau, the long-term survivors who have emerged from these clinical trials offer an important reason to keep pushing forward. Each patient provides valuable insight into how the immune system responds to brain cancer and how future treatments might be improved.  Her goal is to build on those discoveries so that more patients can benefit from treatments that once seemed out of reach.  For Newirth, the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial changed the course of his life. Fourteen years after being told he had little time left, he has built a life and career that once seemed impossible.  “The hope is that stories like Newirth's will one day become less of an exception and more of a reality for patients facing brain cancer,” said Dr. Liau. In 1875, an estimated 12.5 trillion Rocky Mountain locusts descended on America, covering 198,000 square miles, an area larger than California.

Nebraska ordered citizens aged 16 to 60 to kill locusts or pay a fine. Missouri offered $1 per bushel. One scientist even published a recipe for frying them in butter.

Yet by 1902, the last known living specimens had been collected. The species was extinct.

text:
November 2018. Before dawn, strangers lined up in the dark outside a tiny California donut shop.

They bought every crumb early so the 62 year old owner could lock up and hold his sick wife's hand.

His name was John Chhan.

In 1979, John and his wife Stella came to America as refugees with nothing. For 28 years, they worked side by side at Donut City in Seal Beach, waking in the dark and staying until the trays emptied each afternoon.

They never spent a day apart.

Then Stella suffered a sudden brain aneurysm. Overnight, she was in a rehab clinic relearning how to speak and eat, while John stood behind the counter completely alone.

Every unsold donut meant one less hour he could sit beside Stella's bed.

Heartbroken regulars offered to start an online charity fund so he could close the shop.

John refused.

"I have enough," he told them. Having worked for every dollar of his life, he didn't want handouts. He only wanted time.

So the town of Seal Beach made a quiet pact.

Each morning in the dark, sleepy neighbors wrapped down the block. People on diets bought two dozen. Commuters carried out white boxes three at a time.

Nobody called it charity. They just smiled, paid cash, and wiped every metal rack bare hours ahead of schedule.

Morning after morning, an entire town ate donuts at sunrise so a husband could take off his apron and spend all day holding his bride's hand.

Charity gives a man money, but dignity buys out his shop at dawn so he can go love his wife.

News
$MBRX  
Preclinical data indicate that Annamycin sensitizes pancreatic cancer to immune checkpoint inhibitors, opening a new avenue for combination therapies with immunotherapies.
Price at time of publication: $8.70
Suppression of CD8+ T cells reduces survival in mice treated with Annamycin, suggesting that the immune system is a functional contributor to Annamycin’s anti-tumor activity, rather than a mere bystander.

Annamycin demonstrates significantly higher drug exposure in pancreatic tissue compared to Doxorubicin—a finding that may explain why topoisomerase II, a validated target in pancreatic cancer, has historically proven difficult to target effectively in this context.

HOUSTON, November 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc. (NASDAQ: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) announced today new preclinical data showing that its lead drug candidate, Annamycin (naxtarubicin), when combined with a PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor, significantly extends survival in pancreatic cancer models—outperforming either agent used alone. These findings will be presented orally today by Dr. Waldemar Priebe of The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center at the 6th Annual Marie Curie Cancer Research and Care Symposium, hosted by Moffitt Cancer Center. The symposium is taking place in Tampa, Florida, from November 8 to 11, 2026.

The presentation, titled “Targeting Pancreatic Cancer with Annamycin: Converting ‘Cold’ Tumors into ‘Hot’ Tumors,” is scheduled for 2:45 PM ET on November 10, during the symposium’s session on Gastrointestinal and Genitourinary Malignancies. In a syngeneic, immunocompetent KPC mouse model of advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the combination of liposomal annamycin (L-ANN) and PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade significantly extended survival compared to treatment with either agent alone. This finding has been replicated in a second, independent experiment. Pancreatic cancer is among the tumor types that respond most poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors, such as pembrolizumab and nivolumab—a limitation largely attributed to an immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironment characterized by a scarcity of infiltrating T cells. The company believes these data support the evaluation of annamycin in combination with approved PD-1 inhibitors for the treatment of pancreatic cancer, as well as other cancers where an immunologically "cold" microenvironment restricts the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors.

These combination study results build upon a series of findings from Dr. Priebe’s laboratory. Topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) is upregulated in pancreatic cancer, with higher expression levels correlating with shorter overall survival and increased rates of metastasis; however, approved topoisomerase II-targeting agents, such as doxorubicin, have not demonstrated clinical efficacy in this disease. Pharmacokinetic studies indicate that, at equivalent doses, annamycin achieves significantly higher and more sustained exposure within pancreatic tissue compared to doxorubicin, offering a potential explanation for this discrepancy. In treated tumors, high concentrations of annamycin were observed, accompanied by evidence of DNA damage consistent with topoisomerase II inhibition, as well as a marked increase in the infiltration of CD8+ cytotoxic T cells and CD4+ helper T cells. Depleting CD8+ T cells in treated animals reduced survival, suggesting that these cells are not merely bystanders but, rather, functional contributors to the anti-tumor activity of annamycin. These data expand upon research findings presented at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Annual Meeting in April 2026, as well as at the AACR Pancreatic Cancer Conference in September of the same year. Previous studies had already demonstrated the activity of annamycin in human orthotopic and syngeneic pancreatic cancer models—including models with liver metastases—and, for the first time, revealed the contribution of CD8+ T cells to its anti-tumor effects.

"In April of this year, we demonstrated in animal models that annamycin can reach pancreatic tumors and induce tumor shrinkage. In September, we further showed that the immune system plays a critical role in this process. Together, these data form a complete body of evidence: when annamycin is combined with an immune checkpoint inhibitor, the survival of the animals is significantly longer than when either agent is used alone," said Walter Klemp, Chairman, President, and CEO of Moleculin. "This combination strategy presents an exciting opportunity to apply immuno-oncology approaches to pancreatic cancer. Furthermore, it offers an additional advantage: unlike doxorubicin, annamycin has been shown—in both preclinical and clinical studies—to be free of cardiotoxicity. While our primary focus remains the MIRACLE trial in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and the data readout expected in the first quarter of 2027, these findings continue to broaden the strategic value of annamycin, extending its potential utility well beyond AML."

text:
TWO PRESIDENTS, TWO VERY DIFFERENT MOMENTS WITH AMERICAN WAR HEROES 🇺🇦🇺🇸🇫🇷

When Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met Melvin Hurwitz, an American World War II veteran, the elderly soldier reached for his hand and attempted to kiss it. Zelenskyy gently pulled his hand away, lowered himself to the veteran’s level and embraced him instead.

What followed was a deeply moving exchange.

Veteran: “You’re the savior of the people!”

Zelenskyy: “No, no, no. You saved Europe.”

Veteran: “You bring tears to my eyes. You are my hero.”

Zelenskyy: “No, no, you are our hero.”

Veteran: “I pray for you.”

The encounter offers a contrast with controversies surrounding Donald Trump’s remarks and treatment of American military service members.

During a 2018 visit to France marking the centenary of the end of World War I, Trump cancelled a planned visit to the Aisne-Marne American Cemetery, where 2,289 American military personnel are buried. According to accounts published by The Atlantic, Trump privately questioned why he should visit a cemetery filled with “losers” and referred to fallen Marines at Belleau Wood as “suckers.” Trump has denied making those remarks.

The soldiers who died at Belleau Wood were fighting Germany in World War I, not the Nazi regime of World War II.

In 2024, Trump also attracted criticism for comparing the Presidential Medal of Freedom with the Medal of Honor. He called the civilian decoration “much better” while noting that Medal of Honor recipients are often severely wounded or awarded the distinction posthumously.

In 2025, Trump was criticised for playing golf in Florida rather than attending a dignified transfer ceremony for four fallen American service members, although presidential attendance at such ceremonies is not mandatory.

Zelenskyy’s exchange with Hurwitz was a simple moment of mutual respect between two men from different generations, both shaped by wars in Europe.

Neither wanted to be called a hero. Each insisted that the other deserved the honour.

text:
Braden Atkinson leads all of college football in passing yards, and coming out of high school he was ranked the 151st quarterback in his class.

This morning he signed a deal to stay at Oregon State through 2027, and Pete Thamel at ESPN had it first.

He is from Rolesville, North Carolina.

At Rolesville High School he threw for 3,701 yards and 46 touchdowns as a junior. As a senior he threw for 3,925 yards and 53 touchdowns with three interceptions the whole year.

More than 9,400 yards and 121 touchdowns before he ever left home.

The recruiting services made him the 151st quarterback in the country and the 67th player in his own state.

His offers were Elon, Wofford, Boston College, Miami of Ohio and Mercer.

He took Mercer, which is in Macon, Georgia and plays in the FCS.

He got there as a backup. Two games into his true freshman year they gave him the job.

He threw for 3,596 yards and 34 touchdowns. He went over 300 yards eight times in eleven games. Against VMI he put up 533 and five touchdowns in a 62-0 win, and that is still the Mercer record.

Mercer won the Southern Conference.

Then they gave him the Jerry Rice Award, which goes to the best freshman in FCS football at any position.

On January 11 he signed with Oregon State.

Oregon State had just gone 2-10. When the Pac-12 came apart they were one of two schools nobody took. They had hired JaMarcus Shephard, who had never been a head coach anywhere.

And they already had a quarterback. Maalik Murphy had started at Texas and at Duke.

Atkinson beat him out in August, and when Shephard has been pressed on how a kid out of the FCS took that job off a quarterback with two Power Four schools on his record, the answer has not gotten any longer than this.

"Braden just rose to the top."

376 yards at Houston, ranked 23rd in the country. 399 against Texas Tech, ranked 13th. Those were the first two games he ever played at this level and Oregon State lost both of them.

Then 333 and five touchdowns. 301. 427. 409 and five more. 347.

Through seven games he had 2,604 yards, which is 372 a game.

He is at 3,169 now, with 25 touchdowns and three interceptions, and nobody in America has thrown for more.

Oregon State is 5-4.

On Saturday his throwing hand came down on a helmet in the third quarter against Texas State. He did not come back, and the Beavers lost 42-21. Shephard said Monday he is hopeful for Boise State.

James Crepea at OregonLive reported late last month that Oregon State was working to keep him. Atkinson sent the question to his agent, and said he was "extremely proud of" Jesse Legree, the freshman who leads the country in receiving and had already signed to come back. He is a sophomore and he has an agent.

This morning the quarterback signed too.

The 151st quarterback in his high school class is the best one in America this season, and he is staying at the school nobody wanted either.

text:
Joel Osteen's megachurch reported $600,000 stolen from its safe. Seven years later a plumber took off a toilet in the church bathroom and the envelopes started falling out of the wall.

Lakewood Church in Houston is one of the biggest churches in America. More than 40,000 people come every week to hear Osteen preach.

In March 2014, sometime between Sunday afternoon and Monday morning, someone opened the church safe. Inside were the weekend donations: $200,000 in cash and $400,000 in checks. Gone.

The church said the money was fully insured. Crime Stoppers offered a $25,000 reward. Nobody was ever charged.

Seven years passed.

In 2021 a plumber named Justin was called in to fix a loose toilet. He took the toilet off the wall and pulled out the insulation behind it.

About 500 envelopes fell out. Cash and checks.

He handed it all to the maintenance supervisor. Then he called a Houston radio show and told the story live on air.

The church said only that "an undisclosed amount of cash and checks" had been found, and called the police.

Justin said nobody from the church ever thanked him. In the end Crime Stoppers paid him a $20,000 reward.

In the video below the radio host and the plumber explain what was hiding behind that toilet.

The safe was emptied. The money was insured. And for seven years it was sitting in the bathroom wall. Who do you think put it there?

text:
After a full day of learning, meaningful conversations, and a little Houston hospitality, we wrapped up yesterday evening with some wonderful fellowship!

We brought together partners, friends, and colleagues from across the higher education and community engagement community at The Original Ninfa’s on Navigation. So many institutions, perspectives, and experiences around the table. A great reminder that some of the best ideas and collaborations start with simply making time to connect.

Always grateful for the friendships, partnerships, and conversations that make these gatherings special. Wonderful spending time with so many familiar faces and new friends across our community!

Earlier in the evening, we also had the chance to explore the incredible immersive experiences, artwork and surreal installations at Meow Wolf Houston. What a fun way to experience a little more of what Houston has to offer! @VisitHouston

And before the evening festivities, there was plenty of learning to kick things off at #CUMU2026: Anchored in Purpose.

A few highlights from yesterday’s sessions:

- Christine Lemesianou and Bryan Murdock @montclairstateu shared lessons from the Paterson One Square Mile initiative, connecting institutional purpose, resources, shared metrics, and evidence to demonstrate community impact. 

- The housing and homelessness plenary, moderated by Kris Larson @downtownhouston with Neal Rackleff @HousAllianceHTX and Kelly Young @HomelessHOU, explored affordability, supportive housing, and the coordinated systems needed to address homelessness. 

- Nyeema Watson, Daniel Tome, and Nathaniel Wright @rutgers_camden shared how their Urban Innovation Fund invests in community-identified priorities. 

- Cecelia Borgman, Ruthie Yow, and Cody Cocchi @georgiatech explored how experiential learning connects student development, workforce readiness, and community partner capacity. 

- Kayla Sims @DePaulSteans shared how students can translate civic experiences into capabilities they can share with employers.

And there were some fantastic poster presentations and conversations happening throughout the day, too!

What connects all these conversations is the opportunity for universities to move beyond good intentions and build the relationships, resources, evidence, and partnerships that create lasting impact in the communities they call home.

Grateful to everyone who joined us last night and to all the presenters, colleagues, and community partners who shared their work throughout the day.
